# Phase F4b: the plain-TypeScript surfaces - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The two TypeScript surfaces that are not React stop naming a cart or a console. One grouped `Host<G>` in core
replaces the three slices F4a introduced (`ConstructCaps`, `RenderHost`, `SongImportHost`), and a hook types itself by the
groups it uses; a new `ui` package holds the menu model and the menu-contribution types, and each cart and device
contributes its own rows, builders, tracker entries and services through a `retroplug.ui` manifest member; the cart CLI
tools and the six cart example sessions move into their packages behind a `CliTool` contract and a `retroplug.cli`
generated table, with the host modules a package may import listed in `host-modules.json` and checked by rule 3; and the
proof lands with them: rule 9 and the literal scanner over `cli/` (rule 9 with per-root semantics), a bundle check that
keeps `@retroplug/ui` out of the six non-UI bundles and every package's CLI module out of the UI bundle, and a `ui/`
ratchet naming the five view files F4c moves. **F4b changes no behaviour and re-records nothing:** strict parity, the kit
and render baselines, `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the protocol digests, the
`[packages]` golden, `edio-golden.json`, both device images, the box's, and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes hold unmodified;
every menu row id, label, stored value and staged MIDI is pinned by a matrix recorded from the design commit's own code;
and the one user-visible edge is the CLI command index's order (E1). Task 7 is the acceptance run.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md), whose section 11 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 6 lands, sections 1 to 10 corrected in place to what the prototype found. Task 1
lands `core/ts/host.ts` and `core/ts/capability.ts`, the three host builders over `src/hostGroups.ts`, the three slices
deleted and every hook retyped. Task 2 lands `packages/ui` with the menu model moved into it, the contribution types, the
`retroplug.ui` member and `ui/generated/menus.ts`, the role-row renderer, the SameBoy, Mesen and LSDj-sync rows, and the
recorded menu matrix. Task 3 lands the four carts' `TrackerUi` entries with their callbacks and specs, the `.rit` code in
tracker, and `@retroplug/core/path`. Task 4 lands the N8 and Launchpad `ts/ui/` modules, the Link Group builder, the
`Embed.shortLabel` title read, the services that replace the three watchers, the `ui/` ratchet and the device-pack scan's
`ui`/`cli` rule. Task 5 lands `CliTool` and `retroplug.cli`, the cart tools, `@retroplug/dsp/wav`, the examples with
`retroplug.examples`, the four SDK additions, `host-modules.json` with rule 3's surface rule and the two generated
`tsconfig` path files, and the CMake target that builds the examples. Task 6 lands rule 9 over `cli/`, the scanner's
second root, the bundle check, the root `typecheck` script and the docs pass, and folds the design's "As built". Task 7 is
the acceptance run.

**Tech stack:** no native build change and no dependency change beyond workspace links: TypeScript (the workspace
packages under `packages/`, the shell in `packages/retroplug/src`, `ui/`, `cli/`, `test/` and `test-native/`), the F1
package generator (`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`) and the boundary check
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs`) with the pinned `typescript-5` it loads, esbuild through
`tools/build-session.js`, `tools/build-ui.js` and `tools/build-device-pack.mjs`, the pnpm workspace's own runners, and
CMake only where an example session's target and the generator's byproducts need it (`cmake/packages.cmake`,
`packages/native/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake`).

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md) and
[package-split.md](package-split.md) (F4b is the plain-TypeScript half of its fourth phase; F4c is React in packages).
The mechanism it builds on is F1's ([modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md) section 4's
`definePackage` and generated registries, spec/06's "Adding a package"), the contract it replaces is F4a's
([modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f4a-design.md): the three host slices, the tracker hooks, rule 9
and the literal scanner), and [modular-graph-phase-f4a-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-f4a-plan.md) is a plan executed the
way this one is. The user's decisions are the `## F4` section of `.superpowers/f-split/decisions.md`, from "F4b cut" on.

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (`8a74339b9`).** The design was written before the
prototype; this plan follows what was built, and Task 6 lands the design with section 11's record and sections 1 to 10
corrected in place. In short (a bullet quotes the record where it uses quotation marks):

- **`png` joins the song import hook**, so it takes `Host<"files" | "png" | "systems">`: `lsdjSongImport` folds the
  role's overrides through `applyOverridesToRom` to build the ROM a `.lsdprj`'s kits are deduped against, and a font
  override decodes a PNG there. The design's body check missed it; the stage 1 report is the record.
- **`createUiHost(stores, peers)`, not `(stores, views)`**: `liveSongs.beginImport` is `useSongImport`'s picker,
  which is App's React state and not a store, so the peers are `{ views, beginImport }` (`begin` became a
  `useCallback`, so the host really is built once). **`devices.rpc` is a plain function resolving `makeCall()` on
  first use** in both hosts, because `makeCall` throws with no native channel and a getter could be forced by a
  spread. **`ProcessHost.args()` is the tool's own vector** (what `run(host, args)` was given, the name excluded).
  **`controller.set` throws on an unknown target** rather than laundering it into the live settings.
  **`SystemInfo.roles` is `readonly`**, which is what the shell's view can satisfy.
- **Core holds a narrow structural `ControllerSettings`** (`target: string` and a `ControllerAppField` union),
  because `target` is the launchpad package's enum and core cannot import launchpad; the shell keeps its enum-typed
  one, and the union is held equal to `ui`'s `ConfigRow` by a two-way assignability case in
  `ui/ts/test/rows.test.ts` (core cannot import `ui` either).
- **The capability types are their own module**, `@retroplug/core/capability` (`CapabilityOp`, `CapabilityArgs`,
  `CapabilityResults`, `CapabilityProgress`), which `src/capability.ts` re-exports and rule 9's list names.
- **`batteryListing` came forward into Task 1**, with its recorded oracle, so `ui/` never imported `cli/` and
  `n8-load`'s `--show-song` reached its first recorded test: each tracker integration carries `batteryListing`,
  `src/batteryListing.ts` composes the header, the trial order and the refusal line, and the three strings were
  recorded by running the design commit's `decodeAndPrint` before anything moved.
- **`TrackerUi.asset` is optional** (a battery-only cart simply has none); **`MenuBuildContext` gained
  `romPatterns`** and the per-path `assetRom` cache; **`AssetMenuSpec.selectedSlot` and `selectSlot` take the build
  context**, so a selectable-slot read hits the cache instead of the disk per row; **`MenuContext.host` is
  optional**, with `hostOf(ctx)` building the same host from the context's own peers for the menu tests;
  **`PLACEMENTS` is data** (`@retroplug/ui/contribution` exports it, and the generated module imports it, so a
  placement cannot be added to the type without the load-time check seeing it); the generated module's refusals are
  broader than the design's list (an unread `key` or `when.key`, an unknown or duplicate tracker id, a
  `UiService.id` declared twice); and **`UiHost` is declared in the package**, because a package may not import the
  shell.
- **The controller-app rows keep their old display** (`legacyConfigIndex`): the typed reading would have changed a
  hand-edited `appConfig`'s `quantise: 3` from "Immediately" to "Next bar", so the old reading is reproduced byte
  for byte and the latent display bug is owed (Task 6's list, and the design's section 10). A controller decision.
- **Services**: `start` runs once per MOUNT and each `start` resets its latches, which is what the refs and effect
  it replaced did; the frame counting is `ui/app/serviceTicker.ts`'s `tickServices`; the tests are
  `test/services.test.ts` (mock tier, fake services) and `test-ui/ui-services.test.ts` through frames; and the packs
  read test-injected globals (`__rp_launchpadClient`, `__rp_launchpadClock`, `__rp_n8LinkClient`) before their
  module state, because the prebuilt UI bundle holds its own module copies. **`createSubscribable` moved to
  `@retroplug/ui/menu` in Task 4**, not to F4c's kit, so a device pack can push a native change without importing
  the shell.
- **A device pack publishes one `./ui` export** (n8 dropped the two subpath exports it first had): a pack's UI
  contract is one module, the contribution plus the seam a test or another surface reaches it by.
  **`launchpadDevices.ts`'s global RPC fallback was deleted** (`resolveClient` takes the caller's channel), and the
  one host-less caller passes `makeCall()` once. **The shell's `SystemView` gained `embeddedRom`** so the instance
  title reads the embed's declaration without the shell holding a cart's name.
- **The device-pack scan skips the modules a manifest names as `app`, `ui` and `cli`** (and the directory of one
  that is its directory's index), and refuses a core module that imports one: the design did not foresee the
  Launchpad scenario reaching the host through its menu half.
- **The Link Group builder reads a number or Off by `typeof`** (the old `sameboyConfig` rule, not `Number(...)`, so
  a hand-edited string group stays Off), and **BlipToaster pins its settings at its OWN system's cart only** (the
  old `cartFor` rule; `drivenCart()` alone would have staged SysEx at another NES's console in a two-NES project).
  Both are pinned by recorded cases.
- **`src/pathUtil.ts` and `src/savPaths.ts` stay as re-export shims** over `@retroplug/core/path` (so git sees
  `pathUtil.ts` modified and `core/ts/path.ts` added, not a rename), and tracker keeps its own three-line `pick()`
  over `host.dialogs.browse`, because `ui` depends on `tracker`.
- **Tools are `ts/cli/` modules behind a `ts/cli/index.ts`** that default-exports `defineCliTools([...])`; `n8`
  publishes `./cli`, `./bridge` and `./ui`; there is ONE CLI host name (`CliHost`, no `CliToolHost` alias);
  `composeTools(shell, contributed)` is exported so the name-clash refusal has a test; and the shell's three example
  names are known to CMake, which refuses a package that reuses one.
- **The SDK drift check was extended** to the four additions' shapes, and its first run found real drift in
  `sdk-types.d.ts`'s `ConstructSpec` (`romBytes?`, `sramBytes?`, `stateBytes?`, `coreConfig?` with their real
  optional types); **`sdkSurfaceCheck.ts` reads the console a REAL cart drives**, not `CONSOLES[0]` (which is
  sameboy's and put a Mesen knob on the Game Boy).
- **Help and summaries are recorded from the OLD binary** before any tool moved (13 tools,
  `test/cli/recorded-help.json`), and `recorded-index.json` is the old index verbatim whose rows the test rebuilds
  in the registry's order, so the record stays a recording and E1's order is derived rather than hand-written.
- **The typecheck `paths` are two generated files**, `tsconfig.host-modules.json` (what a package with `examples/`
  extends) and `tsconfig.paths.json` (the same entries plus the shell-owned `tsconfig.aliases.json`'s `ui-harness`),
  because TypeScript REPLACES a child's `paths` with the extending config's rather than merging them; the generator
  checks an examples package's parsed `extends` and refuses an example outside `examples/` or a name two packages
  share; the root `typecheck` script runs the generator first, so a fresh checkout typechecks before any build (CI's
  order); `bundles.cmake` lists the new generated files; and `retroplug_examples()` skips an empty list.
- **Rule 3 enforces `surface`** (`surfaceOf` decides a file's surface from its own directory, and a module's
  `surface` is one name or a list) and walks `examples/` as well as `ts/`; the design left the field as
  documentation and this was a controller decision during the last pass.
- **Rule 9 has per-root semantics and one 29-entry list** (`src` reaches only `src`, `cli` reaches `cli/` or `src/`,
  `generated/` is unjudged, and a relative import out of either root is refused). **The scanner takes `--dirs
  src,cli` and `--carts`**; a bare cart id is a hit, an id inside a string with whitespace skips the
  extension-suffix rule, `generated/` and `cli/sdk-types.d.ts` are skipped, and the carts' ids are read from the
  generated module. **The ratchet** was written in Task 4, derives its package list from the manifests, and catches
  a relative reach. **The bundle check gained the script-node bundle**, `/packages/<name>/ts/ui/` on the non-UI side
  and `/packages/<name>/ts/cli/` on the UI side, and `tools/build-ui.js` exports `uiBuildOptions` and an in-memory
  `bundleInputs`.
- **New workspace dependencies, and the lockfile moved by them:** `ui` (new); `tracker` to `dsp` (types) and `n8`;
  `n8` to `tracker` and `ui`; `risa` to `n8` and `ui`; `bliptoaster` to `dsp` and `ui`; and `ui` into `launchpad`,
  `lsdj`, `mesen`, `sameboy`, `smsggdj` and the shell. No specifier or version changed, and the phase total is the
  55 lines each task's lockfile diff shows.
- **No C++ or CMake logic changed.** The C++ edits are three stale-path comments (`ControllerLink.hpp`,
  `N8Host.cpp`, `cli/main.cpp`); the CMake edits are the example-session target, `retroplug_examples()` and the
  generator's byproduct list.
- **The docs pass touched more than the design's list**: `spec/03`, `spec/04`, `spec/13`, `docs/launchpad-plan.md`
  and `docs/ui-shared-utils-audit.md` (the last two path-only) as well as `AGENTS.md`, `spec/00`, `02`, `06`, `07`,
  `09`, `docs/lsdj.md`, `docs/n8-usb-capabilities.md`, `docs/package-split.md` and `README.md`. **The design's own
  typo**: the tool's flag is `--show-song`, not `--ls`.

**The behaviour edges, which is the whole of what a user can see change.** Each is recorded in the design's section
6, and each is pinned by a test or a recorded table:

- **E1: the command index changes order.** Today `topLevelHelp` prints the shell's five first; after F4b it prints "
  "them, then the packages' in product order, so the single line reads `test run render analyze-capture grab-frame
  launchpad-probe lsdj-rom n8-load n8-bridge n8-play risa-rom n8-sync bliptoaster-rom`. `test/cli/cli.test.ts` pins the
  whole index, and `README.md`'s table follows it. `<cmd> --help` and every tool's output are unchanged.
- **E2: `n8-load`'s battery listing is unchanged**, byte for byte, through `host.songs.list` and the integrations'
  `batteryListing`, including the `not a risa or LSDj save` line by rank.
- **E3: the instance title reads the embed's short label** (`Embed.shortLabel`, `"mGB"`), the same output.
- **E4: the example sessions no longer bundle the control plane**, so `build/cli/*.js` differ in bytes and not in
  behaviour; each runs against the SDK of the binary that runs it. Checked before anything else in Task 5.
- **E5: `n8-load`'s output paths and two cart strings move with the tools** and keep their text.
- **E6: `validSplits` and `validAudioRoutings` are descriptor-driven**: equal for the five platforms.
- **E7: the watchers run as services at the same cadences** (6 and 3 frames), with the same latches, reset per mount.
- **E8: a hand-edited role config reads as before** (the three fallbacks, row by row).
- **E9: the menu's device entries sit by product order.**
- **E10: `UiHost`'s `kits` group does not exist**, so the UI cannot compile a kit.
- **E11: the controller-app rows keep their old display** for a hand-edited `appConfig` (a controller decision).
- **E12: the N8 Load ROM dialog offers the shell's `ROM_PATTERNS`**, through `MenuBuildContext.romPatterns`.

**The re-records: none, and the plan proves it.** F4b moves where TypeScript looks things up and who contributes a
row, never what it computes or shows. No `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
`RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`, `RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE` or
`RP_SKIP_BASELINE_UPDATE` is set anywhere in this plan. `packages/retroplug/scripts/skip-baseline.json` is untouched by
every commit (the moved `n8Play` test's cases skip nothing, so no slug moved). The only existing tests whose shape
changes are the ones the design's edges force, each quoted in its task as its diff with section 11's reason: the two
`ConfigRow` narrowing cases (`test/controller/registry.test.ts`), `test/render/ui-seam.test.ts` (`validSplits` drops the
unused `core` field), the four native tool tests (they pass `cliHost(session)`, no assertion changed),
`test-native/launchpad-devices.test.ts` (passes `makeCall()`), `test/cli/cli.test.ts` (the full index, plus the two
recorded cases), the menu tests' import paths, and the recorded matrix's own extension (recorded from the design commit's
code, never hand-written). Everything else passes unchanged, `test:ui` included.

**The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/f-split/decisions.md`, the F4 entries from "F4b cut" on; the design was approved
section by section):

- **The cut, and the contract.** F4 is two phases by mechanism (the user's choice B): F4b is the plain-TypeScript
  surfaces - one grouped `Host` in core, the menu contributions, the cart CLI tools as a generated table, rule 9 and
  the scanner over `cli/` - and F4c is React in packages. The host is `Host<G>` over named groups (the user's choice
  A), a hook types itself by the groups it uses, the shell builds one host per surface (the UI: no `process`; the
  CLI: no `dialogs`), and asking for an absent group is a type error; F4a's three slices are re-expressed as group
  selections and deleted.
- **The menu contributions are both forms (choice A)**, behind a `retroplug.ui` member imported only by `ui/`:
  declarative role rows (generalising the Launchpad controller-app field shape) and builder functions with a
  placement, plus the trackers' song and asset specs and the device services. A new `ui` package is their home
  (choice A): the menu model and the contribution types in F4b, the React kit in F4c; the Host stays in core.
- **The examples move into their packages (choice B)** and import the SDK by the bare `retroplug-cli` specifier,
  with the SDK gaining `runSession`, `DirectGraph`, `interleaveStereoStreams` and `deinterleaveStereo` (the
  controller's decision), and **the host modules are a `retroplug.host` member checked against one shell-owned
  list** (choice A) that also generates the typecheck paths.
- **`bliptoaster-rom` compiles by the string id `"risa"`** through `host.kits.compile`, with the shared NES DMC
  pieces and the two kit-spec types in `tracker` (the user's choice A), so BlipToaster stays risa-free; and
  **`n8-sync` moves to `risa`**, which depends on `n8`, while `n8` exports the shared bridge loop and stays free of
  every cart (choice A). The shared `.rit` code goes to `tracker`; `n8-load`'s listing stays byte-identical; the
  menu tests and the native tool tests stay in the shell and `n8Play`'s pure cases move; row equality is pinned by a
  table recorded from the old code; `Embed.shortLabel` is accepted; a service test comes first in its stage; new
  workspace dependencies are allowed with the lockfile change quoted.
- **The controller decisions taken during the prototype**, each in its stage's fix pass: the controller-app rows
  keep their old display byte for byte and the latent bug is owed; the N8 Load ROM dialog's patterns and the
  services' per-mount latches stay identical to the code they replaced; the host-module list's `surface` is enforced
  now; and the host-module surface and the menu matrix are pinned, not described. `host-modules.json`'s surface and
  the matrix are the two places where a later edit has to fail a test rather than drift.
- **The model routing, which this plan's execution follows:** the prototype's six stages were built by DeepSeek
  (Flash) and reviewed stage by stage (and, at the end, whole) by Opus; the design document was written by Sonnet,
  and its as-built section too, folded into Task 6's commit; this plan was generated by DeepSeek from the
  prototype's record, and the final review's requested legs are Task 7's. The user's routing for the phases sets the
  plan's implementers, the acceptance run and the follow-ups (the Windows agent's run among them, owed).
- **What only the record backs.** The design's section 11 is the description of what was built and of what no log
  records; the stage reports in `/tmp/f4bpro` are the working record (which run each figure is from, every review
  finding and its fix, the departures a fix pass forced), the reviews are each stage's verdict, `results.md` is the
  controller's log of them, and `s6f-report.md` is the last fix pass's. Where this plan quotes a figure, it quotes
  the report or log that states it; where nothing does, it says so and asks for the count.

**Hardware safety: this plan touches no hardware, ever.** The rig this plan was generated on has a real NES with an N8
flash cart, a Pico box, a probe, a Zoom L6 and MIDI interfaces attached, and this machine's ALSA sequencer lists them.
Nothing in this plan may list, open, write to, claim, flash or reconfigure any of it. The rules:

- **Never touch the NES, the N8, the Pico box, the probe or the Zoom L6.** No serial port is opened, no `n8-*` CLI
  command runs against a device, nothing is flashed to a Pico, and no `picotool`, `openocd`, `probe-rs` or `dfu-util`
  command is run. The moved N8 tools (`n8-load`, `n8-play`, `n8-bridge`, `n8-sync`) are exercised only by their
  existing fake-backed tests: `pnpm test:n8` over fake port factories, and the four native tool tests over scripted
  backends. Every device-related step in this plan happens on a **build**: `pnpm device:check` and `pnpm device:box`
  compile their images and run the check's plan in an arena, and both are built and never flashed.
- **Nothing that lists or opens a system MIDI port may run, with one exception.** `tools/run-sdl-controller.sh`
  (`pnpm sdl:controller`) is that exception: it sets `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` itself, from its two ALSA fakes' full port
  names, and **refuses** a caller who preset the variable; its listing pass runs before anything is claimed, and it
  fails the run when a listed port is not one of its fakes. Run it as `pnpm sdl:controller`, never a bare
  `retroplug-sdl`, and never with the variable preset.
- **`pnpm sdl:smoke` runs under a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` with `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`, a list that
  matches nothing** (an EMPTY list means every port, so the nothing-matching list has to name something). It sets it
  itself; do not remove it, and do not export a list of your own.
- **Never run `amidi`, `aconnect`, `aseqdump`, `aplaymidi`, `acpi_listen` or any other port tool against this machine's
  devices**, and never `git`-checkout or build with a saved enabled `controlSurface` in the real `~/.config/retroplug`:
  a saved, enabled pair is claimed at startup and its close bytes go out at quit, which is why the SDL tools take a
  scratch config dir. The Launchpad menu rows and the N8 card rows in the recorded matrix are read through fakes.
- **`retroplug-device-mode-test`, `test:plugin`, `test:native`, `pnpm test` and the CLI legs open no port**: their MIDI
  fakes are scripted openers in C++ and TypeScript. If a run of one of them seems to be waiting on MIDI, stop and
  report it rather than reaching for a queueing tool.
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (two tracked patches). That is expected; never stage, reset or
  stash it, and never touch any submodule (`deps/dpf.js` and everything under it included).

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 7 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own, named for what it fixes). A commit message is a subject line, a blank line, then the body, and the
  prototype's bodies are quoted whole: use `git commit -F -` as the blocks show. No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with"
  trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code, the specs, and a tool's own output
  a diff quotes): leave those be. The prototype's own passes removed every emdash from an added line.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself. Never bare `git stash`, never switch branches with uncommitted work in the tree, and never `rm -rf build` to
  fix CMake: investigate.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a
  `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not
  just something that applies. **Every `patch` block is a TEMPORARY mutation or revert**: apply it, watch the run fail
  or print what the step says, then reverse it with the range the next command gives, so the task's tree is what the
  commit expects.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,consoles,protocol,
  scriptNodes}.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/generated/menus.ts`, `packages/retroplug/cli/generated/tools.ts`,
  `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.host-modules.json` and `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.paths.json` are written by
  `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, gitignored (Task 2 and Task 5 add the four entries), and regenerated by
  the runners, `pnpm typecheck` and the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages` target. A worktree a prototype build ran in holds
  all of them, untracked and ignored (this one does): Task 1 Step 1 deletes them either way, and no `git status` list
  below shows them. If one ever does, the `.gitignore` entry is wrong: stop and report it.
- **NOTHING is re-recorded.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
  `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`, `RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE` or
  `RP_SKIP_BASELINE_UPDATE`, at any step. Strict parity (30 files, 250 cases), the kit and render baselines,
  `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the protocol digests, the `[packages]` golden,
  `edio-golden.json`, the device and box images and the pack's bytes are the phase's proof that nothing moved, and each
  task's suites step runs them. A change in any is a bug to find, not a re-record.
- **The lockfile moves in this phase, and only by workspace links.** Tasks 2, 3, 4 and 5 add `@retroplug/*` dependencies
  to package manifests, so each of them runs `pnpm install --offline` (the command the prototype used: **not**
  `--frozen-lockfile`, and never a bare re-resolve that prunes another platform's optional packages) and quotes that
  task's whole `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff, which is part of the task's changed-file diff block. Nothing in it may change a
  specifier or a version. Tasks 1 and 6 add no dependency, and their steps run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` and check the lockfile's blob.
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with three exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` reports a total that moves from run to run (its threaded cases assert in loops), and so
  do `retroplug-launchpad-test`'s and the ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must match and
  the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which the quotes
  below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s final line counts FILES; a case total is quoted from a report and is not the
  runner's own line, and the `jobs=N` a runner prints is the pool it was given (the kit's caps), not a figure to match.
- **A fresh checkout typechecks before it builds** (Task 6 changes the root script so the generator runs first). Until
  then, `pnpm typecheck` needs the generated modules, so each task's build step configures and builds first and only its
  per-task tree step runs the generator explicitly.
- **The Catch2 binaries and `retroplug-render-host-test` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the default build:**
  `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run
  (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first, and the render-host tool is built by name).
  **A new manifest member needs `cmake -S . -B build` first** (the generator target's inputs are the manifests, and the
  configure is what reads the product list and the example list), which is why each task that touches a manifest
  configures before it builds.
- **The scratch root, and one filesystem rule.** Every scratch path this plan writes is under `/tmp/f4b-accept` (the
  scripts, the logs, the base trees) or `/tmp/f4b-tree-<n>` / `/tmp/f4b-fresh` (the per-task and fresh-archive trees);
  none is inside the repository. One rule decides where a tree may go: the per-task and fresh-archive recipes run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` in the tree, and `build/` is SYMLINKED from this worktree, so those paths
  must be on a filesystem the worktree's symlink target is reachable from (they are, from `/tmp`, here). Do not
  `cp -al node_modules` into a scratch tree instead: a hardlink cannot cross a filesystem, and a plain symlink makes
  pnpm's per-package links resolve back into this worktree, which would make the tree's tests read THIS tree's sources.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build recompiles what changed and
  regenerates the generated modules; that is expected. Task 7 rebuilds all of it and hashes the images from the dirs it
  made.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose failing
  file, case or target is the one predicted but whose wording differs (the red steps say which are predicted); and a
  device script's trap-probe lines, whose object path and offsets are this devcontainer's and this binutils' (the device
  scripts judge a probe by its own object and the two symbol names, `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`, and that check
  is the pass criterion). Never edit code, a test or a golden to make a step pass. In Tasks 1 to 6 each task's tree must
  equal its prototype commit, so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a fix belongs to a commit of its own
  after the plan.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does not
  show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote: Task 7 states the owed items, and no step below builds on Windows. macOS
  and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either: `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and pushes to
  `main` only, so their first run is a dispatched run or a PR the user starts. **No step below needs a real device, and
  none may touch one.**

**Commit this plan before Task 1.** Before the commit, check where the tree is: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` must
print `feature/modularize`, `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` must print `8a74339b`, and `git status --short --untracked-files=all` must show
` m deps/sameboy` and nothing else (the generated modules are ignored, so they do not appear; Task 1 Step 1 deletes them
anyway). If the branch or the commit differs, stop: every step below assumes the design commit on a tree with nothing
else in it. (`git -C deps/sameboy status --short` shows the five files the two tracked SameBoy patches change:
`Core/apu.c`, `Core/apu.h`, `Core/camera.c`, `Core/random.c` and `Core/sgb.c`.) The run below copies the plan to its home
in the repository and commits it on its own, so every later task's `git status` and `git add` see a clean tree:

````bash
cp .superpowers/f4bplan/plan.md docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-plan.md
git add -- docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-plan.md
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
docs: the F4b implementation plan

The plan for Phase F4b, the plain-TypeScript surfaces, generated from the prototype's six commits on
proto/f4b-surfaces: one grouped Host contract in core with the three surfaces' builders; the ui package with the menu
model, the contribution types and the recorded menu matrix; the tracker entries in their carts; the device menus and

Every expected count is quoted from a stage report, a stage log, the design's record, the reviews or the user's
````

### Task 1: the host contract, and the three surfaces' hosts

Design sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 8's first stage. One grouped `Host<G>` replaces F4a's three slices, and every hook
that took a slice takes a group selection instead: the shell builds one host per surface, so a hook that asks for a group
its surface lacks fails `tsc`. The types the groups name that the shell owned move to core as types only, with the shell's
modules re-exporting them, so no caller changed for them; the three slices and `src/songImportHost.ts` are deleted.

Two departures from the design's snippet are this task's, both recorded in the header and in the stage reports:
`createUiHost` takes the two peers App owns the state for, and the UI host's `songs` group is composed in `src/` from the
tracker integrations' new `batteryListing` member, with the three strings recorded from the design commit's own
`decodeAndPrint` before anything moved. That last one came forward from Task 5 because the stage 1 review found the first
cut making `ui/` import `cli/` (and every cart behind it) and reaching `n8-load` with no recorded test.

**Files:**

- Create (10): `packages/core/ts/capability.ts`, `packages/core/ts/host.ts`, `packages/core/ts/test/host.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/cli/cliHost.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/batteryListing.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/hostGroups.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/render/renderHost.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/hosts/battery-listing.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/hosts/host-groups.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/host/uiHost.ts`
- Modify (41 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 7 under `packages/retroplug/src/`; 6 under `packages/lsdj/ts/`; 5 under `packages/tracker/ts/`; 4 under `packages/risa/ts/`; 2 under `packages/bliptoaster/ts/`; 2 under `packages/lsdj/ts/test/` and the rest)
- Delete (1): `packages/retroplug/src/songImportHost.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Delete the generated modules a prototype build may have left**

They are derived, gitignored and regenerated by the configure, so deleting them costs nothing; leaving them would let
a stale module from another tree shadow this one's until the next build.

Run: `rm -f packages/retroplug/src/generated/packages.ts packages/retroplug/src/generated/consoles.ts packages/retroplug/src/generated/protocol.ts packages/retroplug/src/generated/scriptNodes.ts packages/retroplug/ui/generated/menus.ts packages/retroplug/cli/generated/tools.ts packages/retroplug/tsconfig.host-modules.json packages/retroplug/tsconfig.paths.json`
Expected: nothing: the eight derived files are gone, and every later step's `git status` list is free of them (`git status --short --untracked-files=all | grep -c 'generated\|tsconfig\.\(host-modules\|paths\)'` prints `0` and exits 1).

- [ ] **Step 2: The contract in core**

`HostGroups` with its thirteen groups (`files png kits systems songs liveSongs emulator dialogs devices process views
controller config`), `Host<G>`, and the types the groups name that the shell owned: `SystemInfo` (the part of a system
a hook may read, `roles` readonly), `KitBank`, `PngImageData`, `FileBrowserOpts`, `Call`, `MidiClient`,
`ControllerSettings` (the narrow structural one, with `ControllerApp` and the `ControllerAppField` union) and
`ControlSurfaceSettings`. The capability table is its own module, because rule 9's list names it.

Create `packages/core/ts/host.ts`:

````ts
// The host contract (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3): one object of named groups, one per capability
// a surface has, which the shell builds once per surface - the UI, the CLI, the render worker - out of the stores,
// backend and driver it already has. A hook types itself by the GROUPS it uses (`Host<"files" | "png">`, say), so a
// hook given a surface that lacks one is a compile error rather than a member that is undefined when the hook runs, and
// the manifest of a surface's host is its group list (ui/host/uiHost.ts, cli/cliHost.ts, src/render/renderHost.ts).
//
// Every member exists because code outside the shell calls it today; the shell's own generic machinery keeps using its
// stores directly. A type a group names that the shell owns (a PNG image, a file dialog's options, a MIDI client, the
// capability jobs' operation table) lives here as a type only, with the shell's module re-exporting it, so a cart or a
// console's TS can name it without importing the shell.
import type { Core, Platform } from "./platform";
import type { RoleInstance } from "./systemRoles";
import type {
  CapabilityArgs,
  CapabilityOp,
  CapabilityProgress,
  CapabilityResults,
} from "./capability";

/** A raw RGBA8888 image: `rgba` is `width*height*4` bytes, row-major, top-to-bottom (the output of a PNG decode and
 *  the shape a font override maps to and from tiles). */
export interface PngImageData {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  rgba: Uint8Array;
}

/** Presentation for an OS file dialog: its title and the glob patterns to show. */
export interface FileBrowserOpts {
  title: string;
  patterns: string[];
  /** True for a SAVE dialog (a filename can be typed and an overwrite confirmed); absent/false opens for reading. */
  saving?: boolean;
  /** A suggested filename for a save dialog (e.g. `"project.rplg"`); ignored when opening. */
  defaultName?: string;
  /** Directory the dialog opens in; the host's own default (its working directory) when absent or empty. Used to
   *  reopen a dialog where the user last saved (the render output dir today). */
  startDir?: string;
  /** Pick a FOLDER instead of a file: `patterns`/`defaultName` are then ignored. Supported on Linux + macOS; on Windows
   *  the OS opens a file dialog instead, and the caller takes the dirname. */
  directory?: boolean;
}

/** A compiled kit bank: the bytes, and each spec sample's reason in spec order, null exactly when the bank holds that
 *  sample whole. The dsp package's own `KitCompileResult` is this shape member for member; core declares it because it
 *  cannot import dsp, and a test holds the two assignable both ways. */
export interface KitBank {
  bytes: Uint8Array;
  errors: (string | null)[];
}

/** The synchronous JSON-RPC caller every native client reaches the host through: the method name and its params, the
 *  reply's result, a throw when the reply is an error. */
export type Call = (method: string, ...params: unknown[]) => unknown;

/** A live-MIDI client (mounted CLI-only today), for the TS N8 bridges and the Launchpad probe. `poll()` drains the
 *  messages queued since the last call (each = raw bytes; MIDI carries no timing). Synchronous like every other facet.
 *  `listInputs` returns [] on a host that did not mount it. The output half exists because a control surface has to be
 *  LIT as well as read, and `send` takes any length - a bulk-LED sysex runs to hundreds of bytes. */
export interface MidiClient {
  listInputs(): string[];
  listOutputs(): string[];
  /** Open a virtual "<clientName> In/Out" + the selected hardware input ("" = all inputs). False if no MIDI system. */
  open(clientName: string, input: string): boolean;
  /** Mirror sends to this hardware output ("" = the virtual port only). Applied immediately. */
  selectOutput(output: string): void;
  poll(): Uint8Array[];
  send(bytes: Uint8Array | number[]): void;
  close(): void;
}

/** The part of a system a hook may read: the shell's system view less its live `focused`/`settings` fields, which a
 *  cart has no business reading, so the view satisfies it structurally. */
export interface SystemInfo {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly platform: Platform;
  readonly core: Core;
  readonly romPath: string;
  readonly savPath: string;
  readonly savSuffix: number;
  readonly embedded: boolean;
  readonly battery: boolean;
  readonly missing: boolean;
  readonly roles: readonly RoleInstance[];
}

/** A controller app as a project surface reads it: its id, its menu text, the rows that edit its config and the schema
 *  a saved config is parsed with. The launchpad package's own contribution type satisfies this as written; core keeps
 *  the narrow shape so the host can name the list without importing the package that registers it. */
export interface ControllerAppField {
  readonly key: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly choices?: readonly { readonly value: string | number; readonly label: string }[];
  readonly toggle?: boolean;
}
export interface ControllerApp {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly config: { parse(config: unknown): Record<string, unknown> };
  readonly menu?: readonly ControllerAppField[];
}

/** The control-surface session a project stores: which app runs, where its launches go and the app's own config. Only
 *  the user's CHOICES live here; the runtime's derived document is the graph's. */
export interface ControllerSettings {
  readonly enabled: boolean;
  readonly app: string;
  /** Where a launch goes: into the emulated cart's sync node, or out of the host to real hardware. The launchpad
   *  package's enum is the closed list; the host leaves it an open string, as it does the platform and core ids. */
  readonly target: string;
  /** 0 = the first system. */
  readonly systemId: number;
  readonly appConfig: Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** The control surface this machine uses (Settings > MIDI's scan and the instance menu's controller submenu). HOST
 *  state rather than project state, because port names belong to the machine: a project opened elsewhere would carry
 *  names that do not exist there, and one process holds one device for every project it has open.
 *
 *  The port names are opaque - often an interface's, not the device's, since a Launchpad also speaks TRS/DIN - and
 *  `device` is what a scan read off the hardware ("" = never scanned), shown and never interpreted. */
export interface ControlSurfaceSettings {
  input: string; // "" = none chosen
  output: string;
  enabled: boolean; // the user's Connect: claim the pair now, and again at the next launch
  device: string;
}

/** The file I/O every surface has, and the backend's own methods one for one. */
export interface FilesHost {
  readFile(path: string): Uint8Array | null;
  writeFile(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  writeFileAtomic(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  fileExists(path: string): boolean;
}

/** The PNG codec: a font override decodes a linked image, a font export encodes one. */
export interface PngHost {
  encode(width: number, height: number, rgba: Uint8Array): Uint8Array | null;
  decode(bytes: Uint8Array): PngImageData | null;
}

/** Compiling a kit bank, which only a CLI tool does today. */
export interface KitsHost {
  /** The bank format `id` names among the product's registered kit formats, the spec compiled by its compiler. A
   *  per-sample failure leaves that slot empty and comes back in `errors`; an unknown id rejects, naming it. */
  compile<S>(id: string, spec: S): Promise<KitBank>;
}

/** The live systems of a project: their view, their battery, their roles and the nodes the graph places them at. */
export interface SystemsHost {
  /** The live systems, in slot order. */
  view(): readonly SystemInfo[];
  setRoleConfig(id: number, kind: string, config: Record<string, unknown>): boolean;
  /** Reboot a system in place from what it holds (the one rebuild a keep-open row ends in). */
  reload(id: number): unknown;
  /** The system's live battery, or null when its core has none to read. */
  readSram(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** Reboot a system from the `.sav` at `path`: the one rebuild an import ends in. */
  loadSram(id: number, path: string): unknown;
  /** The `.sav` a save of system `id` writes: its paired-save override when it has one, else the file beside its ROM.
   *  Null when the system is gone, so a caller writes nothing rather than an empty path. */
  savPathOf(id: number): string | null;
  /** The graph id of a system's own node (`sys-<id>`), which a node aimed message names. */
  nodeIdOf(id: number): string;
  /** The system the document places a real cart for, and that cart's node id, or null when no system drives one. The
   *  one rule the document and every caller read, so they cannot disagree about which system's cart it is. */
  drivenCart(): { id: number; nodeId: string } | null;
  /** Deliver MIDI bytes straight to the input of one node of the running graph, outside the project's musical
   *  routing. */
  stageNodeMidi(nodeId: string, bytes: number[]): boolean;
  /** Run capability job `op` on node `nodeId` and settle with its completion (a read at once, a write once the block
   *  after it published, a device's job on its own thread). Rejects with native's reason when it is refused. */
  capability<O extends CapabilityOp>(
    nodeId: string,
    op: O,
    args: CapabilityArgs,
    onProgress?: (p: CapabilityProgress) => void,
  ): Promise<CapabilityResults[O]>;
}

/** The saved songs of a battery image as LINES to print: a CLI host prints them as they are, so a tool's output stays
 *  the tool's own while what a cart's battery means stays the cart's. */
export interface SongsHost {
  /** The header and one row per song (or the "unrecognized battery image" line) for `bytes`. */
  list(bytes: Uint8Array): string[];
}

/** The UI's half of a cart's songs: the live battery, and the picker an import from a `.sav` opens. A CLI host cannot
 *  offer either (it has no running system and no overlay), which is why the listing and these are two groups. */
export interface LiveSongsHost {
  /** Apply a byte transform to a running system's battery and cold-boot it, all or nothing. False when the transform
   *  declined (`fn` returned null) or the write/boot did not take, so a caller that CHAINS edits can stop at the first
   *  one that did not land. */
  mutate(sys: SystemInfo, fn: (sav: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array | null): boolean;
  /** Open the Songs "import from a `.sav`" picker on `source`, validated against `sys`'s console. */
  beginImport(sys: SystemInfo, source: Uint8Array): void;
}

/** What a render hook drives of the booted system. The render's own output stream is NOT here: it is the request's, so
 *  it is passed to the one hook that captures into it and a hook that runs before it exists cannot call it. */
export interface EmulatorHost {
  /** The audio a hook discards while it works (a boot wait, a prep press): whole milliseconds, in the render's mix. */
  renderAudio(ms: number): void;
  /** A CPU register's value, or null when the core cannot be read. */
  readCpu(id: number, addr: number): number | null;
  /** The system's work RAM, or null when a snapshot is not available this block. */
  readRam(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** Write into the system's work RAM; false when the range is refused (a wrong layout, a full command ring). */
  writeRam(id: number, offset: number, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  pressButton(id: number, button: number, down: boolean): void;
}

/** The OS file dialog. */
export interface DialogsHost {
  browse(opts: FileBrowserOpts): Promise<string | null>;
}

/** The native facets a tool reaches directly rather than through a store: the RPC channel, and the live-MIDI client. */
export interface DevicesHost {
  /** The JSON-RPC caller: what a client of a native facet this host does not model is built over. */
  rpc: Call;
  /** A live-MIDI client. A FACTORY, because a tool opens as many as it needs (a bridge calls it twice per run). */
  midi(): MidiClient;
}

/** The process a tool runs in. */
export interface ProcessHost {
  /** The tool's own arguments, exactly the `args` its `run(host, args)` was given: the dispatcher strips the command
   *  name, so a flag a tool reads from `args` reads the same here. A session run by path (no dispatcher) has none. */
  args(): string[];
  /** Keep the launcher pumping after the tool returns: what a long-running tool (a live bridge) asks for. */
  keepAlive(): void;
  exit(code: number): void;
}

/** A full-window view the shell owns, by the id a cart names it with: the LSDj HD player today. */
export interface ViewsHost {
  open(id: string, systemId: number): void;
}

/** The project's control-surface session: what the Launchpad submenu reads and edits. */
export interface ControllerHost {
  settings(): ControllerSettings;
  /** Apply a patch to the project's controller. THROWS when `target` is not a launch target this host knows: the patch
   *  is written into the live settings, the published document and the next save unread, so a bad value would be a
   *  controller that launches nowhere - a package's bug, refused loudly rather than dropped. */
  set(patch: { enabled?: boolean; app?: string; appConfig?: Record<string, unknown>; target?: string }): void;
  /** The cart's own SYNC setting as last polled, or null when it cannot be read. */
  cartSync(): string | null;
  /** What an enabled controller does to the cart's sync mode in the published document, or null when it drives none. */
  syncOverride(): { driving: boolean } | null;
  /** Every controller app the product carries, in product order. */
  apps(): readonly ControllerApp[];
}

/** `config.json`'s control surface: the machine's port pair, which a scan fills and the user's choices edit. */
export interface ConfigHost {
  controlSurface(): ControlSurfaceSettings;
  setControlSurface(patch: Partial<ControlSurfaceSettings>): void;
}

/** Every group a host can offer. A surface's host names the subset it has, and what it cannot do it does not offer. */
export interface HostGroups {
  files: FilesHost;
  png: PngHost;
  kits: KitsHost;
  systems: SystemsHost;
  songs: SongsHost;
  liveSongs: LiveSongsHost;
  emulator: EmulatorHost;
  dialogs: DialogsHost;
  devices: DevicesHost;
  process: ProcessHost;
  views: ViewsHost;
  controller: ControllerHost;
  config: ConfigHost;
}

/** A surface's host, narrowed to the groups `G` names: `Host<"files" | "png">` is what a construct hook takes, and a
 *  host offering more satisfies it. */
export type Host<G extends keyof HostGroups = keyof HostGroups> = { readonly [K in G]: HostGroups[K] };
````

Create `packages/core/ts/capability.ts`:

````ts
// What a capability job asks and answers (docs/modular-graph-phase-c5-design.md section 6): a node of the running
// graph, asked to read, write or dump something of the system behind it, answers one of these operations. The shell's
// job pump (packages/retroplug/src/capability.ts) submits them and settles their promises, and re-exports these types;
// they live here because a host names them - `Host.systems.capability` - so a hook, a cart's menu or a console's TS can
// type a job without importing the shell.

/** The operations, as `<capability>.<op>`; each names its versioned native interface below. */
export type CapabilityOp =
  | "memory.regions"
  | "memory.read"
  | "memory.write"
  | "sram.dump"
  | "sram.restore"
  | "rom.header"
  | "rom.title"
  | "rom.upload";

/** The arguments an operation reads; the rest are ignored. memory: `region` by name, `offset`, and `length` for a read
 * (absent or 0: to the region's end) or `bytes` for a write; sram: `bytes` for a restore; rom: `length` for a header
 * (absent or 0: the whole image), and `bytes` and `name` (the file it is stored under) for an upload, which only a
 * device's node (rp.n8.nes) performs. On that node `name` also names the ROM whose battery file (EDN8/gamedata/<rom>/
 * bram.srm on its SD card) sram.dump and sram.restore reach, defaulting to the ROM this host last booted. */
export interface CapabilityArgs {
  region?: string;
  offset?: number;
  length?: number;
  bytes?: Uint8Array;
  name?: string;
}

/** What a cart's `sram.restore` wrote: the battery file, and whether the ROM's folder had to be made for it (a ROM that
 * never saved on the card, or a mistyped name). Only a device's node restores in place; an emulated system refuses. */
export interface SramRestore {
  path: string;
  created: boolean;
}

/** What a cart's `rom.upload` booted: where the image went, the mapper core the cart's menu chose, and that streaming
 * stopped (a running game has no menu, so the link is reconnected to the new ROM). */
export interface RomUpload {
  path: string;
  mapIndex: number;
  streaming: "stopped";
}

/** A region `memory.regions` lists: its name and its published size in bytes. */
export interface MemoryRegion {
  name: string;
  size: number;
}

/** What each operation's promise resolves with. */
export interface CapabilityResults {
  "memory.regions": MemoryRegion[];
  "memory.read": Uint8Array;
  "memory.write": void;
  "sram.dump": Uint8Array;
  "sram.restore": SramRestore | undefined;
  "rom.header": Uint8Array;
  "rom.title": string;
  "rom.upload": RomUpload;
}

/** A long job's progress: `progress` of `total` (units the job chooses: bytes for a transfer). */
export interface CapabilityProgress {
  progress: number;
  total: number;
}
````

`src/hostGroups.ts` is the one definition of "the backend as a host" (`filesHost`, `pngHost`, `filesPngHost`), used by

composes `n8-load`'s listing over the tracker integrations, naming no cart: the header (`<name> battery - <n>
<noun>(s):`), the rank order, and the refusal line with the names joined by `" or "` so it still reads `not a risa or

Create `packages/retroplug/src/hostGroups.ts`:

````ts
// The host groups a control-plane hook runs on (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3): the file I/O and the
// PNG codec, over the backend. A construct-time role hook and an asset bake are handed exactly this, and each surface's
// own host builds its `files` and `png` groups here, so "the backend as a host" has one definition.
import type { FilesHost, Host, PngHost } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import type { HostBackend } from "./backend";

/** The backend's file I/O as core's files group. The methods are wrapped rather than handed over, so what a hook
 *  receives is a table it cannot reach the rest of the backend through. */
export function filesHost(
  backend: Pick<HostBackend, "readFile" | "writeFile" | "writeFileAtomic" | "fileExists">,
): FilesHost {
  return {
    readFile: (path) => backend.readFile(path),
    writeFile: (path, bytes) => backend.writeFile(path, bytes),
    writeFileAtomic: (path, bytes) => backend.writeFileAtomic(path, bytes),
    fileExists: (path) => backend.fileExists(path),
  };
}

/** The backend's PNG codec as core's png group. */
export function pngHost(backend: Pick<HostBackend, "pngEncode" | "pngDecode">): PngHost {
  return {
    encode: (width, height, rgba) => backend.pngEncode(width, height, rgba),
    decode: (bytes) => backend.pngDecode(bytes),
  };
}

/** The two groups a construct-time hook or an asset bake is handed. */
export function filesPngHost(
  backend: Pick<HostBackend, "readFile" | "writeFile" | "writeFileAtomic" | "fileExists" | "pngEncode" | "pngDecode">,
): Host<"files" | "png"> {
  return { files: filesHost(backend), png: pngHost(backend) };
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/batteryListing.ts`:

````ts
// A battery image as the lines a listing prints (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 5.2): a header and one
// row per saved song, or the "unrecognized battery image" line. Each cart describes its own records through its tracker
// integration's `batteryListing`, so what a cart's battery means stays the cart's and no cart is named here: the shell
// composes them in rank order, which is the order the listing used to hard-code (risa before LSDj).
import type { BatteryListing } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerIntegration";
import { TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS } from "./trackerRegistry";

/** Every integration that lists a battery, in the order they are tried: a cart's rank first, and product order between
 *  equal ranks (a stable sort, so the list is deterministic). */
function listings(): BatteryListing[] {
  return TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS.map((integration) => integration.batteryListing)
    .filter((listing): listing is BatteryListing => listing !== undefined)
    .sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank);
}

/** The listing for `sram`: the first cart that reads it heads its own rows, and an image no cart reads gets the one
 *  refusal line naming them all. */
export function batteryListing(sram: Uint8Array): string[] {
  const carts = listings();
  for (const cart of carts) {
    const rows = cart.describe(sram);
    if (rows) return [`${cart.name} battery - ${rows.length} ${cart.noun}(s):`, ...rows];
  }
  const names = carts.map((cart) => cart.name).join(" or ");
  return [`unrecognized battery image (${sram.length} bytes) - not a ${names} save`];
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The three surfaces' builders**

`createUiHost(stores, peers)` returns the UI's ten groups and is built once in `App.tsx` behind a `useMemo`;
`importHost(backend, systems)` is the same host narrowed to what one menu call site needs. `cliHost(session, args)`
returns the CLI's six, with `process.args()` the tool's own vector. `renderHost(ctx)` returns the render's two and
replaces `render.ts`'s local table. `devices.rpc` is a plain function resolving `makeCall()` on first use in both
hosts, the UI host's `controller.set` checks `CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES` and throws on an unknown target, and

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/host/uiHost.ts`:

````ts
// The UI surface's host (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3.2): built once, in App.tsx, over the store
// graph, and the way a cart's or a console's UI code reaches the shell. It offers the ten groups a UI has - files, png,
// systems, songs, liveSongs, dialogs, devices, views, controller, config - and nothing a UI cannot do: no kits (the UI
// composes no audio driver) and no process (the UI does not own the process).
import type { AppStores } from "../../src/appStores";
import type { ControlPlaneBackend } from "../../src/backend";
import type { SystemsStore } from "../../src/systemsStore";
import type { Call, DevicesHost, Host, SystemInfo, SystemsHost, ViewsHost } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import { CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES, type ControllerTarget } from "@retroplug/launchpad/enums";
import { roleConfig } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { filesPngHost } from "../../src/hostGroups";
import { resolveSavPath } from "../../src/savPaths";
import { cartNodeId, drivenCartSystem, systemNodeId } from "../../src/graph/buildGraph";
import { controllerSyncOverride } from "../../src/graph/controller";
import { controllerApps } from "../../src/controller/registry";
import { mutateLiveSav } from "../../src/tracker/liveSav";
import { makeCall } from "../../src/rpcClient";
import { createMidiClient } from "../../src/realBackend";
import { batteryListing } from "../../src/batteryListing";

export type UiHost = Host<
  "files" | "png" | "systems" | "songs" | "liveSongs" | "dialogs" | "devices" | "views" | "controller" | "config"
>;

/** What the host needs that is not a store: the views the shell owns and the song-import picker, both of them App's
 *  React state (the picker is useSongImport's overlay). */
export interface UiHostPeers {
  readonly views: ViewsHost;
  readonly beginImport: (sys: SystemInfo, source: Uint8Array) => void;
}

/** The host groups an import uses - the file I/O, the PNG codec and the running systems - over a backend and a systems
 *  store. `createUiHost` spreads it into the UI host, and the host-groups test builds it on its own; a surface's whole
 *  host satisfies the import hook either way. */
export function importHost(
  backend: ControlPlaneBackend,
  systems: SystemsStore,
): Host<"files" | "png" | "systems"> {
  return { ...filesPngHost(backend), systems: systemsHost(backend, systems) };
}

export function createUiHost(stores: AppStores, peers: UiHostPeers): UiHost {
  const systems = stores.project.systems;
  // The RPC caller and a MIDI client are built on first use: a UI that never builds an N8 client (every mock-tier test,
  // a DAW host with no device) must not need the native RPC channel to exist to have a host at all. A function rather
  // than a getter, so copying the group (`{ ...host.devices }`) does not resolve it.
  let rpc: Call | undefined;
  const devices: DevicesHost = {
    rpc: (method, ...params) => (rpc ??= makeCall())(method, ...params),
    midi: () => createMidiClient(),
  };
  return {
    ...importHost(stores.backend, systems),
    songs: { list: (bytes) => batteryListing(bytes) },
    liveSongs: {
      mutate: (sys, fn) => mutateLiveSav(stores.backend, systems, sys, fn),
      beginImport: peers.beginImport,
    },
    dialogs: { browse: (opts) => stores.backend.openFileBrowser(opts) },
    devices,
    views: peers.views,
    controller: {
      settings: () => stores.project.settings().controller,
      // A package hands the target over as a plain string, and ProjectStore writes the patch into the live settings, the
      // published document and the next .rplg save unread, so an unknown value would be a controller that launches
      // nowhere. It is refused here, naming the value, rather than laundered into the closed type with a cast: a bad
      // target is a package's bug, not a user's input to drop quietly.
      set: (patch) => {
        const { target, ...rest } = patch;
        if (target === undefined) {
          stores.project.setController(rest);
          return;
        }
        if (!isControllerTarget(target))
          throw new Error(`controller target '${target}' is not one of ${CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES.join(", ")}`);
        stores.project.setController({ ...rest, target });
      },
      cartSync: () => stores.project.controllerCartSync(),
      // What the published document will have the cart's sync node run, computed by the SAME helper buildGraph uses, so
      // a row cannot describe something other than what is happening.
      syncOverride: () => {
        const settings = stores.project.settings().controller;
        return controllerSyncOverride(
          systems.view(),
          settings.enabled ? { ...settings, cartSync: stores.project.controllerCartSync() } : null,
        );
      },
      apps: () => controllerApps.list(),
    },
    config: {
      controlSurface: () => stores.userConfig.controlSurface(),
      setControlSurface: (patch) => void stores.userConfig.setControlSurface(patch),
    },
  };
}

/** The live systems of a project: the view, the battery, the role edits and the nodes the graph places them at. */
function systemsHost(backend: ControlPlaneBackend, systems: SystemsStore): SystemsHost {
  const view = () => systems.view();
  return {
    view,
    setRoleConfig: (id, kind, config) => systems.setRoleConfig(id, kind, config),
    reload: (id) => systems.reloadSystem(id),
    readSram: (id) => systems.readSram(id),
    loadSram: (id, path) => systems.loadSram(id, path),
    savPathOf: (id) => {
      const sys = view().find((s) => s.id === id);
      // A system that went away between the caller reading it and its write has no path, and quietly writing its
      // battery to "" would be a failure reported as a success.
      return sys ? resolveSavPath(sys.romPath, sys.savSuffix, sys.savPath) : null;
    },
    nodeIdOf: (id) => systemNodeId(id),
    drivenCart: () => {
      const cart = drivenCartSystem(
        view().map((system) => ({
          system,
          platform: system.platform,
          coreConfig: roleConfig(system.roles, system.core),
        })),
      );
      return cart ? { id: cart.system.id, nodeId: cartNodeId(cart.system.id) } : null;
    },
    stageNodeMidi: (nodeId, bytes) => backend.stageNodeMidi(nodeId, bytes),
    capability: (nodeId, op, args, onProgress) => backend.capability(nodeId, op, args, onProgress),
  };
}

/** Whether `value` is a launch target the shell knows: the controller-host contract carries it as an open string, and
 *  this is the one place it becomes the launchpad package's closed type. */
function isControllerTarget(value: string): value is ControllerTarget {
  return (CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES as readonly string[]).includes(value);
}
````

````ts
// The CLI surface's host (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3.2): built per tool run from the session,
// over the backend, the audio driver and the process the tool runs in. It offers the six groups a tool has - files,
// png, kits, devices, process, songs - and nothing a tool cannot do: no dialogs (a tool takes paths), no live systems
// and no views.
import type { Call, Host } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import type { Session } from "./session";
import { keepAlive, exitProcess } from "./session";
import { makeCall } from "../src/rpcClient";
import { createMidiClient } from "../src/realBackend";
import { filesPngHost } from "../src/hostGroups";
import { batteryListing } from "../src/batteryListing";

export type CliHost = Host<"files" | "png" | "kits" | "devices" | "process" | "songs">;

/** `args` is the tool's own argument vector, exactly what its `run(host, args)` was given: the dispatcher strips the
 *  command name, so a tool reads its flags from either. A tool that builds its host without them (or a session run by
 *  path, which has none) gets an empty vector. */
export function cliHost(session: Session, args: readonly string[] = []): CliHost {
  // The RPC channel is built on first use: a tool that never reaches a native facet (most of them) must not need one to
  // exist to have a host, which is also what lets a mock-tier test build one.
  let rpc: Call | undefined;
  return {
    ...filesPngHost(session.backend),
    kits: {
      compile: (id, spec) => session.audio.compileKitFormat(id, spec),
    },
    devices: {
      rpc: (method, ...params) => (rpc ??= makeCall())(method, ...params),
      // A factory rather than one client: a bridge opens as many as its run needs.
      midi: () => createMidiClient(),
    },
    process: {
      args: () => [...args],
      keepAlive: () => keepAlive(),
      exit: (code) => exitProcess(code),
    },
    songs: { list: (bytes) => batteryListing(bytes) },
  };
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/render/renderHost.ts`:

````ts
// The render surface's host (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3.2): what a cart's render hooks drive of
// the booted system, and the file I/O a hook may read with. Built per render over the render's own context - the
// backend and the audio driver it already holds. The render's OUTPUT stream is not here: it is the request's own sink,
// built after this host and passed to the one hook that captures into it.
import type { Host } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import type { RenderContext } from "./types";
import { filesHost } from "../hostGroups";

export type RenderHostGroups = Host<"emulator" | "files">;

export function renderHost(ctx: RenderContext): RenderHostGroups {
  return {
    emulator: {
      renderAudio: (ms) => ctx.audio.renderAudio(ms),
      readCpu: (id, addr) => ctx.backend.readCpu(id, addr),
      readRam: (id) => ctx.backend.readRam(id),
      writeRam: (id, offset, bytes) => ctx.backend.writeRam(id, offset, bytes),
      pressButton: (id, button, down) => ctx.audio.pressButton(id, button, down),
    },
    files: filesHost(ctx.backend),
  };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The tests that follow their code, and the three new ones**

The five existing test files change only their call sites: a hook's second argument is a host now, so each builds one
over its mock backend, and no assertion changed. The three new files are the contract's tests: core's group mechanics
(a `files` host cannot be given a PNG-codec hook; a name the table lacks is no group - with the note that a mapped
type accepts `Host<"nope">`, so the unknown-name refusal is not what is pinned), the shell's per-surface group lists

listing's three recorded strings.

Create `packages/core/ts/test/host.test.ts`:

````ts
// The host contract's group selections (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3.2): a hook types itself by the
// groups it uses, so a surface whose host lacks one is a compile error rather than a member that is undefined when the
// hook runs. The cases that decide that are the type errors, which `tsc` holds; the one runtime case keeps the table
// itself honest.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import type { FilesHost, Host, PngHost } from "@retroplug/core/host";

const files: FilesHost = {
  readFile: () => null,
  writeFile: () => true,
  writeFileAtomic: () => true,
  fileExists: () => false,
};
const png: PngHost = {
  encode: () => null,
  decode: () => null,
};

/** A hook that asks for the PNG codec: an asset override decodes a linked font image. */
function needsPng(host: Host<"png">): string | null {
  return host.png.decode(new Uint8Array(0)) === null ? null : "";
}

/** A hook that asks for the file reads alone. */
function needsFiles(host: Host<"files">): Uint8Array | null {
  return host.files.readFile("");
}

test("a group selection is exactly the groups it names", () => {
  const both: Host<"files" | "png"> = { files, png };
  // A host that offers more than a hook asks is what the shell passes: a surface's own host satisfies every hook
  // narrower than it.
  expect(needsFiles(both)).toBe(null);
  expect(needsPng(both)).toBe(null);

  // The refusals, held by the compiler and never run.
  const typeCases = (filesOnly: Host<"files">): void => {
    // @ts-expect-error a files host has no png group, so the codec hook cannot be given one
    needsPng(filesOnly);
    // @ts-expect-error a host lacking a group does not satisfy that group's selection (and has an excess `files`)
    const noSuchGroup: Host<"kits"> = { files };
    void noSuchGroup;
  };
  // Marks the type cases used without running them.
  expect(typeof typeCases).toBe("function");
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/hosts/host-groups.test.ts`:

````ts
// Each surface's host offers exactly the groups its type names (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 3.2): a
// group a surface lacks does not exist on its host, so asking for one is a compile error rather than a member that is
// undefined when a hook runs - which is what makes a surface's abilities its host's group list. The cases below are
// held by `tsc`; the one runtime case checks the table the compiler reads.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import type { Host, KitBank } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import type { KitCompileResult } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";
import type { CliHost } from "../../cli/cliHost";
import { cliHost } from "../../cli/cliHost";
import type { RenderHostGroups } from "../../src/render/renderHost";
import { renderHost } from "../../src/render/renderHost";
import type { RenderContext } from "../../src/render/types";
import type { Session } from "../../src/bootSession";
import { composeAppStores } from "../../src/appStores";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { createUiHost, type UiHost } from "../../ui/host/uiHost";

/** A hook that opens a file dialog. */
function needsDialogs(host: Host<"dialogs">): unknown {
  return host.dialogs;
}
/** A hook that owns the process. */
function needsProcess(host: Host<"process">): unknown {
  return host.process;
}
/** A hook that drives a booted system, which is what a render hook does. */
function needsEmulator(host: Host<"emulator">): unknown {
  return host.emulator;
}

test("a UI host is its ten groups and no others", () => {
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: new MockBackend("/cfg") });
  const ui: UiHost = createUiHost(stores, {
    views: { open: () => {} },
    beginImport: () => {},
  });
  expect(Object.keys(ui).sort()).toEqual(
    ["config", "controller", "devices", "dialogs", "files", "liveSongs", "png", "songs", "systems", "views"].sort(),
  );
  // The UI offers what a construct hook, an import and a menu need, and a hook narrower than the host takes it.
  expect(needsDialogs(ui) === ui.dialogs).toBe(true);

  // The per-surface cases. Nothing here runs - the compiler is what checks it - so the CLI and render hosts are taken
  // as types: a mock-tier test has no native session and no render context to build one over.
  const typeCases = (cli: CliHost, render: RenderHostGroups): void => {
    // Each surface's exact group list: a group added to or dropped from a host fails one of these.
    const uiGroups: Record<keyof UiHost, true> = {
      files: true, png: true, systems: true, songs: true, liveSongs: true, dialogs: true, devices: true, views: true,
      controller: true, config: true,
    };
    const cliGroups: Record<keyof CliHost, true> = {
      files: true, png: true, kits: true, devices: true, process: true, songs: true,
    };
    const renderGroups: Record<keyof RenderHostGroups, true> = { emulator: true, files: true };
    void uiGroups;
    void cliGroups;
    void renderGroups;

    // @ts-expect-error a CLI host has no dialogs group: a tool takes paths, so it never asks for a picker
    needsDialogs(cli);
    // @ts-expect-error a render host has no dialogs group either
    needsDialogs(render);
    // @ts-expect-error the UI host has no process group: the UI does not own the process
    needsProcess(ui);
    // @ts-expect-error the CLI host has no emulator group: a tool runs no live system
    needsEmulator(cli);
    expect(needsEmulator(render) === render.emulator).toBe(true);
    // @ts-expect-error the UI host has no kits group: the UI composes no audio driver
    ui.kits;
    // @ts-expect-error the CLI host has no views group: a tool shows no screen
    cli.views;
    // @ts-expect-error the render host has no systems group: a render owns one booted system, not a project's list
    render.systems;

    // A compiled kit is dsp's own type, member for member (core declares it so a host can name it without importing
    // dsp).
    const asDsp = (b: KitBank): KitCompileResult => b;
    const asCore = (r: KitCompileResult): KitBank => r;
    void asDsp;
    void asCore;
  };
  // Marks the type cases used without running them.
  expect(typeof typeCases).toBe("function");
});

test("a CLI host is its six groups, and its arguments are the tool's own", () => {
  const backend = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  // A tool run has a native host and a real audio driver; a mock tier has neither, and neither is read to have a host.
  const session = {
    backend,
    audio: { compileKitFormat: async () => ({ bytes: new Uint8Array(0), errors: [] }) },
  } as unknown as Session;
  const cli = cliHost(session, ["--show-song", "cart.srm"]);
  const keys = Object.keys(cli).sort();
  expect(keys).toEqual(["devices", "files", "kits", "png", "process", "songs"]);
  // `run(host, args)`'s args are the host's, without the command name the dispatcher stripped, as a copy the tool
  // cannot mutate the dispatcher's vector through.
  expect(cli.process.args()).toEqual(["--show-song", "cart.srm"]);
  const args = cli.process.args();
  args.push("extra");
  expect(cli.process.args()).toEqual(["--show-song", "cart.srm"]);
  // A session run by path has none.
  expect(cliHost(session).process.args()).toEqual([]);
  // The RPC caller is built on first call, not on the host's: a mock tier has no channel, and only a tool that reaches
  // a native facet should need one.
  expect(typeof cli.devices.rpc).toBe("function");
  expect(() => cli.devices.rpc("version")).toThrow("no native backend");
});

test("a render host is its two groups", () => {
  const backend = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  // A render's context is the backend, the audio driver and the stores; this host reads the first two.
  const ctx = { backend, audio: { renderAudio: () => {}, pressButton: () => {} } } as unknown as RenderContext;
  const host: RenderHostGroups = renderHost(ctx);
  expect(Object.keys(host).sort()).toEqual(["emulator", "files"]);
  expect(Object.keys(host.emulator).sort()).toEqual([
    "pressButton",
    "readCpu",
    "readRam",
    "renderAudio",
    "writeRam",
  ]);
});

test("a controller target is checked against the launchpad package's list", () => {
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: new MockBackend("/cfg") });
  const ui = createUiHost(stores, { views: { open: () => {} }, beginImport: () => {} });
  // A package hands the target over as an open string, and an unknown one would leave launches going nowhere, so it is
  // refused here rather than written into the live settings and the next save.
  expect(() => ui.controller.set({ target: "nowhere" })).toThrow("controller target 'nowhere'");
  expect(ui.controller.settings().target).toBe("system");
  ui.controller.set({ target: "midiOut" });
  expect(ui.controller.settings().target).toBe("midiOut");
  // A patch without a target leaves it alone.
  ui.controller.set({ enabled: true });
  expect(ui.controller.settings().target).toBe("midiOut");
  expect(ui.controller.settings().enabled).toBe(true);
});
````
