// `decodeAndPrint` before a cart's rows moved into its tracker integration: the header, one row per saved song and the
// refusal line are byte-identical, so `n8-load --show-song`'s output did not move with the code that composes it.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";
import { savBytes as lsdjSav } from "@retroplug/lsdj/testFixtures";
import { batteryListing } from "../../src/batteryListing";

test("a risa battery lists its songs as the old listing did", () => {
  // Recorded from the old code: the header names the cart, and each row is the slot, the name, the record version and
  // its length.
  expect(batteryListing(risaSav("v2_blumarbl"))).toEqual([
    "risa battery - 1 song(s):",
    "  [ 0] BLUMARBL  v5  6905B",
  ]);
});

test("an LSDj battery lists its projects as the old listing did", () => {
  expect(batteryListing(lsdjSav("lsdj888"))).toEqual(["LSDj battery - 1 project(s):", "  [ 0] SNDTESTx"]);
});

test("an image no cart reads gets the one refusal line naming them in rank order", () => {
  expect(batteryListing(new Uint8Array(0x8000))).toEqual([
    "unrecognized battery image (32768 bytes) - not a risa or LSDj save",
  ]);
});

Every line is one error of that run, ending in the exit status; the four `@ts-expect-error` lines that follow the first eight are the per-surface refusals losing their target

**(c) The battery listing's oracle is the OLD code's, and the command re-derives it.** `record-battery.mjs` carries
the design commit's `decodeAndPrint` verbatim and runs it over a risa save, an LSDj save and a blank 32 KB image; the
recorder is written to a scratch path and bundled from a full `git archive` of the design commit, whose own
`node_modules` (hardlinked, so each workspace link resolves inside the archive) supplies the packages it imports. The
three strings it prints are committed in `test/hosts/battery-listing.test.ts`.

````js
// Records 8a74339b9's n8-load `decodeAndPrint` output for a risa save, an LSDj save and a blank image.
import { isRisaSav, listSongs } from "@retroplug/risa";
import { isLsdjSav, listProjects } from "@retroplug/lsdj";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";
import { savBytes as lsdjSav } from "@retroplug/lsdj/testFixtures";

function decodeAndPrint(sram) {
  const out = [];
  if (isRisaSav(sram)) {
    const songs = listSongs(sram);
    out.push(`risa battery - ${songs.length} song(s):`);
    for (const song of songs)
      out.push(`  [${String(song.index).padStart(2)}] ${song.name.trim() || "(unnamed)"}  v${song.version}  ${song.length}B`);
  } else if (isLsdjSav(sram)) {
    const projects = listProjects(sram);
    out.push(`LSDj battery - ${projects.length} project(s):`);
    for (const p of projects) out.push(`  [${String(p.slot).padStart(2)}] ${p.name.trim() || "(unnamed)"}`);
  } else {
    out.push(`unrecognized battery image (${sram.length} bytes) - not a risa or LSDj save`);
  }
  return out;
}
const inputs = {
  risa: risaSav("v2_blumarbl"),
  lsdj: lsdjSav("lsdj888"),
  blank: new Uint8Array(0x8000),
};
const result = {};
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(inputs)) result[k] = decodeAndPrint(v);
console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

feat(f4b): the host contract, and the three surfaces' hosts

One grouped Host<G> in core (@retroplug/core/host) replaces the three ad hoc
slices F4a left: ConstructCaps, RenderHost and SongImportHost, and
src/songImportHost.ts with them. A group is a named capability a surface has -
files, png, kits, systems, songs, liveSongs, emulator, dialogs, devices,
process, views, controller, config - and a hook types itself by the groups it
uses, so asking a surface for one it lacks is a compile error instead of a
member that is undefined at run time.

The shell builds one host per surface, beside what it adapts:

- ui/host/uiHost.ts: createUiHost(stores, peers), built once in App.tsx over
  the stores. Its peers are App's own state: the shell's views (the HD player)
  and useSongImport's picker. importHost(backend, systems) is the three groups
  a song import uses, for the one menu call site.
- cli/cliHost.ts: cliHost(session, args) per tool run, over the backend, the
  audio driver and the process, its process.args being exactly what
  run(host, args) was given. Both hosts build the RPC caller on first call, so a
  mock-tier host that never reaches a native facet needs no channel; n8-load's
  battery listing prints through host.songs.list, byte for byte as before.
- src/render/renderHost.ts: renderHost(ctx) per render, replacing render.ts's
  local table.

The types a group names that the shell owned move to core as types only, with
the shell's module re-exporting them: the capability operation table
(@retroplug/core/capability, re-exported by src/capability.ts), PngImageData and
FileBrowserOpts (src/backend.ts), Call (src/rpcClient.ts), MidiClient
(src/realBackend.ts) and ControlSurfaceSettings (src/userConfig.ts). Controller
settings and the controller-app list keep a narrow structural type of core's
own, because the launchpad package is downstream of core; the UI host checks the
one target string against that enum and refuses an unknown value rather than
casting it.

songs.list is composed in src/batteryListing.ts over the tracker integrations'
new batteryListing: risa's rows (rank 0) and LSDj's (rank 1) live in their carts
and the shell prints them in rank order, so the UI host imports no CLI module
and n8-load's output is held by a recorded test.

Every hook that took a slice takes its groups: onConstruct and the asset
catalogs' applyRoleConfig/applyRitOverride Host<"files" | "png">, the render
hooks Host<"emulator"> (RenderPlaySink stays an explicit argument: it is the
request's stream, not an emulator capability), and a song import
Host<"files" | "png" | "systems"> - the design's "files | systems" misses the
png codec an applied font override decodes with.

Tests: core/ts/test/host.test.ts holds a group selection's refusals and
test/hosts/host-groups.test.ts each surface's exact group list, with one
@ts-expect-error per surface, the CLI and render hosts' runtime group tables,
process.args, the controller target's refusal and the KitBank/KitCompileResult
two-way assignability; test/hosts/battery-listing.test.ts holds the listing's
lines to the old n8-load output; the fakes for the render hooks and the LSDj
import now build hosts. check-boundaries' SHELL_IMPORTS gains @retroplug/core/host and
@retroplug/core/capability and loses the now-unused
@retroplug/tracker/trackerSongImport.

No behaviour changes: every menu row, tool output and golden is unchanged, and
parity, the kit and render baselines, render-chunks, the device and box images
and the pack bytes all hold.
EOF

### Task 2: the `ui` package and the declarative menu rows

Design sections 4.1 to 4.4 and 8's second stage. The menu model becomes a package's, the contribution types go beside it,
and each console package contributes its own declarative rows through a `retroplug.ui` manifest member that the generator
reads into `ui/generated/menus.ts`. The row renderer that reads and writes a role config is the shell's one, and it
reproduces the old reader's three fallbacks exactly.

The recorded menu matrix is this task's RED anchor and comes FIRST, before any menu code moves: 34 cases recorded from a
scratch tree of the design commit, each case's tree flattened (id, kind, label, `disabled`, children), every cycler's
starting label and, per step of one cycle, the label it shows afterwards beside the state the step wrote and the node
MIDI it staged. The recorder and the replay are one definition (`recorded-cases.ts`), so a row that changes placement,
label, gate, order or value fails there. The matrix is extended by Tasks 3 and 4 and derived again from the design
commit's tree each time; this task derives the final 54,613-line record and copies it into place, and the plan never
quotes it.

**Files:**

- Create (17): `packages/lsdj/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/mesen/ts/test/ui.test.ts`, `packages/mesen/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/menu/recorded-cases.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/menu/recorded-matrix.json`, `packages/retroplug/test/menu/recorded-trees.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/menu/row-carriers.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/packages/fixtures/expected/menus.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/packages/fixtures/tree/packages/alpha/ts/ui.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/host/menuContributions.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/screens/menu/configRows.ts`, `packages/sameboy/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/ui/package.json`, `packages/ui/ts/contribution.ts`, `packages/ui/ts/menu/index.ts`, `packages/ui/ts/test/rows.test.ts`, `packages/ui/tsconfig.json`
- Move (2 files, each by the `git mv` its step prints; 0 of them changed too and carry that file's diff after its move): from `packages/retroplug/ui/screens/menu/`
- Modify (48 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 13 under `packages/retroplug/test/menu/`; 5 under `packages/retroplug/ui/app/`; 3 under `packages/retroplug/ui/screens/menu/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/test/packages/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/ui/host/`; 1 under `.gitignore` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 1: The recorder, its case list, and the test-side scaffolding**

`recorded-cases.ts` is the case list and the collector, and `recorded-trees.test.ts` rebuilds every case over
`MockBackend` and `composeAppStores` and compares the tree and each cycler's steps against the record the next step
derives. It was green against the old code before the first menu edit and green against the new one unchanged. The
record itself is 54,613 lines, so it is not quoted into this plan at all: the next step produces it and the blob hash
below is what proves its bytes.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/menu/recorded-cases.ts`:

````ts
// The case matrix the menu equality test records and replays (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.5,
// item 1). Every case builds a project over MockBackend, composes the app's stores and builds the tree the menu shows:
// each console, each tracker cart with a readable ROM, a project that drives an N8 and one with a Launchpad running
// MI.MAP, a two-system project (the Link Group row), the start menu and the settings menus. The record is taken from
// the menu code before F4b moved any of it (a `git archive 8a74339b9` tree) and this module is the same code that
// replays it, so a row that changes placement, label, gate, order or the value a step writes fails there.
//
// A tree is recorded flattened (id, kind, label, disabled, children, and an inline row's verb list). A cycler is
// recorded the way a user reads it: its label after each step, beside the project state that step changed and the node
// MIDI it staged. The state is a diff of the whole reachable config (each system's role configs, the project settings,
// the user config), so a step that writes a different VALUE fails even when it writes the label its table shows, and a
// step that writes nothing (a host-only picker) records `{}`. The staged MIDI is its own list: which node each step
// aimed at and which bytes it sent, which is how a hardware row (BlipToaster's SysEx) is pinned as well as its label.
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { composeAppStores, type AppStores } from "../../src/appStores";
import { buildInstanceMenu, buildStartMenu, type MenuContext } from "../../ui/screens/menu/menuDefs";
import type { MenuItem } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import { resetN8CartJob } from "../../ui/screens/menu/n8SdOps";
import { setN8LinkClient } from "../../ui/screens/menu/n8Devices";
import {
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest, setLaunchpadClient, setLaunchpadScanClock, startLaunchpadScan,
} from "../../ui/screens/menu/launchpadDevices";
import type { LaunchpadClient } from "@retroplug/launchpad/client";
import { ROM_SIZE, BANK_SIZE, PALETTE_SIZE, PALETTE_CHECK } from "@retroplug/lsdj/rom";
import { loadSongToWorking, savFrom, injectSong } from "@retroplug/lsdj";
import { normalizeSaveContainer } from "@retroplug/risa/risaSav";
import * as R from "@retroplug/lsdj/codec/regions";
import { savBytes as risaSav } from "@retroplug/risa/testFixtures";
import {
  blipToasterRom,
  gbRom,
  gbRomBattery,
  gbaRom,
  lsdjRom,
  nesRom,
  risaRom,
  smsggdjRom,
} from "../systems/fixtures";

/** One case: the project it builds and the tree it shows. */
export interface RecordedCase {
  readonly name: string;
  /** The menu the case records: the instance menu of its first system, or the start menu (which holds the settings). */
  readonly menu: "instance" | "start";
  /** Whether the case has the two native facets' fakes mounted. Off is a machine with no N8 and no Launchpad, which is
   *  the state most systems are in: both submenus then have to be ABSENT, which the tree records like any other row. */
  readonly n8?: boolean;
  readonly launchpad?: boolean;
  /** The mock host reports itself as the standalone, which is the only host that draws Settings > MIDI, Settings > Audio
   *  and the Exit rows. `midi`/`audio` add the native seams those submenus read (a stub, so the lists are fixed). */
  readonly standalone?: boolean;
  readonly midi?: boolean;
  readonly audio?: boolean;
  /** Leave a control-surface scan in flight while the menu is read (Settings > MIDI's scan row, and the instance
   *  submenu's disabled port rows). Needs `launchpad`. */
  readonly scanning?: boolean;
  build(backend: MockBackend, stores: AppStores): void;
}

/** One step of a cycler: the label it shows afterwards, the state it wrote (empty for a host-only picker) and the node
 *  MIDI it staged (empty for a row that sends none). */
export interface RecordedStep {
  readonly label: string;
  readonly stored: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly staged: readonly { readonly nodeId: string; readonly bytes: readonly number[] }[];
}

export interface RecordedRow {
  readonly default: string;
  readonly steps: readonly RecordedStep[];
}

export interface RecordedCaseResult {
  readonly tree: readonly unknown[];
  readonly rows: Readonly<Record<string, RecordedRow>>;
  readonly dialogs: Readonly<Record<string, readonly unknown[]>>;
}

/** What the recorder writes and the equality test reads: one result per case, keyed by name. */
export type RecordedMatrix = Readonly<Record<string, RecordedCaseResult>>;

/** The `MenuContext` App.tsx assembles from its hooks, minus React. */
export function ctxOf(stores: AppStores): MenuContext {
  return {
    stores,
    settings: stores.project.settings(),
    userConfig: stores.userConfig.config(),
    bindings: stores.bindings.resolvedBindings(),
    systems: stores.project.systems.view(),
    recent: stores.recent.view(),
    version: "",
    newProject: () => {},
    loadProject: () => {},
    loadRomAsProject: () => {},
    requestExit: () => {},
    openLsdjHd: () => {},
    beginSongImport: () => {},
  };
}

/** The N8 link the mock tier has no provider for: one attached, connected port - what the submenu needs to render. */
const N8_CONFIG = {
  ports: [{ port: "/dev/ttyACM0", isN8: true }],
  selectedPort: "/dev/ttyACM0",
  connected: true,
  enabled: true,
  lookaheadMs: 10,
  bytes: 0,
  error: "",
};

/** The Launchpad facet the mock tier has no provider for: a claimed Pro MK3 pair, which is what makes the submenu
 *  render and its port rows show a live link. */
const LP_INPUTS = ["Arturia KeyStep 32", "LPProMK3 MIDI"];
const LP_OUTPUTS = ["LPProMK3 MIDI"];

function fakeLaunchpad(connected = true): LaunchpadClient {
  const status = {
    connected,
    generation: 1,
    sent: 0,
    dropped: 0,
    input: "LPProMK3 MIDI",
    output: "LPProMK3 MIDI",
    error: "",
  };
  // The loose-port pool a scan opens. Handles rather than refusals, so a scan that starts actually probes its first
  // output and waits out that output's answer window (the clock is frozen), which is the "in flight" state.
  const open = new Map<number, { input: boolean; name: string }>();
  let next = 1;
  const openPort = (input: boolean, name: string): number => {
    const handle = next++;
    open.set(handle, { input, name });
    return handle;
  };
  return {
    ports: () => ({ inputs: [...LP_INPUTS], outputs: [...LP_OUTPUTS] }),
    status: () => ({ ...status }),
    claim: () => ({ ...status }),
    release: () => ({ ...status }),
    send: () => true,
    restored: () => true,
    openInputs: (names: string[]) => names.map((name) => openPort(true, name)),
    openOutput: (name: string) => openPort(false, name),
    sendOn: () => true,
    read: () => ({ messages: [], dropped: 0 }),
    close: (handle: number) => open.delete(handle),
    portError: () => "",
  } as unknown as LaunchpadClient;
}

/** A GG or SMS cart: the Sega header read from the first bank, its region nibble the console (an SMS is 4, a Game Gear
 *  is 6). Nothing else in the image is a ROM any core boots; the menu only classifies it. */
function segaRom(region: number): Uint8Array {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(0x8000);
  bytes.set([0x54, 0x4d, 0x52, 0x20, 0x53, 0x45, 0x47, 0x41], 0x7ff0); // "TMR SEGA"
  bytes[0x7ff0 + 0xf] = region << 4;
  return bytes;
}

/** Add a system at `path` from the backend's seeded bytes and return its id. */
function add(backend: MockBackend, stores: AppStores, path: string, rom: Uint8Array): number {
  backend.seed(path, rom);
  return stores.project.systems.addSystem(path)!;
}

/** A project loaded from a document whose core-role config was written by hand: adopt keeps a core role's config as
 *  stored (SystemsStore.parsedForTheirNodes skips the core role), which is exactly the hand-edited case the menu's
 *  fallbacks exist for. */
function adoptHandEdited(
  backend: MockBackend,
  stores: AppStores,
  path: string,
  rom: Uint8Array,
  core: string,
  config: Record<string, unknown>,
): void {
  backend.seed(path, rom);
  stores.project.systems.adopt({ romPath: path, core: core as never, roles: [{ kind: core, config }] });
}

/** The Launchpad's own state (its selected pair and app) is project/user state, so it is set through the stores the
 *  way the shell's rows would leave it. `appConfig` is the project's stored config as written, which is what a
 *  hand-edited project (or an older build) leaves behind. */
function launchpadProject(stores: AppStores, app: string, appConfig: Record<string, unknown> = {}): void {
  stores.userConfig.setControlSurface({
    enabled: true,
    input: "LPProMK3 MIDI",
    output: "LPProMK3 MIDI",
    device: "Launchpad Pro [MK3]",
  });
  stores.project.setController({ app, appConfig });
}

/** A full 1 MiB LSDj ROM (the title makes the provider attach lsdj-sync). */
function lsdjRomFull(): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(ROM_SIZE);
  b.set(gbRomBattery(), 0);
  const title = "LSDJ-V9.4.2";
  for (let i = 0; i < title.length; i++) b[0x134 + i] = title.charCodeAt(i);
  const count = 2;
  b.set(PALETTE_CHECK, 1 * BANK_SIZE + 0x100 + count * PALETTE_SIZE);
  const nb = 27 * BANK_SIZE + 0x200;
  for (let i = 0; i < 3 + 2 * count; i++) for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) b[nb + i * 5 + j] = 0x41 + j;
  b[nb + 15 + 2 * count * 5 + 4] = 0x01;
  return b;
}

/** A battery with two songs at spare slots 0 and 3. */
function twoSongSav(): Uint8Array {
  const song = savFrom({ workingSong: { settings: { tempo: 120 } } }).subarray(0, 0x8000).slice();
  let sav = savFrom({});
  sav = injectSong(sav, 0, "AAA", 1, song)!;
  sav = injectSong(sav, 3, "BBB", 2, song)!;
  return sav;
}

/** The native seams a standalone host installs, and what they answer here: fixed lists, so the device rows and their
 *  cyclers are recorded without a real audio or MIDI device. */
const AUDIO_SEAM = {
  sampleRate: 48000,
  blockSize: 512,
  outChannels: 2,
  driver: "Auto",
  device: "",
  drivers: ["Auto", "PipeWire"],
  devicesByDriver: { Auto: ["", "Built-in Audio"], PipeWire: ["", "Built-in Audio"] },
  defaultByDriver: { Auto: "Built-in Audio", PipeWire: "Built-in Audio" },
  autoDriver: "PipeWire",
};
const MIDI_SEAM = {
  inputs: ["Arturia KeyStep 32", "LPProMK3 MIDI"],
  outputs: ["LPProMK3 MIDI"],
  selectedInput: "",
  selectedOutput: "",
};

/** A tree with its children inline, which is what was recorded: every item's identity and gate, in order. */
export function flat(items: readonly MenuItem[]): unknown[] {
  return items.map((i) => ({
    id: i.id,
    kind: i.kind,
    label: i.label,
    ...(i.disabled === true ? { disabled: true } : {}),
    ...(i.children ? { children: flat(i.children) } : {}),
  }));
}

/** Every item of a tree, children first-consumed in document order. */
function walk(items: readonly MenuItem[], out: MenuItem[] = []): MenuItem[] {
  for (const i of items) {
    out.push(i);
    if (i.children) walk(i.children, out);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The project state a menu row can change, as one JSON-shaped object: each system's role configs (by position, so a
 *  run's allocated ids do not reach the record), the project settings and the user config. */
function snapshot(stores: AppStores): unknown {
  const systems: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  stores.project.systems.view().forEach((s, i) => {
    const roles: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    s.roles.forEach((r, j) => (roles[String(j)] = { kind: r.kind, config: r.config }));
    systems[`sys${i}`] = { roles };
  });
  return { systems, project: stores.project.settings(), user: stores.userConfig.config() };
}

/** A staging target by POSITION rather than by the id a run happened to allocate, so the record replays anywhere: a
 *  node a call aims at names its system ("sys-<id>", "cart-<id>"), and the record's system is its slot. */
function nodeKey(stores: AppStores, nodeId: string): string {
  const m = /^(sys|cart)-(\d+)$/.exec(nodeId);
  if (!m) return nodeId;
  const at = stores.project.systems.view().findIndex((s) => s.id === Number(m[2]));
  return at < 0 ? nodeId : `${m[1]}${at}`;
}

/** The paths at which `after` differs from `before`, with the value each holds after the step. */
function diff(before: unknown, after: unknown, path: string, out: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  if (JSON.stringify(before) === JSON.stringify(after)) return;
  const both =
    before !== null &&
    after !== null &&
    typeof before === "object" &&
    typeof after === "object" &&
    !Array.isArray(before) &&
    !Array.isArray(after);
  if (!both) {
    out[path] = after === undefined ? "<absent>" : after;
    return;
  }
  const a = before as Record<string, unknown>;
  const b = after as Record<string, unknown>;
  for (const key of new Set([...Object.keys(a), ...Object.keys(b)]))
    diff(a[key], b[key], path ? `${path}.${key}` : key, out);
}

/** The rows that open a file browser: a card operation's filter is part of the menu, so its dialog options are
 *  recorded beside the tree. */
const CARD_DIALOG_ROWS = new Set(["n8-load-rom", "n8-dump-sram", "n8-restore-sram"]);

/** One case: its tree, then each cycler it shows, stepped one full cycle and read the way a user reads it. */
function recordCase(c: RecordedCase): RecordedCaseResult {
  // The mock tier has no native host, so the two facets and the standalone seams the submenus gate on are stubbed here
  // and cleared after; a case that does not build a system still gets them (the start menu shows the N8 block from the
  // same seam).
  resetN8CartJob();
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  setLaunchpadScanClock(() => 0);
  const globals = globalThis as Record<string, unknown>;
  const seams = { standalone: globals.__rp_isStandalone, midi: globals.__rp_getMidiConfig, audio: globals.__rp_getAudioConfig };
  if (c.standalone === true) globals.__rp_isStandalone = true;
  if (c.midi === true) globals.__rp_getMidiConfig = () => ({ ...MIDI_SEAM });
  if (c.audio === true) globals.__rp_getAudioConfig = () => ({ ...AUDIO_SEAM });
  if (c.n8 === true)
    setN8LinkClient({
      linkConfig: () => ({ ...N8_CONFIG }),
      setPort: () => {},
      connect: () => {},
      setLookahead: () => {},
    });
  // A scan is refused while the link holds a pair (those ports cannot be reopened), so the scanning case's device is
  // enumerated by its port name and not yet claimed, which is the state Settings > MIDI's scan exists for.
  if (c.launchpad === true) setLaunchpadClient(fakeLaunchpad(c.scanning !== true));
  if (c.scanning === true) startLaunchpadScan();
  try {
    const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
    const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
    c.build(be, stores);
    const tree = (): MenuItem[] => {
      const ctx = ctxOf(stores);
      if (c.menu === "start") return buildStartMenu(ctx).items;
      return buildInstanceMenu({ ...ctx, system: stores.project.systems.view()[0] }).items;
    };

    const recorded = flat(tree());
    const rows: Record<string, RecordedRow> = {};
    // Every cycler the tree shows, in document order. A row that a step gates away ends its own cycle there: the row
    // is gone, so there is no next label to read.
    for (const id of walk(tree())
      .filter((i) => i.kind === "cycler")
      .map((i) => i.id)) {
      if (rows[id]) continue;
      const first = walk(tree()).find((i) => i.id === id);
      if (!first) continue;
      const start = first.label;
      const steps: RecordedStep[] = [];
      for (let n = 0; n < 60; n++) {
        const row = walk(tree()).find((i) => i.id === id);
        if (!row) break;
        const before = snapshot(stores);
        const stagedFrom = be.stageNodeMidiCalls.length;
        row.onCycle!(1);
        const stored: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        diff(before, snapshot(stores), "", stored);
        const staged = be.stageNodeMidiCalls.slice(stagedFrom).map((call) => ({
          nodeId: nodeKey(stores, call.nodeId),
          bytes: call.bytes,
        }));
        const next = walk(tree()).find((i) => i.id === id);
        if (!next) {
          steps.push({ label: "<row gone>", stored, staged });
          break;
        }
        steps.push({ label: next.label, stored, staged });
        if (next.label === start) break;
      }
      rows[id] = { default: start, steps };
    }
    // The card rows' file dialogs: the options each opens with (title, filter, save flag, default name). A filter is
    // how a hardware operation names what it may upload, so it is part of what the menu must not change; selecting a
    // row is enough, because the mock browser answers null and the operation behind the dialog never runs.
    const dialogs: Record<string, readonly unknown[]> = {};
    for (const row of walk(tree()).filter((i) => i.kind === "action" && CARD_DIALOG_ROWS.has(i.id))) {
      const from = be.fileBrowserCalls.length;
      row.onSelect!();
      if (be.fileBrowserCalls.length > from) dialogs[row.id] = be.fileBrowserCalls.slice(from);
    }
    return { tree: recorded, rows, dialogs };
  } finally {
    setN8LinkClient(undefined);
    setLaunchpadClient(undefined);
    resetN8CartJob();
    resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
    globals.__rp_isStandalone = seams.standalone;
    globals.__rp_getMidiConfig = seams.midi;
    globals.__rp_getAudioConfig = seams.audio;
  }
}

/** The whole matrix, in case order. */
export function collect(): RecordedMatrix {
  const out: Record<string, RecordedCaseResult> = {};
  for (const c of CASES) out[c.name] = recordCase(c);
  return out;
}

````ts
// The menus held to what the OLD code built (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.5, item 1), for the whole
// matrix the case file describes: every console, every tracker cart, a project that drives an N8 and one with a
// Launchpad running MI.MAP, a two-system project (the Link Group row), the start menu and the settings menus, a
// standalone host with a control-surface scan idle and in flight, the trackers with songs and a working song, an
// override and a pinned BlipToaster, a tracker whose ROM cannot be read, and the role and controller configs a
// hand-edited project can hold.
//
// ./recorded-matrix.json was recorded from 8a74339b9's menu code before F4b moved any of it: a `git archive 8a74339b9`
// tree, over the same ./recorded-cases.ts this test replays, printed `collect()`'s JSON from a throwaway recorder test
// that stayed outside the repository. Each case's tree carries every item's id, kind, label, `disabled` flag, children
// and an inline row's verbs in order; each cycler carries its starting label and, per step, the label it shows
// afterwards beside the project state the step wrote (a diff of the systems' role configs, the project settings and the
// user config) and the node MIDI it staged (by node position, and the bytes), so a row whose choice list is paired with
// the wrong values, whose step writes another value than the old one did, or whose step aims a message at another node
// fails here even though its labels read the same. Each case's card rows also carry the file dialogs they open (the
// N8's Load ROM filter among them), recorded from the same old tree and held here.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import recorded from "./recorded-matrix.json";
import { CASES, collect, type RecordedMatrix } from "./recorded-cases";

// One record for the whole file: rebuilding the matrix is the expensive part, and every case's own expectations are
// independent of the others (a case builds its own stores and stubs its own facets).
let recordedNow: RecordedMatrix | undefined;
function matrix(): RecordedMatrix {
  return (recordedNow ??= collect());
}

for (const c of CASES) {
  test(`${c.name}: the menu tree is the recorded one`, () => {
    const want = (recorded as unknown as RecordedMatrix)[c.name];
    expect(matrix()[c.name].tree, `${c.name} tree`).toEqual(want.tree);
  });

  test(`${c.name}: every cycler reads and writes what was recorded`, () => {
    const want = (recorded as unknown as RecordedMatrix)[c.name];
    expect(matrix()[c.name].rows, `${c.name} rows`).toEqual(want.rows);
  });

  test(`${c.name}: every card dialog offers what was recorded`, () => {
    const want = (recorded as unknown as RecordedMatrix)[c.name];
    expect(matrix()[c.name].dialogs, `${c.name} dialogs`).toEqual(want.dialogs);
  });
}
````

Create `packages/ui/ts/contribution.ts`:

````ts
// What a package's UI module declares (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.2): the system-settings rows it
// adds as DATA (a role-config knob, its choices and its gate), the menu fragments a function builds where data cannot
// say it (a state machine over a native host, a peer count), its tracker specs, and the services its device needs
// polled or subscribed to. A manifest's `retroplug.ui` member names the module, which default-exports
// defineUi({ ... }); the generator concatenates them in product order into packages/retroplug/ui/generated/menus.ts.
//
// Everything here is plain TypeScript: the contract a package's module is checked against, and the helpers that read a
// row's stored value the way the shell renders it. The React kit is F4c's, in this package beside the menu model.
import type { Host, SystemInfo } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import type { AssetCatalog, AssetTypeInfo } from "@retroplug/tracker/assetCatalog";
import type { SongCatalog } from "@retroplug/tracker/songCatalog";
import type { MenuItem } from "./menu";

/** The groups a UI surface's host has: what a package's UI code may reach. The shell builds this host once per UI
 *  (ui/host/uiHost.ts) and a contribution is handed it; core declares the groups, so this is a selection, not a new
 *  contract. */
export type UiHost = Host<
  "files" | "png" | "systems" | "songs" | "liveSongs" | "dialogs" | "devices" | "views" | "controller" | "config"
>;

/** One choice of a config row: the value the role schema stores and the label the cycler shows. */
export interface ConfigChoice {
  readonly value: string | number;
  readonly label: string;
}

/** A row over one config key: a fixed choice list, an Off/On toggle, or a numeric range offered in steps. */
export type ConfigRow = { readonly key: string; readonly label: string } & (
  | { readonly choices: readonly ConfigChoice[] } // exact match; a value the list does not have reads as index 0
  | { readonly toggle: true } // Off/On, a boolean key
  | { readonly range: { readonly steps: readonly number[]; readonly labels: readonly string[] } } // nearest step
);

/** A row over a system's role config: what the shell renders as a cycler and edits with systems.setRoleConfig. Its id
 *  is the row's menu id, byte-identical to the hand-built row it replaces. */
export type RoleRow = ConfigRow & {
  /** The row id, byte-identical to today's ("sys-model"). */
  readonly id: string;
  /** The role kind whose config holds `key` ("sameboy", "mesen", "lsdj-sync"). */
  readonly role: string;
  /** Shown only on these platforms (the NES block): absent means every platform the role attaches to. */
  readonly platforms?: readonly string[];
  /** Shown only when the sibling key `key` is one of `in` / none of `notIn` (the DMG/CGB display split). */
  readonly when?: { readonly key: string; readonly in?: readonly string[]; readonly notIn?: readonly string[] };
  /** A separator id emitted before the first visible row carrying it, so a fenced group keeps its fence whichever of
   *  its rows shows first. */
  readonly separatorBefore?: string;
};

/** Where a builder's rows land. Rows (RoleRow) take "system.settings" alone; a builder takes whichever placement it
 *  fills. "instance.footer" is the block after Remove Instance and before Exit (the Link Group). The list is data so
 *  the generated registry reads the same one the type is built from: a placement added here reaches its check without
 *  a second copy to update. */
export const PLACEMENTS = [
  "instance.tracker",
  "instance.devices",
  "instance.footer",
  "system.settings",
  "start",
  "settings.midi",
] as const;
export type Placement = (typeof PLACEMENTS)[number];

/** What a builder reads that is not the host: the project's systems, and the shell's per-path base-ROM cache (a
 *  catalog parses the ROM once per path rather than per menu build). */
export interface MenuBuildContext {
  readonly systems: readonly SystemInfo[];
  assetRom(romPath: string): Uint8Array | null;
}

/** A menu fragment a package builds itself, because its content is state the row data cannot hold. `[]` hides the
 *  entry (no device attached, no peers to link). */
export interface MenuBuilder {
  readonly placement: Placement;
  build(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo | null, ctx: MenuBuildContext): MenuItem[];
}

/** A tracker's Songs submenu: the shared menu's structure over a SongCatalog, and the file-dialog actions its cart
 *  owns (only a cart knows its song formats). Callbacks take the host because every file op goes through it. */
export interface SongMenuSpec {
  /** Row-id prefix, e.g. "lsdj" / "risa". */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly catalog: SongCatalog;
  exportSong(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number, name: string): void;
  replaceSong(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number): void;
  addSong(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo): void;
  /** The synthetic working-song row's actions (only for a console whose catalog reports an unsaved working song). */
  exportWorking?(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, name: string): void;
  saveWorkingToCatalog?(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo): void;
  /** Commit the live working song into the catalog: the pure byte-op behind "Save Working Song & Load". Null
   *  when declined, so the menu greys the row rather than offering a save that fails. */
  commitWorking?(sav: Uint8Array, name?: string): Uint8Array | null;
  /** True when the working song has no name to inherit and the user must supply one. */
  workingNeedsName?(sav: Uint8Array): boolean;
  /** Whether there is anywhere to put it: a cheap test, asked once per menu build. Omitted = assume yes. */
  canCommitWorking?(sav: Uint8Array): boolean;
}

/** A tracker's asset submenus: the shared structure over an AssetCatalog, and the per-cart file actions. */
export interface AssetMenuSpec {
  /** Row-id and submenu-id prefix, e.g. "lsdj" / "risa". */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly catalog: AssetCatalog;
  exportAsset(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, type: AssetTypeInfo, slot: number, label: string): void;
  replaceAsset(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, type: AssetTypeInfo, slot: number): void;
  /** A console where one slot of an asset type is the LIVE one returns it, so the list is also the picker; null for a
   *  type that has no such notion. Omitted by a console whose rows are the plain override list. */
  selectedSlot?(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, kind: string): number | null;
  selectSlot?(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, kind: string, slot: number): void;
}

/** A tracker's UI: its song and asset specs, its role-config rows and any fragment it builds. Keyed to its integration
 *  by id, so the shell finds this for the tracker a system resolved. */
export interface TrackerUi {
  /** The integration id (TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS' key, e.g. "lsdj"). */
  readonly id: string;
  /** The cart's song and asset specs: a cart contributes the ones it has (an asset-only cart has no Songs submenu). */
  readonly song?: SongMenuSpec;
  readonly asset?: AssetMenuSpec;
  readonly extras?: {
    readonly rows?: readonly RoleRow[];
    build?(host: UiHost, sys: SystemInfo, ctx: MenuBuildContext): MenuItem[];
  };
}

/** A UI service: a device's state the menu shows, kept current without a React hook. `start` runs once when the UI is
 *  up, `subscribe` asks for a repaint on a native-host change, and `poll` runs every `frames` render frames (true =
 *  repaint). The version-and-edge latches live in the service's own closure, so a remount changes nothing. */
export interface UiService {
  readonly id: string;
  start?(host: UiHost): void;
  subscribe?(listener: () => void): () => void;
  poll?: { readonly frames: number; run(host: UiHost): boolean };
}

/** Everything a package's UI module contributes. */
export interface UiContribution {
  /** Role-config rows, which the shell renders in the System submenu for every system whose roles they name. */
  readonly rows?: readonly RoleRow[];
  readonly menus?: readonly MenuBuilder[];
  readonly trackers?: readonly TrackerUi[];
  readonly services?: readonly UiService[];
}

/** The identity function with types: a UI module's default export, checked against what a package may contribute. */
export function defineUi(contribution: UiContribution): UiContribution {
  return contribution;
}

/** How a row reads: the labels a cycler steps through, where the stored value points, and the value a step applies. */
export interface RowReading {
  readonly names: readonly string[];
  readonly index: number;
  /** The value to store when the cycler steps to `step`. */
  at(step: number): string | number | boolean;
}

/** The index of the preset in `steps` nearest `value`, so a cycler over a continuous value still shows the current
 *  setting when it is off-grid (a project written by an older build, or by hand). */
export function nearestIndex(steps: readonly number[], value: number): number {
  let best = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < steps.length; i++) {
    if (Math.abs(steps[i] - value) < Math.abs(steps[best] - value)) best = i;
  }
  return best;
}

/** Whether a value of the wrong type reads as the schema's default: the shell's long-standing rule, so a project
 *  written with a string where a number belongs shows the default rather than a blank. */
function typed(value: unknown, fallback: unknown): unknown {
  return typeof value === typeof fallback ? value : fallback;
}

/** Read a config row's stored value the way the shell renders it: the three fallbacks are the default for a wrong
 *  type, index 0 for a choice the list does not have, and the nearest step for a range. `fallback` is the role
 *  schema's default for the row's key (`schema.parse({})[key]`). */
export function readConfigRow(row: ConfigRow, stored: unknown, fallback: unknown): RowReading {
  const value = typed(stored, fallback);
  if ("choices" in row) {
    const names = row.choices.map((choice) => choice.label);
    const found = row.choices.findIndex((choice) => choice.value === value);
    return { names, index: Math.max(0, found), at: (step) => row.choices[step].value };
  }
  if ("toggle" in row) {
    const on = value === true;
    return { names: ["Off", "On"], index: on ? 1 : 0, at: (step) => step === 1 };
  }
  const numeric = typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value);
  return {
    names: row.range.labels,
    index: nearestIndex(row.range.steps, Number.isFinite(numeric) ? numeric : row.range.steps[0]),
    at: (step) => row.range.steps[step],
  };
}

/** Where a controller app's row points for a stored value, the way those rows have always read it: the rule predates
 *  the typed fallback `readConfigRow` gives a role row, and an app's knobs keep it so a hand-edited project's menu reads
 *  exactly as it did. A toggle is On unless it is `false`; a choice list with no match shows its first label. The app's
 *  RUNTIME still falls back to its schema's default (`parseAppConfig`), so an invalid stored value can read one way and
 *  run another: that latent display bug is owed, not fixed by a move. A `range` row (which these rows did not have) has
 *  no legacy reading, so the caller reads it the typed way. */
export function legacyConfigIndex(row: ConfigRow, value: unknown): number | undefined {
  if ("range" in row) return undefined;
  if ("toggle" in row) return value === false ? 0 : 1;
  return Math.max(0, row.choices.findIndex((choice) => choice.value === value));
}

/** Whether a row is shown on `platform` (no `platforms` means the role's own reach is the gate). */
export function rowShownOn(row: RoleRow, platform: string): boolean {
  return row.platforms === undefined || row.platforms.includes(platform);
}

/** Whether a row's `when` passes, given the sibling key's stored value and its schema default. A row with no `when`
 *  always passes. */
export function rowShownFor(row: RoleRow, stored: unknown, fallback: unknown): boolean {
  if (!row.when) return true;
  const value = String(typed(stored, fallback));
  if (row.when.in && !row.when.in.includes(value)) return false;
  if (row.when.notIn && row.when.notIn.includes(value)) return false;
  return true;
}
````

Create `packages/ui/ts/test/rows.test.ts`:

````ts
// Reading a config row the way the menu renders it (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.2): the labels a
// cycler shows, the index a stored value reads as, and the value a step applies. The three fallbacks are the shell's
// long-standing behaviour, kept byte-identical by a declarative row so a project written by an older build (or by hand)
// shows what it did: a value of the wrong type reads as the schema default, a choice the list does not hold reads as
// index 0, and an off-grid number reads as the nearest step.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { nearestIndex, readConfigRow, rowShownFor, rowShownOn, type RoleRow } from "../contribution";

const CHANNELS: RoleRow = {
  id: "sys-channel",
  role: "test-role",
  key: "channel",
  label: "Channel",
  choices: [
    { value: "left", label: "Left" },
    { value: "right", label: "Right" },
  ],
};
const DIVISOR: RoleRow = {
  id: "sys-divisor",
  role: "test-role",
  key: "divisor",
  label: "Divisor",
  choices: [
    { value: 1, label: "1" },
    { value: 2, label: "2" },
    { value: 4, label: "4" },
  ],
};
const FAST: RoleRow = { id: "sys-fast", role: "test-role", key: "fast", label: "Fast", toggle: true };
const TEMP: RoleRow = {
  id: "sys-temp",
  role: "test-role",
  key: "temp",
  label: "Temp",
  range: { steps: [-1, 0, 1], labels: ["Cool", "Neutral", "Warm"] },
};

test("a choice row reads its stored value, and index 0 for one it does not hold", () => {
  const right = readConfigRow(CHANNELS, "right", "left");
  expect(right.names).toEqual(["Left", "Right"]);
  expect(right.index).toBe(1);
  expect(right.at(0)).toBe("left");
  const unlisted = readConfigRow(CHANNELS, "middle", "left");
  expect(unlisted.index).toBe(0);
});

test("a wrong type reads as the schema default", () => {
  // A string where the schema stores a number: the default's type decides, so a number row given "4" reads its default.
  expect(readConfigRow(DIVISOR, "4", 2).index).toBe(1);
  // A number where the schema stores a boolean or a string: the default again.
  expect(readConfigRow(FAST, 1, true).index).toBe(1);
  expect(readConfigRow(FAST, false, true).index).toBe(0);
  expect(readConfigRow(CHANNELS, 3, "right").index).toBe(1);
});

test("a range row reads the nearest step, and applies that step's value", () => {
  const near = readConfigRow(TEMP, 0.7, 0);
  expect(near.names).toEqual(["Cool", "Neutral", "Warm"]);
  expect(near.index).toBe(2);
  expect(near.at(2)).toBe(1);
  expect(nearestIndex([-1, 0, 1], 0.4)).toBe(1);
  // An off-grid value from a project written by another build still shows a step rather than a blank.
  expect(readConfigRow(TEMP, -0.9, 0).index).toBe(0);
  // A stored value of the wrong type is the default before the nearest step is taken.
  expect(readConfigRow(TEMP, "warm", -1).index).toBe(0);
});

test("a platform gate and a when gate decide whether a row shows", () => {
  expect(rowShownOn(CHANNELS, "gba")).toBe(true);
  const nesOnly: RoleRow = { ...CHANNELS, platforms: ["nes"] };
  expect(rowShownOn(nesOnly, "nes")).toBe(true);
  expect(rowShownOn(nesOnly, "gb")).toBe(false);

  const dmgOnly: RoleRow = {
    ...CHANNELS,
    when: { key: "model", in: ["dmgB", "mgb"] },
  };
  expect(rowShownFor(dmgOnly, "dmgB", "cgbC")).toBe(true);
  expect(rowShownFor(dmgOnly, "cgbC", "cgbC")).toBe(false);
  // A sibling value of the wrong type falls back to its default before the gate reads it.
  expect(rowShownFor(dmgOnly, 7, "dmgB")).toBe(true);
  const notDmg: RoleRow = { ...CHANNELS, when: { key: "model", notIn: ["dmgB", "mgb"] } };
  expect(rowShownFor(notDmg, "cgbC", "cgbC")).toBe(true);
  expect(rowShownFor(notDmg, "dmgB", "cgbC")).toBe(false);
  // No when clause at all always passes.
  expect(rowShownFor(CHANNELS, undefined, undefined)).toBe(true);
});
````

````ts
// SameBoy's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.3): the core-role knobs the
// System submenu offers for a Game Boy, as declarative rows. A row says which role config key it edits, its choices (or
// Off/On, or a range's steps) and its gate; the shell renders it as a cycler and edits it with
// systems.setRoleConfig, so a label table or a default lives here, beside the schema whose values it spells.
//
// The display group keeps the split the core makes: colour correction and light temperature apply only to a CGB model
// and the DMG palette only to a DMG one (see app.ts). `auto` counts as CGB, because RetroPlug resolves it to CGB-C, so
// it gets the CGB rows. The separator before the group is `separatorBefore` on the first row of either side, so the
// fence shows whichever of the two groups is up.
import { defineUi, type RoleRow } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import {
  COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES,
  DMG_PALETTE_VALUES,
  HIGHPASS_VALUES,
  MODEL_VALUES,
  type SameBoyModel,
} from "../enums";

/** The model names in MODEL_VALUES' order: SameBoy's enum as the menu spells it, `auto` first. */
const MODEL_NAMES = [
  "Auto",
  "DMG-B",
  "MGB",
  "SGB",
  "SGB PAL",
  "SGB2",
  "CGB-0",
  "CGB-A",
  "CGB-B",
  "CGB-C",
  "CGB-D",
  "CGB-E",
  "AGB",
  "GBP",
];
const HIGHPASS_NAMES = ["Off", "Accurate", "DC-Block"];
const COLOR_CORRECTION_NAMES = [
  "Off",
  "Correct Curves",
  "Balanced",
  "Boost Contrast",
  "Reduce Contrast",
  "Low Contrast",
  "Accurate",
];
const DMG_PALETTE_NAMES = ["Grey", "DMG", "MGB", "GBL"];
/** Light temperature is a continuous -1..1 in the core; the menu has cyclers, not sliders, so it offers 11 steps over
 *  the full range (upstream's own slider is 21, a lot of key presses for a tint). Stored as the double, so a value from
 *  elsewhere still round-trips to the closest row. */
const LIGHT_TEMP_STEPS = [-1, -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1];
const LIGHT_TEMP_NAMES = [
  "Cool 100%",
  "Cool 80%",
  "Cool 60%",
  "Cool 40%",
  "Cool 20%",
  "Neutral",
  "Warm 20%",
  "Warm 40%",
  "Warm 60%",
  "Warm 80%",
  "Warm 100%",
];

/** The models that render in DMG mode, i.e. the ones the DMG palette applies to. Mirrors the core's own split:
 *  GB_is_cgb is `model >= GB_MODEL_CGB_0`, and everything below it takes its colours from GB_update_dmg_palette instead
 *  of the CGB palette RAM. `auto` is NOT one of them: RetroPlug resolves it to CGB-C, so it gets the CGB rows. */
const DMG_MODELS: readonly SameBoyModel[] = ["dmgB", "mgb", "sgb", "sgbPal", "sgb2"];

const choices = <T extends string>(values: readonly T[], labels: readonly string[]) =>
  values.map((value, i) => ({ value, label: labels[i] }));

export const SAMEBOY_ROWS: readonly RoleRow[] = [
  { id: "sys-model", label: "Model", role: "sameboy", key: "model", choices: choices(MODEL_VALUES, MODEL_NAMES) },
  {
    id: "sys-highpass",
    label: "Highpass",
    role: "sameboy",
    key: "highpass",
    choices: choices(HIGHPASS_VALUES, HIGHPASS_NAMES),
  },
  { id: "sys-fastboot", label: "Fast Boot", role: "sameboy", key: "fastBoot", toggle: true },
  {
    id: "sys-dmg-palette",
    label: "DMG Palette",
    role: "sameboy",
    key: "dmgPalette",
    choices: choices(DMG_PALETTE_VALUES, DMG_PALETTE_NAMES),
    when: { key: "model", in: DMG_MODELS },
    separatorBefore: "sys-sep-display",
  },
  {
    id: "sys-color-correction",
    label: "Color Correction",
    role: "sameboy",
    key: "colorCorrection",
    choices: choices(COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES, COLOR_CORRECTION_NAMES),
    when: { key: "model", notIn: DMG_MODELS },
    separatorBefore: "sys-sep-display",
  },
  {
    id: "sys-light-temp",
    label: "Light Temp",
    role: "sameboy",
    key: "lightTemperature",
    range: { steps: LIGHT_TEMP_STEPS, labels: LIGHT_TEMP_NAMES },
    when: { key: "model", notIn: DMG_MODELS },
  },
];

export default defineUi({ rows: SAMEBOY_ROWS });
````

````ts
// Mesen's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.3): the core-role knobs the
// System submenu offers for a Mesen console, as declarative rows. Mesen's one role holds every platform's settings, so
// a row's gate is the PLATFORM (`platforms`), not the core: region, the sprite limit, the APU flush window, the
// expansion chip's volume and driving a real cart are NES knobs, FM audio is the SMS/GG one, and a GBA has none yet.
//
// Two numeric knobs are RANGES with a handful of steps: the role schema accepts any value inside its bound, so a
// project written elsewhere still shows the nearest step rather than a blank. `driveRealCart` is the descriptor's own
// opt-out field (`realCartOptOut`), read by buildGraph to decide which system drives the physical cart; the NES
// descriptor names that field as this row's key, and mesen's ts/test/ui.test.ts pins the two spellings together.
import { defineUi, type RoleRow } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { REGION_VALUES } from "../enums";

/** Console region (ConsoleRegion 0..4), the "mesen" role's region knob. */
const REGION_NAMES = ["Auto", "NTSC", "PAL", "Dendy", "NTSC-J"];
/** APU flush-window latency presets (ms). The role accepts any value in [0.25, 6.0]; 1.4 ms is the historical window,
 *  so it is the default the row starts on. */
const APU_LATENCY_MS = [0.5, 1.0, 1.4, 3.0, 5.0];
const APU_LATENCY_NAMES = ["0.5 ms", "1.0 ms", "1.4 ms", "3.0 ms", "5.0 ms"];
/** The expansion chip's level as a percentage of the hardware's mix (never the 2A03's): a cart without an expansion
 *  chip hears nothing from it. A connected Everdrive N8 Pro gets the same value as its node's param. */
const EXP_VOLUMES = [0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 200];
const EXP_VOLUME_NAMES = EXP_VOLUMES.map((v) => (v === 0 ? "Off" : v === 100 ? "100% (unity)" : `${v}%`));

export const MESEN_ROWS: readonly RoleRow[] = [
  {
    id: "sys-nes-region",
    label: "Region",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "region",
    platforms: ["nes"],
    choices: REGION_VALUES.map((value, i) => ({ value, label: REGION_NAMES[i] })),
  },
  {
    id: "sys-nes-spritelimit",
    label: "Remove Sprite Limit",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "removeSpriteLimit",
    platforms: ["nes"],
    toggle: true,
  },
  {
    id: "sys-nes-apu-latency",
    label: "APU Latency",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "apuLatencyMs",
    platforms: ["nes"],
    range: { steps: APU_LATENCY_MS, labels: APU_LATENCY_NAMES },
  },
  {
    id: "sys-nes-exp-volume",
    label: "Expansion Volume",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "expansionVolume",
    platforms: ["nes"],
    range: { steps: EXP_VOLUMES, labels: EXP_VOLUME_NAMES },
  },
  {
    id: "sys-nes-drive-cart",
    label: "Drive Real Cart",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "driveRealCart",
    platforms: ["nes"],
    toggle: true,
  },
  {
    id: "sys-sms-fm",
    label: "FM Audio",
    role: "mesen",
    key: "enableFm",
    platforms: ["sms", "gg"],
    toggle: true,
  },
];

export default defineUi({ rows: MESEN_ROWS });
````

````ts
// Two spellings of one fact, pinned (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.3). "Drive Real Cart" is a
// declarative row over the mesen role's `driveRealCart`, and the NES console descriptor names the same field as its
// real-cart opt-out (`realCartOptOut`), which buildGraph reads to decide which system's traffic reaches a physical cart.
// A rename on either side would leave the row editing a key nothing places by, and nothing else would notice.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MESEN_ROWS } from "../ui";
import { MESEN_ROLE } from "../app";
import consoles from "../consoles";

test("the Drive Real Cart row edits the field the NES descriptor names as its real-cart opt-out", () => {
  const nes = consoles.consoles?.find((descriptor) => descriptor.platforms.some((p) => p.id === "nes"));
  expect(nes !== undefined).toBe(true);
  const optOut = nes!.platforms.find((p) => p.id === "nes")!.realCartOptOut;
  const row = MESEN_ROWS.find((r) => r.id === "sys-nes-drive-cart");
  expect(row !== undefined).toBe(true);
  expect(row!.key).toBe(optOut);
  // The row is a toggle over the role's own field, and its default is the schema's (ON: every project drove a cart
  // before the setting existed).
  expect("toggle" in row!).toBe(true);
  expect(MESEN_ROLE.schema.parse({})[row!.key]).toBe(true);
});

test("the NES rows are gated on the platform, and every row edits a key of the mesen schema", () => {
  const schema = MESEN_ROLE.schema.parse({});
  for (const row of MESEN_ROWS) {
    expect(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(schema, row.key)).toBe(true);
    expect(row.role).toBe("mesen");
  }
  const nesRows = MESEN_ROWS.filter((row) => row.platforms?.includes("nes")).map((row) => row.id);
  expect(nesRows).toEqual([
    "sys-nes-region",
    "sys-nes-spritelimit",
    "sys-nes-apu-latency",
    "sys-nes-exp-volume",
    "sys-nes-drive-cart",
  ]);
  expect(MESEN_ROWS.find((row) => row.id === "sys-sms-fm")!.platforms).toEqual(["sms", "gg"]);
});
````

// LSDj's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.3): its sync rows, which live in
// the LSDj instance submenu rather than the System one, so they are a TrackerUi's `extras.rows` over the `lsdj-sync`
// role. The HD Player action and the separator after the sync block stay the shell's until the tracker entries'
// builders land; the rows are data, so a name table or a default lives here beside the role schema that names them.
import { defineUi, type TrackerUi } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { LSDJ_MODE_VALUES } from "../enums";

/** LSDj sync modes (LsdjSyncMode 0..8), as the menu spells them. All shown; "Keyboard"(4) is not yet driven. "MIDI
 *  Out"(7, SYNC=MI.OUT) and "Master Sync"(8, SYNC=LSDJ) are the two LSDj-to-host MIDI-out modes. */
const LSDJ_MODE_NAMES = [
  "Off",
  "MIDI Sync",
  "MIDI Sync (Arduinoboy)",
  "MIDI Map",
  "Keyboard",
  "Keyboard MIDI",
  "MIDI Passthrough",
  "MIDI Out",
  "Master Sync",
];
/** Tempo divisor subdivides the 24-PPQN clock (24/divisor) for MIDI Sync + MIDI Sync (Arduinoboy). */
const LSDJ_DIVISORS = [1, 2, 4, 8];

/** The tracker's UI: its sync rows today, its Songs and asset specs when those move here. */
export const LSDJ_TRACKER_UI: TrackerUi = {
  id: "lsdj",
  extras: {
    rows: [
      {
        id: "lsdj-mode",
        label: "Mode",
        role: "lsdj-sync",
        key: "mode",
        choices: LSDJ_MODE_VALUES.map((value, i) => ({ value, label: LSDJ_MODE_NAMES[i] })),
      },
      {
        id: "lsdj-divisor",
        label: "Tempo Divisor",
        role: "lsdj-sync",
        key: "tempoDivisor",
        choices: LSDJ_DIVISORS.map((value) => ({ value, label: String(value) })),
      },
      // Auto Start taps START on the host transport rise to auto-arm SYNC=MIDI carts (MidiSync / Arduinoboy): off by
      // default, so the modes keep their manual-arm behaviour.
      { id: "lsdj-autostart", label: "Auto Start", role: "lsdj-sync", key: "autoStart", toggle: true },
    ],
  },
};

export default defineUi({ trackers: [LSDJ_TRACKER_UI] });
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The generator, its byproducts and its fixtures**

The generator reads the `ui` member (`entryFile`, so a missing module is refused by name), counts it in
`contributes()` (so an unlisted contributor is refused), and writes `ui/generated/menus.ts` in product order with the
load-time refusals: a row id used twice in a placement (a tracker's extras count as `instance.tracker:<id>`), a
builder at a placement `PLACEMENTS` does not list, a row or a `when.key` over a role key no registered schema
declares, a `TrackerUi.id` no integration has or two packages contribute, and a `UiService.id` declared twice. The
file is gitignored and a `retroplug-ts-packages` byproduct. The fixtures are the generator's: `alpha` gains a
`ts/ui.ts` module and the member, `fixtures/expected/menus.ts` is the emitted text, and six new cases cover the
module, the product order, the duplicate row, the unknown placement, the undeclared role and the missing module.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/packages/fixtures/expected/menus.ts`:

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the
// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.
//
// The product's UI contributions, in product order: each package's `retroplug.ui` module, which default-exports the
// system-settings rows, menu builders, tracker specs and services it adds. The shell composes the menus from this
// list, so a package's place in `retroplug.products.desktop` is where its rows and entries land. Only ui/ imports
// this module: the control plane, the render worker, the SDK and the planner carry no menu contribution.
import { PLACEMENTS, type RoleRow, type UiContribution } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import ui_alpha from "@retroplug/alpha/ui";
import { ROLES, TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS } from "../../src/generated/packages";

/** Each package's UI contribution, in product order. */
export const UI_CONTRIBUTIONS: readonly { pkg: string; ui: UiContribution }[] = [
  { pkg: "alpha", ui: ui_alpha },
];

// A row's id has to be unique inside its placement: the menu is keyed by id, so a second row of one id would
// take the first one's place (a system-settings row lands in the System submenu, a tracker's extras in its own
// submenu).
const rowOwners = new Map<string, string>();
function claimRow(placement: string, id: string, pkg: string): void {
  const owner = rowOwners.get(`${placement}:${id}`);
  if (owner === undefined) {
    rowOwners.set(`${placement}:${id}`, pkg);
    return;
  }
  throw new Error(owner === pkg
    ? `the package ${pkg} declares the row ${id} twice in the placement ${placement}`
    : `two packages declare the row ${id} in the placement ${placement}: ${owner} and ${pkg}`);
}

const roleKinds = new Set(ROLES.map((role) => role.kind));
/** The keys a role's schema declares, which are the only ones a row can read (or gate on). */
const roleKeys = new Map(ROLES.map((role) => [role.kind, new Set(Object.keys(role.schema.parse({})))]));
const trackerIds = new Set(TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS.map((integration) => integration.id));
const trackerOwners = new Map<string, string>();
// A service is looked up by its id: two of one id would run one of them twice or the other never, so a
// duplicate is refused rather than let the second definition win.
const serviceOwners = new Map<string, string>();
const placements = new Set<string>(PLACEMENTS);

/** One contributed row: its role must be registered, its id unique in its placement, and its key (and its
 *  gate's key) one its role's schema reads. */
function checkRow(placement: string, pkg: string, row: RoleRow): void {
  if (!roleKinds.has(row.role)) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the row ${row.id} over the role ${row.role}, which no ` +
      "registered role type has");
  }
  claimRow(placement, row.id, pkg);
  const keys = roleKeys.get(row.role)!;
  if (!keys.has(row.key)) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the row ${row.id} over the key ${row.key}, which the role ` +
      `${row.role} does not read`);
  }
  if (row.when && !keys.has(row.when.key)) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the row ${row.id} gated on the key ${row.when.key}, which ` +
      `the role ${row.role} does not read`);
  }
}

for (const { pkg, ui } of UI_CONTRIBUTIONS) {
  for (const row of ui.rows ?? []) checkRow("system.settings", pkg, row);
  for (const tracker of ui.trackers ?? []) {
    if (!trackerIds.has(tracker.id)) {
      throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares a tracker UI for ${tracker.id}, which no registered ` +
        "tracker integration has");
    }
    const owner = trackerOwners.get(tracker.id);
    if (owner !== undefined) {
      throw new Error(owner === pkg
        ? `the package ${pkg} declares the tracker UI ${tracker.id} twice`
        : `two packages declare a tracker UI for ${tracker.id}: ${owner} and ${pkg}`);
    }
    trackerOwners.set(tracker.id, pkg);
    for (const row of tracker.extras?.rows ?? []) checkRow(`instance.tracker:${tracker.id}`, pkg, row);
  }
  for (const service of ui.services ?? []) {
    const owner = serviceOwners.get(service.id);
    if (owner !== undefined) {
      throw new Error(owner === pkg
        ? `the package ${pkg} declares the UI service ${service.id} twice`
        : `two packages declare a UI service ${service.id}: ${owner} and ${pkg}`);
    }
    serviceOwners.set(service.id, pkg);
  }
  for (const menu of ui.menus ?? []) {
    if (!placements.has(menu.placement)) {
      throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares a menu builder at the placement ${menu.placement}, ` +
        `which is no placement (the placements are ${PLACEMENTS.join(", ")})`);
    }
  }
}
````

+      writeTree(
+        "packages/alpha/ts/ui.ts",
+        'export default { services: [{ id: "alpha-watch" }, { id: "alpha-watch" }] };\n',
+      );
+      writeTree("packages/alpha/ts/app.ts", uiApp("alpha"));
+      generate({ root });
+      try {
+        result = { packages: await loadMenus() };
+      } catch (e) {
+        result = { error: e.message };
+      }
+      break;
+    case "ui-missing-module": {
+      editManifest("alpha", (m) => {
+        m.retroplug.ui = "ts/nothing.ts";
+      });
+      result = refusal();
+      break;
+    }
     case "order":
       // beta depends on alpha, and the list puts beta first: the order is the list's, so this is refused rather than
       // re-sorted.
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The shell: one reader of the generated list, and the row renderer**

`ui/host/menuContributions.ts` is the one module `ui/` has that reads `ui/generated/menus.ts`
(`menuPlacement(placement, host, sys, ctx)`, `contributedTrackerUi(id)`, `uiServices()`), and the two menu composers
read it. `ui/screens/menu/configRows.ts` turns a row into a `cycler` (`configRowCycler`, shared with the
controller-app rows) and filters rows by the role the system has, then by `platforms` and `when`, emitting a
`separatorBefore` once before the first visible carrier. `systemChildren` pushes the contributed rows where the two
hand-written blocks were, and `ui/host/render.ts`'s `validSplits` and `validAudioRoutings` read
`consoleOfPlatform(platform).splits`.

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/host/menuContributions.ts`:

````ts
// The product's UI contributions (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.2), for the shell's menu composers:
// the generated list, in product order, is the one place a package's rows, builders, tracker specs and services are
// read from. Only ui/ imports it, so the control plane, the render worker, the SDK and the planner carry no menu
// contribution; the generated module has already refused a duplicate row id, an unknown placement, a row over a role
// kind no registered type declares or over a key its schema does not read, and a tracker UI no integration matches, so
// what this module reads it can index.
import type { RoleRow, TrackerUi } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { UI_CONTRIBUTIONS } from "../generated/menus";

/** Every contributed role row, in product order: the System submenu's package-owned block. */
export function roleRows(): readonly RoleRow[] {
  return UI_CONTRIBUTIONS.flatMap((entry) => entry.ui.rows ?? []);
}

/** The tracker UI a cart contributes, by its integration id, or undefined for a cart with no contributed specs. */
export function contributedTrackerUi(id: string): TrackerUi | undefined {
  for (const entry of UI_CONTRIBUTIONS) {
    for (const tracker of entry.ui.trackers ?? []) {
      if (tracker.id === id) return tracker;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/screens/menu/configRows.ts`:

````ts
// A config row as a menu cycler (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.3): one place turns a row
// into the row the menu draws, shared by a console's role rows and a controller app's knobs, so both read a stored
// value through the same fallbacks and step through the same label list. A row is data a package declares; what a step
// DOES is the caller's, because that is the one part only a surface knows (systems.setRoleConfig, a project's
// controller).
import { hasRole, roleConfig, type RoleInstance, type RoleType } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { ConfigRow, RoleRow } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { readConfigRow, rowShownFor, rowShownOn } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { cycler, separator, type MenuItem } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";

/** One config row as the menu draws it. The value a row reads is the stored one when its type matches the schema's
 *  default, else the default (`readConfigRow`, core's rule), so a role row and a controller-app row fall back alike.
 *
 *  `index` overrides where the stored value points, for the one caller whose rows predate that rule: a controller app's
 *  knobs keep the index they have always shown for a hand-edited config, so an invalid stored value reads as it did
 *  (the labels and the value a step writes are the same either way). Omitted, the typed reader's index is used. */
export function configRowCycler(
  id: string,
  row: ConfigRow,
  stored: unknown,
  fallback: unknown,
  apply: (value: string | number | boolean) => void,
  index?: number,
): MenuItem {
  const reading = readConfigRow(row, stored, fallback);
  return cycler(id, row.label, [...reading.names], index ?? reading.index, (step) => apply(reading.at(step)));
}

/** What a role-row renderer reads of a system: the platform a row may be gated on and the roles whose configs hold the
 *  values. A view of a system satisfies it. */
export interface RoleRowSystem {
  readonly platform: string;
  readonly roles: readonly RoleInstance[];
}

/** The items a set of contributed rows builds for a system, in the rows' order: a row shows only on a system that has
 *  its role (the core role attaches to every system of that core, so this is the old `core === "sameboy"` gate), where
 *  its platform and `when` gates allow, and a `separatorBefore` id is emitted once, before the first row that shows
 *  carrying it. A row's default is its role schema's (`schema.parse({})[key]`), which is what makes an untouched config
 *  read as the value the core really runs. */
export function roleRowItems(
  rows: readonly RoleRow[],
  sys: RoleRowSystem,
  roleType: (kind: string) => RoleType | undefined,
  apply: (role: string, key: string, value: string | number | boolean) => void,
): MenuItem[] {
  const items: MenuItem[] = [];
  const emitted = new Set<string>();
  const defaultsOf = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>();
  for (const row of rows) {
    if (!hasRole(sys.roles, row.role)) continue;
    if (!rowShownOn(row, sys.platform)) continue;
    let defaults = defaultsOf.get(row.role);
    if (!defaults) {
      defaults = (roleType(row.role)?.schema.parse({}) ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
      defaultsOf.set(row.role, defaults);
    }
    const config = roleConfig(sys.roles, row.role) ?? {};
    if (row.when && !rowShownFor(row, config[row.when.key], defaults[row.when.key])) continue;
    if (row.separatorBefore && !emitted.has(row.separatorBefore)) {
      emitted.add(row.separatorBefore);
      items.push(separator(row.separatorBefore));
    }
    items.push(
      configRowCycler(row.id, row, config[row.key], defaults[row.key], (value) => apply(row.role, row.key, value)),
    );
  }
  return items;
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/menu/row-carriers.test.ts`:

````ts
// A contributed row's separator (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.5, item 6): `separatorBefore` is an
// id a set of rows share so the fence appears before whichever of them shows first, ONCE. The recorded menus pin the
// case where one carrier shows (the display split's palette group beside the colour group), so the emitted-once rule is
// held here with two carriers visible at the same time - a second separator would draw a gap in the middle of a block
// that has one fence, and no shipped console produces that arrangement today.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { roleRowItems } from "../../ui/screens/menu/configRows";
import type { RoleType } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { RoleRow } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";

/** A role whose schema declares the two keys the rows below read, which is all a row's fallback needs. */
const roleType = (kind: string): RoleType | undefined =>
  kind === "test-role"
    ? ({
        kind,
        schema: { parse: (v: Record<string, unknown>) => ({ a: "x", b: "y", ...v }) },
      } as unknown as RoleType)
    : undefined;

const SYSTEM = { platform: "gb", roles: [{ kind: "test-role", config: {} }] };

const ROW_A: RoleRow = {
  id: "row-a",
  label: "A",
  role: "test-role",
  key: "a",
  choices: [
    { value: "x", label: "X" },
    { value: "y", label: "Y" },
  ],
  separatorBefore: "group-sep",
};
const ROW_B: RoleRow = { ...ROW_A, id: "row-b", key: "b" };

const apply = (): void => {};

test("two visible carriers of one separatorBefore id emit it once, before the first", () => {
  const items = roleRowItems([ROW_A, ROW_B], SYSTEM, roleType, apply);
  expect(items.map((i) => i.id)).toEqual(["group-sep", "row-a", "row-b"]);
  expect(items[0].kind).toBe("separator");
});

test("the separator follows the first carrier that SHOWS, not the first declared", () => {
  // The first carrier is gated to a platform this system is not, so the second one opens the fence instead.
  const gated: RoleRow = { ...ROW_A, platforms: ["nes"] };
  const items = roleRowItems([gated, ROW_B], SYSTEM, roleType, apply);
  expect(items.map((i) => i.id)).toEqual(["group-sep", "row-b"]);
});

test("with every carrier hidden, no separator is emitted", () => {
  // Both carriers are gated the same way: with neither visible there is no separator at all, and the block that owns
  // them draws nothing rather than a stray line.
  const nesOnly: RoleRow = { ...ROW_A, platforms: ["nes"] };
  const nesOnlyB: RoleRow = { ...ROW_B, platforms: ["nes"] };
  expect(roleRowItems([nesOnly, nesOnlyB], SYSTEM, roleType, apply)).toEqual([]);
});
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

### Task 3: the tracker entries contribute their own menus

Design sections 4.4, 4.2's tracker specs, 6 (E5, E8) and 8's third stage. `TRACKER_UI` goes: each cart contributes a
`TrackerUi` (its sync rows, its Songs spec, its Assets spec and its builder) from its package's `ts/ui/`, and the generic
machinery that stays in the shell (`songMenu`, `loadGuard`, `assetMenu`, `romPatchRows`, the bakes, the shell's own rows)
reaches it through `contributedTrackerUi(id)`. The cart callbacks take `(host, sys, ...)` over the host groups each uses,
so a callback cannot reach a group its surface lacks.

Two shared pieces move with them: the `.rit` actions to `tracker` (BlipToaster does not depend on risa, and the design's
"because BlipToaster already depends on it" was wrong) and the pure path and save helpers to `@retroplug/core/path`, with
`src/pathUtil.ts` and `src/savPaths.ts` left as re-export shims so the shell's importers are untouched. The two
`cartFor` rules the design's rows relied on are pinned by the matrix: BlipToaster stages its SysEx at its OWN system's
cart, and the Link Group row reads a number or Off.

**Files:**

- Create (5): `packages/bliptoaster/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/core/ts/path.ts`, `packages/risa/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/smsggdj/ts/ui/index.ts`, `packages/tracker/ts/ritAssetOps.ts`
- Modify (19 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 2 under `packages/retroplug/src/`; 1 under `packages/bliptoaster/`; 1 under `packages/bliptoaster/ts/`; 1 under `packages/core/`; 1 under `packages/lsdj/ts/ui/`; 1 under `packages/retroplug/scripts/` and the rest)

`@retroplug/ui/menu` gains `browseThen` (the picker-then-act helper `menuDefs` had, taking `{ dialogs: DialogsHost }`
so a cart passes its host), and `contribution.ts` gains the tracker specs and the build context they take:
`SongMenuSpec` and `AssetMenuSpec` as types, `AssetMenuSpec.selectedSlot` and `selectSlot` taking the
`MenuBuildContext` (so a selectable-slot read hits the shell's ROM cache instead of the disk per row), `TrackerUi`
with its optional `asset`, and `extras.build`.

+  const ov = lsdjOverrides(sys).find((o) => o.type === kind && o.slot === slot);

+  browseThen(host, { title: `Export ${kind} ${slot}`, patterns: type.patterns, saving: true, defaultName }, (path) => {

+    // a kit/font copies its linked file); otherwise read it from the base ROM.

+    if (!rom) return;

+    let entry: LsdjAssetOverride;

+    } catch {

+    host.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "lsdj-assets", { overrides });
