````ts
// risa's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.4): its Songs and Assets specs,
// with the file-dialog actions that own its formats - a `.risong` is the raw self-describing song record (the `.lsdsng`
// analog), and its assets are the shared `.rit` / `.chr` / `.rkit` formats, whose actions are the tracker package's
// because BlipToaster carries the very same surface. The callbacks reach the shell through the UI host's groups only.
import type { FileBrowserOpts, Host, SystemInfo } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import { SAV_PATTERNS, isSavPath, sanitizeName } from "@retroplug/core/path";
import { browseThen } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import {
  defineUi,
  type AssetMenuSpec,
  type SongMenuSpec,
  type TrackerUi,
} from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { exportRitAsset, replaceRitAsset, type RitAssetOps } from "@retroplug/tracker/ritAssetOps";
import { risaAssetCatalog } from "../risaAssetCatalog";
import { risaSongCatalog } from "../risaSongCatalog";
import { RisaRom } from "../rom";
import {
  addSongRecordToSav,
  canSaveWorkingToCatalog,
  replaceSongRecordInSav,
  saveWorkingToCatalog,
  songRecordBytes,
  workingSongRecord,
} from "../risaSongOps";

/** The host groups this cart's rows reach: narrowed to what they use, so a third-party pack copied
 *  from this one takes exactly these and nothing more. */
type RisaUiHost = Host<"files" | "systems" | "liveSongs" | "dialogs">;

/** The facet risa supplies to the shared `.rit` actions: the role kind its override list lives on, and its ROM view. */
const risaOps: RitAssetOps = {
  role: "risa-assets",
  openRom: (host: Host<"files">, romPath: string) => {
    const bytes = romPath ? host.files.readFile(romPath) : null;
    if (!bytes) return null;
    const rom = RisaRom.fromBytes(bytes);
    return rom.isRisa ? rom : null;
  },
};

const risaAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = {
  id: "risa",
  catalog: risaAssetCatalog,
  exportAsset: (host, sys, type, slot, label) => exportRitAsset(risaOps, host, sys, type, slot, label),
  replaceAsset: (host, sys, type, slot) => replaceRitAsset(risaOps, host, sys, type, slot),
};

// The throw->null wrapper for risa's catalog ops used by its file actions (LSDj's ops return null directly; risa's
// byte-ops throw on a bad index / no space).
function tryOp(fn: () => Uint8Array): Uint8Array | null {
  try {
    return fn();
  } catch {
    return null; // out of range / malformed -> leave the sav untouched
  }
}

// risa song file I/O: a `.risong` is the raw self-describing song record - the `.lsdsng` analog (song only, no kits).
// Export writes songRecordBytes; Replace/Add inject the record via the byte-level catalog ops.
function exportSong(host: RisaUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number, name: string): void {
  const opts: FileBrowserOpts = {
    title: `Export song ${index}`,
    patterns: ["*.risong"],
    saving: true,
    defaultName: `${sanitizeName(name)}.risong`,
  };
  browseThen(host, opts, (path) => {
    const bytes = host.systems.readSram(sys.id);
    if (!bytes) return;
    const record = songRecordBytes(bytes, index);
    if (record) host.files.writeFileAtomic(path, record);
  });
}

function replaceSong(host: RisaUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number): void {
  browseThen(host, { title: `Replace song ${index}`, patterns: ["*.risong"] }, (path) => {
    const data = host.files.readFile(path);
    if (!data) return;
    host.liveSongs.mutate(sys, (sav) => tryOp(() => replaceSongRecordInSav(sav, index, data)));
  });
}

function addSong(host: RisaUiHost, sys: SystemInfo): void {
  browseThen(host, { title: "Add Song", patterns: ["*.risong", ...SAV_PATTERNS] }, (path) => {
    const data = host.files.readFile(path);
    if (!data) return;
    if (isSavPath(path)) host.liveSongs.beginImport(sys, data); // a whole .sav/.srm -> the checkbox picker
    else host.liveSongs.mutate(sys, (sav) => tryOp(() => addSongRecordToSav(sav, data))); // a single .risong record
  });
}

// The synthetic working-song row's actions. Export writes the LIVE working song (banks 0-3, encoded as a
// record) to a `.risong`; Save to Catalog promotes it into a new saved slot + links it, so it stops being
// unsaved and moves into the numbered list.
function exportWorking(host: RisaUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, name: string): void {
  const opts: FileBrowserOpts = {
    title: "Export working song",
    patterns: ["*.risong"],
    saving: true,
    defaultName: `${sanitizeName(name)}.risong`,
  };
  browseThen(host, opts, (path) => {
    const bytes = host.systems.readSram(sys.id);
    if (!bytes) return;
    const record = workingSongRecord(bytes);
    if (record) host.files.writeFileAtomic(path, record);
  });
}

function saveWorking(host: RisaUiHost, sys: SystemInfo): void {
  host.liveSongs.mutate(sys, (sav) => tryOp(() => saveWorkingToCatalog(sav)));
}

// risa's working song carries its own name, so it never needs one asked for - `workingNeedsName` is simply
// absent (false) and the menu offers a plain "Save Working Song & Load".
const risaCommitWorking = (sav: Uint8Array): Uint8Array | null => tryOp(() => saveWorkingToCatalog(sav));

const risaSongSpec: SongMenuSpec = {
  id: "risa",
  catalog: risaSongCatalog,
  exportSong,
  replaceSong,
  addSong,
  exportWorking,
  saveWorkingToCatalog: saveWorking,
  commitWorking: risaCommitWorking,
  canCommitWorking: canSaveWorkingToCatalog,
};

/** The tracker's UI: its Songs and Assets specs. It builds no fragment of its own. */
export const RISA_TRACKER_UI: TrackerUi = {
  id: "risa",
  song: risaSongSpec,
  asset: risaAssetSpec,
};

export default defineUi({ trackers: [RISA_TRACKER_UI] });
````

````ts
// smsggdj's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.4): its Songs spec, with the
// `.smdj4` file actions (a 16-byte header - magic, block checksum, the echo settings that live in the DIRECTORY entry
// rather than the song - followed by the verbatim 6,912-byte block, uncompressed on purpose). Its asset catalog is
// empty, so the shared asset menus render nothing; the spec is still contributed so the ROM-scoped bake rows keep their
// place, exactly as the hand-built table had it.
import type { FileBrowserOpts, Host, SystemInfo } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import { SAV_PATTERNS, isSavPath, sanitizeName } from "@retroplug/core/path";
import { browseThen } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import {
  defineUi,
  type AssetMenuSpec,
  type SongMenuSpec,
  type TrackerUi,
} from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { smsggdjAssetCatalog } from "../smsggdjAssetCatalog";
import { smsggdjSongCatalog } from "../smsggdjSongCatalog";
import {
  addSong,
  readSongBlock,
  readSongEcho,
  replaceSong as replaceSmdjSong,
  unwrapSong,
  wrapSong,
} from "../codec/sav";

/** The host groups this cart's rows reach: narrowed to what they use, so a third-party pack copied
 *  from this one takes exactly these and nothing more. */
type SmsggdjUiHost = Host<"files" | "systems" | "liveSongs" | "dialogs">;

function exportSong(host: SmsggdjUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number, name: string): void {
  const opts: FileBrowserOpts = {
    title: `Export song ${index}`,
    patterns: ["*.smdj4"],
    saving: true,
    defaultName: `${sanitizeName(name)}.smdj4`,
  };
  browseThen(host, opts, (path) => {
    const sav = host.systems.readSram(sys.id);
    if (!sav) return;
    const block = readSongBlock(sav, index);
    if (!block) return; // free slot / failed its checksum: nothing honest to write
    const file = wrapSong(block, readSongEcho(sav, index) ?? undefined);
    if (file) host.files.writeFileAtomic(path, file);
  });
}

function replaceSong(host: SmsggdjUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, index: number): void {
  browseThen(host, { title: `Replace song ${index}`, patterns: ["*.smdj4"] }, (path) => {
    const data = host.files.readFile(path);
    if (!data) return;
    const song = unwrapSong(data); // rejects a wrong magic / length / checksum rather than importing junk
    if (!song) return;
    host.liveSongs.mutate(sys, (sav) => replaceSmdjSong(sav, index, song.block, song.echo));
  });
}

function addSongFromDisk(host: SmsggdjUiHost, sys: SystemInfo): void {
  browseThen(host, { title: "Add Song", patterns: ["*.smdj4", ...SAV_PATTERNS] }, (path) => {
    const data = host.files.readFile(path);
    if (!data) return;
    if (isSavPath(path)) {
      host.liveSongs.beginImport(sys, data); // a whole .sav/.srm -> the checkbox picker
      return;
    }
    const song = unwrapSong(data);
    if (!song) return;
    const name = path.replace(/^.*[\\/]/, "").replace(/\.smdj4$/i, "").slice(0, 8).toUpperCase();
    host.liveSongs.mutate(sys, (sav) => addSong(sav, song.block, name));
  });
}

const smsggdjSongSpec: SongMenuSpec = {
  id: "smsggdj",
  catalog: smsggdjSongCatalog,
  exportSong,
  replaceSong,
  addSong: addSongFromDisk,
  // No working-song rows: this cart's working song is work RAM, so the catalog reports no unsaved
  // working song to export or promote. See smsggdjSongCatalog.
};

/** `types: []`, so the shared asset menus render nothing and neither action is reachable. */
const smsggdjAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = {
  id: "smsggdj",
  catalog: smsggdjAssetCatalog,
  exportAsset: () => {},
  replaceAsset: () => {},
};

/** The tracker's UI: its Songs spec, and the empty asset spec the bake rows are built over. */
export const SMSGGDJ_TRACKER_UI: TrackerUi = {
  id: "smsggdj",
  song: smsggdjSongSpec,
  asset: smsggdjAssetSpec,
};

export default defineUi({ trackers: [SMSGGDJ_TRACKER_UI] });
````

````ts
// BlipToaster's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.2 and 4.4): its asset spec and the
// settings rows it builds. It is ASSET-ONLY (no song battery), and its assets are the shared `.rit` / `.chr` / `.rkit`
// formats - risa's surface exactly, which is why the actions are the tracker package's.
//
// THEME and FONT have no row of their own: the cart's baked settings block names one of each as the live one, so their
// lists ARE the picker (a `*` on the live slot, `Select` on every other - see selectedSlot/selectSlot below). The DMC
// kit has none either: ch5 CC 14 picks it, which a song does before it plays anything.
//
// The cart has no settings memory - no battery, and nothing survives a RESET on purpose - so what you would set once
// for your rig is baked into the `.nes`: a 16-byte block in its code bank (@retroplug/bliptoaster/rom/settings).
// These rows edit it exactly the way the asset rows edit assets: the pick is persisted on the `bliptoaster-assets` role
// and folded into the ROM IN MEMORY at construct, and the file on disk is untouched. Every row also tells the running
// cart over SysEx, so it takes effect now; the pin is what a later LOAD replays and what a bake writes.
import type { Host, SystemInfo } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import { roleConfig } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { action, cycler, separator, type MenuItem } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import {
  defineUi,
  type AssetMenuSpec,
  type MenuBuildContext,
  type TrackerUi,
} from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { exportRitAsset, replaceRitAsset, type RitAssetOps } from "@retroplug/tracker/ritAssetOps";
import { bliptoasterAssetCatalog } from "../bliptoasterAssetCatalog";
import { readSettings as readPinnedSettings } from "../bliptoasterAssetsRole";
import {
  BlipToasterRom,
  blipToasterSettingsSysex,
  type BlipToasterSettings,
  type BlipToasterSettingsPatch,
} from "../rom";

/** The host groups this cart's rows reach: narrowed to what they use, so a third-party pack copied
 *  from this one takes exactly these and nothing more. */
type BlipToasterUiHost = Host<"files" | "dialogs" | "systems">;

/** The baked-settings fields this PROJECT pins (not the ROM's own bytes) - only what the user has changed. */
const pinnedSettings = (sys: SystemInfo): BlipToasterSettingsPatch =>
  readPinnedSettings(roleConfig(sys.roles, "bliptoaster-assets"));

/** The cart's baked block with the project's pins on top - what it is set to right now. Null when the ROM has no
 *  readable block (one predating it, or a format this build does not read). */
function effectiveSettings(romBytes: Uint8Array | null, sys: SystemInfo): BlipToasterSettings | null {
  if (!romBytes) return null;
  const rom = BlipToasterRom.fromBytes(romBytes);
  if (!rom.isBlipToaster || !rom.hasSettings) return null;
  return { ...rom.settings()!, ...pinnedSettings(sys) };
}

/** Pin `patch` on the role AND declare the resulting rig to the RUNNING cart. Both halves matter and neither is
 *  redundant: the pin is what a load replays and a bake writes, the SysEx is what the cart in front of you hears.
 *  `romBytes` is the base ROM the build context cached, so a step over the settings rows costs no extra read.
 *
 *  The message is staged at this system's node, so it reaches THIS cart whatever the project's MUSICAL routing is
 *  doing, and at its rp.n8.nes too when the document places one FOR THIS SYSTEM (the real console, in the block the
 *  emulated core hears it). Every NES drives a real cart by default, so in a project with more than one the placed cart
 *  node belongs to the FIRST in slot order: staging there for another system's cart would send this cart's rig to a
 *  console running a different ROM. */
function pinSettings(
  host: BlipToasterUiHost,
  sys: SystemInfo,
  romBytes: Uint8Array | null,
  patch: BlipToasterSettingsPatch,
): void {
  const effective = effectiveSettings(romBytes, sys);
  if (!effective) return;
  const next = { ...pinnedSettings(sys), ...patch };
  host.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "bliptoaster-assets", { settings: next });
  const sysex = blipToasterSettingsSysex({ ...effective, ...patch });
  host.systems.stageNodeMidi(host.systems.nodeIdOf(sys.id), sysex);
  const cart = host.systems.drivenCart();
  if (cart !== null && cart.id === sys.id) host.systems.stageNodeMidi(cart.nodeId, sysex);
}

/** The cart's settings block names one THEME and one FONT as the live ones, so for those two the asset list is also the
 *  picker: the row that IS live wears a `*`, every other row offers `Select`. That replaces a pair of cyclers at the
 *  menu's root which named a slot by number, in a different place from the list of slots. */
const SELECTABLE: Record<string, "theme" | "font" | undefined> = { theme: "theme", font: "font" };

/** The facet BlipToaster supplies to the shared `.rit` actions: the role kind its override list lives on, and its
 *  ROM. */
const blipToasterOps: RitAssetOps = {
  role: "bliptoaster-assets",
  openRom: (host: Host<"files">, romPath: string) => {
    const bytes = romPath ? host.files.readFile(romPath) : null;
    if (!bytes) return null;
    const rom = BlipToasterRom.fromBytes(bytes);
    return rom.isBlipToaster ? rom : null;
  },
};

const blipToasterAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = {
  id: "bliptoaster",
  catalog: bliptoasterAssetCatalog,
  exportAsset: (host, sys, type, slot, label) => exportRitAsset(blipToasterOps, host, sys, type, slot, label),
  replaceAsset: (host, sys, type, slot) => replaceRitAsset(blipToasterOps, host, sys, type, slot),
  selectedSlot(_host, sys, kind, ctx) {
    const field = SELECTABLE[kind];
    if (!field) return null; // kits have no live slot: ch5 CC 14 picks one, and nothing is baked
    const settings = effectiveSettings(ctx.assetRom(sys.romPath), sys);
    return settings ? settings[field] : null;
  },
  selectSlot(host, sys, kind, slot, ctx) {
    const field = SELECTABLE[kind];
    if (field) pinSettings(host, sys, ctx.assetRom(sys.romPath), { [field]: slot });
  },
};

/** The cart's baked rig defaults, as the rows at the top of its instance submenu. Empty when the ROM has no readable
 *  settings block. */
function settingsRows(host: BlipToasterUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, ctx: MenuBuildContext): MenuItem[] {
  const romBytes = ctx.assetRom(sys.romPath);
  const effective = effectiveSettings(romBytes, sys);
  if (!effective) return [];
  const pinned = pinnedSettings(sys);
  const pin = (patch: BlipToasterSettingsPatch): void => pinSettings(host, sys, romBytes, patch);
  const baseChannelNames = Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_v, i) => String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0"));

  return [
    cycler("bliptoaster-set-basech", "Base MIDI Channel", baseChannelNames, effective.baseChannel, (n) =>
      pin({ baseChannel: n }),
    ),
    cycler("bliptoaster-set-ppu", "PPU Enabled", ["Off", "On"], effective.ppu ? 1 : 0, (n) => pin({ ppu: n === 1 })),
    // "not on the VRC7 build" is the ROM's own behaviour (it has no velocity curve), not something to hide here:
    // the byte is still baked and still honoured by every other build of the same project's ROM.
    cycler("bliptoaster-set-curve", "Velocity Curve", ["Linear", "Log"], effective.velCurve ? 1 : 0, (n) =>
      pin({ velCurve: n === 1 }),
    ),
    // Reset is the one row left. There is no "Apply" any more: every row above already reached the cart over SysEx as
    // it was stepped, so there was nothing left for a reboot to do that the row had not done. Reset still reboots,
    // because dropping the pins means going back to the ROM's OWN bytes, which are only read at boot. Offered only once
    // something IS pinned - with nothing pinned the rows show the ROM's bytes already.
    ...(Object.keys(pinned).length
      ? [
          separator("bliptoaster-set-apply-sep"),
          action("bliptoaster-set-reset", "Reset to ROM Defaults", () => {
            host.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "bliptoaster-assets", { settings: {} });
            host.systems.reload(sys.id);
          }),
        ]
      : []),
  ];
}

/** The settings rows sit at the TOP of the BlipToaster menu, above the asset submenus and fenced off from them (they
 *  are what the cart BOOTS with, the asset menus are what it boots FROM). Inline rather than behind a "Settings"
 *  submenu of their own: there are only a handful, and one of the two things you come to this menu to do should not
 *  cost a level. */
function settingsBuild(host: BlipToasterUiHost, sys: SystemInfo, ctx: MenuBuildContext): MenuItem[] {
  const rows = settingsRows(host, sys, ctx);
  return rows.length === 0 ? [] : [...rows, separator("bliptoaster-settings-sep")];
}

/** The tracker's UI: its asset spec, and the settings rows it builds at the top of its submenu. */
export const BLIPTOASTER_TRACKER_UI: TrackerUi = {
  id: "bliptoaster",
  asset: blipToasterAssetSpec,
  extras: { build: settingsBuild },
};

export default defineUi({ trackers: [BLIPTOASTER_TRACKER_UI] });
````

Create `packages/core/ts/path.ts`:

````ts
// The std::filesystem::path member operations RetroPlug's native path code relies on, as pure TS string ops
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.4, decision 10): the shell, a cart's menu callbacks and the shared
// tracker asset code all derive the same `<rom>.sav` / `<asset>.kit` names, so the functions live in the contract
// package every one of them depends on. The shell's src/pathUtil.ts and src/savPaths.ts re-export these, so there is
// one implementation. The plugin is cross-platform, so BOTH `/` and `\` count as separators (matching the mock
// canonicalizer and packages/retroplug's missingFiles.ts), and derived paths are emitted in forward-slash form.
// Faithful to std::filesystem semantics for the cases that matter to ROM/sav/rplg derivation: no-extension,
// multi-dot names, and leading-dot ("dotfiles", which have no extension). No IO - everything here is a pure transform
// of the string.

const SEP = /[\\/]/;

/** Index of the last path separator (`/` or `\`), or -1 if none. */
function lastSep(p: string): number {
  return Math.max(p.lastIndexOf("/"), p.lastIndexOf("\\"));
}

/** Parent directory: everything before the last separator. `""` when the path has
 *  no separator; `"/"` for a root-level entry (matches path::parent_path). */
export function dirname(p: string): string {
  const i = lastSep(p);
  if (i < 0) return "";
  if (i === 0) return "/";
  return p.slice(0, i);
}

/** The last path component (path::filename). */
export function basename(p: string): string {
  const i = lastSep(p);
  return i < 0 ? p : p.slice(i + 1);
}

// The dot that begins the extension of a filename, or -1 when there is none.
// A dot at index 0 (a leading-dot "dotfile") is NOT an extension separator, so
// `.config` has an empty extension and a stem of `.config`, as in std::filesystem.
function extDot(name: string): number {
  const dot = name.lastIndexOf(".");
  return dot <= 0 ? -1 : dot;
}

/** Filename minus the final extension (path::stem). */
export function stem(p: string): string {
  const name = basename(p);
  const dot = extDot(name);
  return dot < 0 ? name : name.slice(0, dot);
}

/** The final extension, including the leading dot; `""` when there is none
 *  (path::extension). */
export function extension(p: string): string {
  const name = basename(p);
  const dot = extDot(name);
  return dot < 0 ? "" : name.slice(dot);
}

/** `extension()` lowercased: the seam native uses to compare against `.sav`. */
export function extensionLower(p: string): string {
  return extension(p).toLowerCase();
}

/** Replace the final extension (or append one when there is none). `ext` includes
 *  the dot (`".rplg"`); an empty `ext` strips the extension (path::replace_extension). */
export function replaceExtension(p: string, ext: string): string {
  const i = lastSep(p);
  const dir = i < 0 ? "" : p.slice(0, i + 1);
  const name = i < 0 ? p : p.slice(i + 1);
  const dot = extDot(name);
  const base = dot < 0 ? name : name.slice(0, dot);
  const suffix = ext === "" ? "" : ext.startsWith(".") ? ext : "." + ext;
  return dir + base + suffix;
}

/** Replace the whole last component, preserving the directory (path::replace_filename). */
export function replaceFilename(p: string, name: string): string {
  const i = lastSep(p);
  return i < 0 ? name : p.slice(0, i + 1) + name;
}

/** Join a directory and a name with a single separator (path::operator/). An empty
 *  dir yields the bare name; a dir already ending in a separator isn't doubled. */
export function joinPath(dir: string, name: string): string {
  if (!dir) return name;
  return SEP.test(dir[dir.length - 1]) ? dir + name : dir + "/" + name;
}

/** True when `p` is absolute: a leading `/` or a drive letter (path::is_absolute,
 *  cross-platform). Mirrors packages/retroplug/src/missingFiles.ts. */
export function isAbsolute(p: string): boolean {
  return /^([a-zA-Z]:[\\/]|[\\/])/.test(p);
}

/** Shorten `s` (e.g. a long directory path) to at most `maxLen` characters by eliding the middle with a
 *  single `…`, keeping the start and end, for display in the narrow menu. A no-op when it already fits.
 *  The end (the target folder) keeps the extra character on an odd budget. */
// ASCII "..." for the elision marker: the LVGL menu font has no "…" (U+2026) glyph (it renders as a tofu
// box), and ".." would read as the parent-directory token inside a path.
const ELLIPSIS = "...";
export function shortenMiddle(s: string, maxLen: number): string {
  if (s.length <= maxLen) return s;
  if (maxLen <= ELLIPSIS.length) return s.slice(0, Math.max(0, maxLen)); // no room for head+tail: hard-truncate
  const budget = maxLen - ELLIPSIS.length;
  const tail = Math.ceil(budget / 2);
  const head = budget - tail;
  return s.slice(0, head) + ELLIPSIS + (tail > 0 ? s.slice(s.length - tail) : "");
}

/** The first of `base`, `base_2`, `base_3`, … for which `isTaken` returns false: the "If Exists: Rename"
 *  render policy. `isTaken(candidate)` reports whether an output for that base already exists (the caller
 *  checks `<base>.wav`, or the split's `<base>_<channel>.wav` files). Pure: the caller owns the fs check. */
export function uniqueBase(base: string, isTaken: (candidate: string) => boolean): string {
  if (!isTaken(base)) return base;
  for (let n = 2; ; n++) {
    const candidate = `${base}_${n}`;
    if (!isTaken(candidate)) return candidate;
  }
}

/** Battery-save file extensions, most-preferred first. `.sav` is the default write target across
 *  GB/NES/GBA; `.srm` is the alternative some NES/risa saves ship with, so it's accepted when pairing a
 *  ROM to its battery and when loading SRAM (but new saves are still written as `.sav`). */
export const SAV_EXTS = [".sav", ".srm"] as const;

/** File-dialog globs for a battery save (`.sav` / `.srm`). */
export const SAV_PATTERNS: string[] = SAV_EXTS.map((ext) => `*${ext}`);

/** True when `path`'s extension is a recognised battery-save extension (`.sav` / `.srm`). */
export function isSavPath(path: string): boolean {
  return (SAV_EXTS as readonly string[]).includes(extensionLower(path));
}

/** A safe filename fragment for a derived export name: an asset's own label, a song's name, a ROM's stem. Every
 *  character outside the set a filesystem (and the carts' own name fields) accepts becomes `_`, and an empty result
 *  becomes "asset" rather than no name at all. */
export const sanitizeName = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, "_") || "asset";
````

Create `packages/tracker/ts/ritAssetOps.ts`:

````ts
// The shared `.rit` asset menu actions (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.4): risa and BlipToaster carry
// the SAME asset surface - a theme table, 8 KB CHR font banks and 8 KB DMC kit banks - down to the file formats
// (.rit / .chr / .rkit), the validation constants and the inline-vs-by-path split. Their two Export/Replace pairs were
// four functions that differed only in which class parsed the ROM and which role kind the override was written to, so
// those are the two things a cart supplies through `RitAssetOps`.
//
// It lives here rather than in risa because BlipToaster does not depend on risa (risa's own rom/index.ts says so), and
// the code needs no menu type: it takes the host's file I/O, its dialog and its role edits. LSDj is deliberately NOT
// folded in: its formats differ, and it validates by trial-applying to a parsed ROM rather than by length, which is a
// genuinely different shape.
import type { FileBrowserOpts, Host, SystemInfo } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import { roleConfig } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { sanitizeName, stem } from "@retroplug/core/path";
import type { AssetTypeInfo } from "./assetCatalog";
import { readRitOverrides, type RitAssetOverride } from "./ritAssets";
import { CHR_BANK_SIZE, KIT_BANK_SIZE } from "./nes/constants";
import { decodeThemeFromRom, parseRit, serializeRit } from "./nes/theme";
import { bankToModel, isBankPopulated } from "./nes/kitBank";

/** What one cart supplies to the shared actions: the role kind its override list lives on, and how to open its ROM. */
export interface RitAssetOps {
  readonly role: string;
  openRom(host: Host<"files">, romPath: string): RitAssetRomReader | null;
}

/** The slice of a parsed ROM the shared Export reads. RisaRom and BlipToasterRom both satisfy it as written. */
export interface RitAssetRomReader {
  getTheme(slot: number): { recordBytes: Uint8Array; nameBytes: Uint8Array } | null;
  getKitBank(slot: number): Uint8Array | null;
  getChrFontSlot(slot: number): Uint8Array | null;
}

/** An override's linked bank, or null when the link is broken. A `.rkit` / `.chr` override records a PATH, and the user
 *  is free to move or delete that file afterwards - at which point Export used to produce nothing at all, silently,
 *  because a null read fell through the `if (bytes && bytes.length)` guard with no message. Returning null here lets
 *  the caller fall back to the base ROM's own bank, which is both useful (that is the asset the cart will actually boot
 *  with once the dead override is removed) and what the LSDj copy of these actions has always done. */
const readLinked = (host: Host<"files">, path: string | undefined): Uint8Array | null =>
  path ? host.files.readFile(path) : null;

const ritOverrides = (sys: SystemInfo, role: string): RitAssetOverride[] =>
  readRitOverrides(roleConfig(sys.roles, role));

/** Open the host's file dialog and apply the pick; a cancel is ignored. A local copy of the menu layer's helper
 *  because this package is what `@retroplug/ui` itself depends on, so it may not import it. */
function pick(host: Host<"dialogs">, opts: FileBrowserOpts, apply: (path: string) => void): void {
  void host.dialogs.browse(opts).then((path) => {
    if (path) apply(path);
  });
}

/** Export theme/font/kit `slot` to a picked file: the override's data if replaced, else the base ROM's asset. */
export function exportRitAsset(
  ops: RitAssetOps,
  host: Host<"files" | "dialogs">,
  sys: SystemInfo,
  type: AssetTypeInfo,
  slot: number,
  label: string,
): void {
  const kind = type.kind;
  const ov = ritOverrides(sys, ops.role).find((o) => o.type === kind && o.slot === slot);
  const defaultName = `${sanitizeName(label)}${type.ext}`;
  pick(host, { title: `Export ${kind} ${slot}`, patterns: type.patterns, saving: true, defaultName }, (path) => {
    let bytes: Uint8Array | null = null;
    if (kind === "theme") {
      // The theme comes from the inline override, or the base ROM decoded; emit a .rit (readable JSON).
      let theme = ov?.theme ?? null;
      if (!theme) {
        const t = ops.openRom(host, sys.romPath)?.getTheme(slot);
        if (t) theme = decodeThemeFromRom(t.recordBytes, t.nameBytes);
      }
      if (theme) bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(serializeRit(theme), null, 2) + "\n");
    } else if (kind === "kit") {
      // The linked bank if overridden, else the base ROM's 8 KB DMC bank - either is a ready-to-link .rkit.
      bytes = readLinked(host, ov?.path) ?? ops.openRom(host, sys.romPath)?.getKitBank(slot) ?? null;
    } else {
      bytes = readLinked(host, ov?.path) ?? ops.openRom(host, sys.romPath)?.getChrFontSlot(slot) ?? null;
    }
    if (bytes && bytes.length) host.files.writeFileAtomic(path, bytes);
  });
}

/** Replace theme/font/kit `slot` from a picked file: validate it, record the override (theme INLINE / font + kit by
 *  PATH) in role config, and reload so it takes effect. NON-DESTRUCTIVE: the base .nes is never written. */
export function replaceRitAsset(
  ops: RitAssetOps,
  host: Host<"files" | "dialogs" | "systems">,
  sys: SystemInfo,
  type: AssetTypeInfo,
  slot: number,
): void {
  const kind = type.kind;
  pick(host, { title: `Replace ${kind} ${slot}`, patterns: type.patterns }, (path) => {
    const data = host.files.readFile(path);
    if (!data) return;
    let entry: RitAssetOverride;
    try {
      if (kind === "theme") {
        const { theme } = parseRit(JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(data))); // throws on a bad .rit
        entry = { type: "theme", slot, name: theme.name.trim() || stem(path), theme };
      } else if (kind === "kit") {
        if (data.length !== KIT_BANK_SIZE || !isBankPopulated(data)) return; // exactly one populated 8 KB DMC bank
        entry = { type: "kit", slot, name: bankToModel(data).name.trim() || stem(path), path };
      } else {
        if (data.length !== CHR_BANK_SIZE) return; // a .chr is exactly one 8 KB CHR bank
        entry = { type: "font", slot, name: stem(path), path };
      }
    } catch {
      return; // malformed .rit / unreadable -> leave the ROM untouched
    }
    const overrides = [
      ...ritOverrides(sys, ops.role).filter((o) => !(o.type === kind && o.slot === slot)),
      entry,
    ];
    host.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, ops.role, { overrides });
    host.systems.reload(sys.id);
  });
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The shell: `TRACKER_UI` gone, and the host the callbacks take**

`menuDefs.ts` keeps the generic machinery and the shell's rows, imports no tracker cart package, and reads
`contributedTrackerUi(t.id)` for the rows, the fragment, the Songs spec, the asset menus and the bake rows.
`MenuContext.host` is optional: App passes the host it built, and a context without one gets `hostOf(ctx)`, the same
host built from the context's own peers and cached per context, so a contribution always receives the full ten groups
and no menu test file changed. LSDj's builder opens the HD player through `host.views.open("lsdj-hd", sys.id)`, and
`uiHost.ts` gains `uiViews(openLsdjHd)`, the one place the interim cart id maps to today's screen (F4c removes it).

````diff
-// --- risa asset file actions (Export/Replace own the .rit/.chr/.rkit formats) -------------------------
-// THEMES are palette indices stored INLINE (readable JSON `.rit`, no file); FONTS LINK a `.chr` bank by path;
-// KITS LINK a pre-built 8 KB `.rkit` DMC bank by path (risa's Export writes one out of a ROM and the CLI's
-// build-kit compiles one; the cart's kit format can compile one in the plugin, though no row does - so a kit override just
-// splices a ready-made bank).
-
-const readRisaRomFor = (be: HostBackend, romPath: string): RisaRom | null => {
-  const bytes = romPath ? be.readFile(romPath) : null;
-  if (!bytes) return null;
-  const rom = RisaRom.fromBytes(bytes);
-  return rom.isRisa ? rom : null;
-};
-
-// risa and BlipToaster carry the SAME asset surface - a 7-role theme table, 8 KB CHR font banks and 8 KB
-// DMC kit banks - down to the file formats (.rit / .chr / .rkit), the validation constants and the
-// inline-vs-by-path split. Their two Export/Replace pairs were four functions that differed only in which
-// class parsed the ROM and which role kind the override was written to, so those are the two things a
-// console supplies here. LSDj is deliberately NOT folded in: its formats differ, and it validates by
-// trial-applying to a parsed ROM rather than by length, which is a genuinely different shape.
-interface RitAssetOps {
-  role: string;
-  openRom(be: HostBackend, romPath: string): {
-    getTheme(slot: number): { recordBytes: Uint8Array; nameBytes: Uint8Array } | null;
-    getKitBank(slot: number): Uint8Array | null;
-    getChrFontSlot(slot: number): Uint8Array | null;
-  } | null;
-}
-
-/** An override's linked bank, or null when the link is broken. A `.rkit` / `.chr` override records a PATH,
- *  and the user is free to move or delete that file afterwards — at which point Export used to produce
- *  nothing at all, silently, because a null read fell through the `if (bytes && bytes.length)` guard with no
- *  message. Returning null here lets the caller fall back to the base ROM's own bank, which is both useful
- *  (that is the asset the cart will actually boot with once the dead override is removed) and what the LSDj
- *  copy of these actions has always done. */
-const readLinked = (be: HostBackend, path: string | undefined): Uint8Array | null =>
-  path ? be.readFile(path) : null;
-
-const ritOverrides = (sys: SystemView, role: string): RisaAssetOverride[] =>
-  readRisaOverrides(roleConfig(sys.roles, role));
-
-// Export theme/font/kit `slot` to a picked file: the override's data if replaced, else the base ROM's asset.
-function exportRitAsset(
-  ops: RitAssetOps,
-  ctx: MenuContext,
-  sys: SystemView,
-  type: AssetTypeInfo,
-  slot: number,
-  label: string,
-): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  const kind = type.kind;
-  const ov = ritOverrides(sys, ops.role).find((o) => o.type === kind && o.slot === slot);
-  const defaultName = `${sanitizeName(label)}${type.ext}`;
-  browseThen(ctx, { title: `Export ${kind} ${slot}`, patterns: type.patterns, saving: true, defaultName }, (path) => {
-    let bytes: Uint8Array | null = null;
-    if (kind === "theme") {
-      // The theme comes from the inline override, or the base ROM decoded; emit a .rit (readable JSON).
-      let theme = ov?.theme ?? null;
-      if (!theme) {
-        const t = ops.openRom(be, sys.romPath)?.getTheme(slot);
-        if (t) theme = decodeThemeFromRom(t.recordBytes, t.nameBytes);
-      }
-      if (theme) bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(serializeRit(theme), null, 2) + "\n");
-    } else if (kind === "kit") {
-      // The linked bank if overridden, else the base ROM's 8 KB DMC bank — either is a ready-to-link .rkit.
-      bytes = readLinked(be, ov?.path) ?? ops.openRom(be, sys.romPath)?.getKitBank(slot) ?? null;
-    } else {
-      bytes = readLinked(be, ov?.path) ?? ops.openRom(be, sys.romPath)?.getChrFontSlot(slot) ?? null;
-    }
-    if (bytes && bytes.length) be.writeFileAtomic(path, bytes);
-  });
-}
-
-// Replace theme/font/kit `slot` from a picked file: validate it, record the override (theme INLINE / font +
-// kit by PATH) in role config, and reload so it takes effect. NON-DESTRUCTIVE — the base .nes is never written.
-function replaceRitAsset(ops: RitAssetOps, ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, type: AssetTypeInfo, slot: number): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  const kind = type.kind;
-  browseThen(ctx, { title: `Replace ${kind} ${slot}`, patterns: type.patterns }, (path) => {
-    const data = be.readFile(path);
-    if (!data) return;
-    let entry: RisaAssetOverride;
-    try {
-      if (kind === "theme") {
-        const { theme } = parseRit(JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(data))); // throws on a bad .rit
-        entry = { type: "theme", slot, name: theme.name.trim() || stem(path), theme };
-      } else if (kind === "kit") {
-        if (data.length !== KIT_BANK_SIZE || !isBankPopulated(data)) return; // a .rkit is exactly one populated 8 KB DMC bank
-        entry = { type: "kit", slot, name: bankToModel(data).name.trim() || stem(path), path };
-      } else {
-        if (data.length !== 0x2000) return; // a .chr is exactly one 8 KB CHR bank
-        entry = { type: "font", slot, name: stem(path), path };
-      }
-    } catch {
-      return; // malformed .rit / unreadable → leave the ROM untouched
-    }
-    writeOverrides(ctx, sys, ops.role, [...ritOverrides(sys, ops.role).filter((o) => !(o.type === kind && o.slot === slot)), entry]);
-  });
-}
-
-const lsdjAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = { id: "lsdj", catalog: lsdjAssetCatalog, exportAsset, replaceAsset };
-const risaAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = {
-  id: "risa",
-  catalog: risaAssetCatalog,
-  exportAsset: (ctx, sys, type, slot, label) => exportRitAsset(risaOps, ctx, sys, type, slot, label),
-  replaceAsset: (ctx, sys, type, slot) => replaceRitAsset(risaOps, ctx, sys, type, slot),
-};
-
-// --- BlipToaster asset file actions (Export/Replace own the .rkit/.chr formats) ---------------------------
-// BlipToaster's overrides: a 16-entry theme table (INLINE), plus the DMC kit and CHR font banks, both LINKED
-// by path (a pre-built 8 KB .rkit / .chr, read at construct). This comment used to say the cart had no themes
-// "yet" and that the actions mirrored risa's "minus themes"; the theme table landed and the comment did not
-// follow it, while the copy underneath grew a theme branch. The actions are now literally risa's - see
-// RitAssetOps - which is the version of "mirrors risa" that cannot drift.
-
-/** The baked-settings fields this PROJECT pins (not the ROM's own bytes) — only what the user has changed. */
-const readBlipToasterSettings = (sys: SystemView): BlipToasterSettingsPatch =>
-  readBlipToasterSettingsConfig(roleConfig(sys.roles, "bliptoaster-assets"));
-
-const readBlipToasterRomFor = (be: HostBackend, romPath: string): BlipToasterRom | null => {
-  const bytes = romPath ? be.readFile(romPath) : null;
-  if (!bytes) return null;
-  const rom = BlipToasterRom.fromBytes(bytes);
-  return rom.isBlipToaster ? rom : null;
-};
-
-const risaOps: RitAssetOps = { role: "risa-assets", openRom: readRisaRomFor };
-const blipToasterOps: RitAssetOps = { role: "bliptoaster-assets", openRom: readBlipToasterRomFor };
-
-// The cart's settings block names one THEME and one FONT as the live ones, so for those two the asset list is
-// also the picker: the row that IS live wears a `*`, every other row offers `Select`. That replaces a pair of
-// cyclers at the menu's root which named a slot by number, in a different place from the list of slots.
-const BLIPTOASTER_SELECTABLE: Record<string, "theme" | "font" | undefined> = { theme: "theme", font: "font" };
-
-const blipToasterAssetSpec: AssetMenuSpec = {
-  id: "bliptoaster",
-  catalog: bliptoasterAssetCatalog,
-  exportAsset: (ctx, sys, type, slot, label) => exportRitAsset(blipToasterOps, ctx, sys, type, slot, label),
-  replaceAsset: (ctx, sys, type, slot) => replaceRitAsset(blipToasterOps, ctx, sys, type, slot),
-  selectedSlot(ctx, sys, kind) {
-    const field = BLIPTOASTER_SELECTABLE[kind];
-    if (!field) return null; // kits have no live slot: ch5 CC 14 picks one, and nothing is baked
-    const s = blipToasterEffectiveSettings(ctx, sys);
-    return s ? s[field] : null;
-  },
-  selectSlot(ctx, sys, kind, slot) {
-    const field = BLIPTOASTER_SELECTABLE[kind];
-    if (field) blipToasterPinSettings(ctx, sys, { [field]: slot });
-  },
-};
-
-// --- BlipToaster settings rows (the cart's baked rig defaults) -----------------------------------------
-// BlipToaster has no settings memory - no battery, and nothing survives a RESET on purpose - so what you would
-// set once for your rig is baked into the `.nes`: a 16-byte block in its code bank
-// (@retroplug/bliptoaster/rom/settings).
-// These rows edit it exactly the way the asset rows edit assets: the pick is persisted on the
-// `bliptoaster-assets` role and folded into the ROM IN MEMORY at construct, and the file on disk is untouched.
-//
-// THEME and FONT have no row here: the cart names one of each as live, so their lists ARE the picker (a `*` on
-// the live slot, `Select` on every other - see blipToasterAssetSpec). The DMC kit has none either: ch5 CC 14
-// picks it, which a song does before it plays anything. What is left is the rig proper - the base channel, the
-// screen, the velocity curve - which nothing else in the menu names.
-//
-// Every row pins the field AND tells the running cart over SysEx, so it takes effect now; the pin is what a
-// later LOAD replays and what a bake writes. A project load needs neither - construct applies the pins on the
-// way in.
-const baseChannelNames = Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_v, i) => String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0"));
-
-/** The cart's baked block with the project's pins on top - what it is set to right now. Null when the ROM has
- *  no readable block (one predating it, or a format this build does not read). */
-function blipToasterEffectiveSettings(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView): BlipToasterSettings | null {
-  const bytes = assetRomBytes(ctx.stores.backend, sys.romPath);
-  if (!bytes) return null;
-  const rom = BlipToasterRom.fromBytes(bytes);
-  if (!rom.isBlipToaster || !rom.hasSettings) return null;
-  return { ...rom.settings()!, ...readBlipToasterSettings(sys) };
-}
-
-/** Pin `patch` on the role AND declare the resulting rig to the RUNNING cart. Both halves matter and neither
- *  is redundant: the pin is what a load replays and a bake writes, the SysEx is what the cart in front of you
- *  hears. Staged at this system's node, so it reaches THIS cart whatever the project's MUSICAL routing is doing, and
- *  at its rp.n8.nes too when the document places one (the real console, in the block the emulated core hears it). */
-function blipToasterPinSettings(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, patch: BlipToasterSettingsPatch): void {
-  const effective = blipToasterEffectiveSettings(ctx, sys);
-  if (!effective) return;
-  const next = { ...readBlipToasterSettings(sys), ...patch };
-  ctx.stores.project.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "bliptoaster-assets", { settings: next });
-  const sysex = blipToasterSettingsSysex({ ...effective, ...patch });
-  // The system's own node, and the cart node when this is the system that drives one (the first NES in slot order
-  // whose setting is on): the emulated core and the real console hear the same message in the same block.
-  ctx.stores.backend.stageNodeMidi(systemNodeId(sys.id), sysex);
-  const cart = cartFor(ctx, sys);
-  if (cart !== null) ctx.stores.backend.stageNodeMidi(cart.nodeId, sysex);
-}
-
-function blipToasterSettingsRows(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView): MenuItem[] {
-  const effective = blipToasterEffectiveSettings(ctx, sys);
-  if (!effective) return [];
-  const pinned = readBlipToasterSettings(sys);
-  const pin = (patch: BlipToasterSettingsPatch): void => blipToasterPinSettings(ctx, sys, patch);
-
-  return [
-    cycler("bliptoaster-set-basech", "Base MIDI Channel", baseChannelNames, effective.baseChannel, (n) => pin({ baseChannel: n })),
-    cycler("bliptoaster-set-ppu", "PPU Enabled", OFF_ON, effective.ppu ? 1 : 0, (n) => pin({ ppu: n === 1 })),
-    // "not on the VRC7 build" is the ROM's own behaviour (it has no velocity curve), not something to hide here:
-    // the byte is still baked and still honoured by every other build of the same project's ROM.
-    cycler("bliptoaster-set-curve", "Velocity Curve", ["Linear", "Log"], effective.velCurve ? 1 : 0, (n) => pin({ velCurve: n === 1 })),
-    // Reset is the one row left. There is no "Apply" any more: every row above already reached the cart over
-    // SysEx as it was stepped, so there was nothing left for a reboot to do that the row had not done. Reset
-    // still reboots, because dropping the pins means going back to the ROM's OWN bytes, which are only read at
-    // boot. Offered only once something IS pinned - with nothing pinned the rows show the ROM's bytes already.
-    ...(Object.keys(pinned).length
-      ? [
-          separator("bliptoaster-set-apply-sep"),
-          action("bliptoaster-set-reset", "Reset to ROM Defaults", () => {
-            ctx.stores.project.systems.setRoleConfig(sys.id, "bliptoaster-assets", { settings: {} });
-            ctx.stores.project.systems.reloadSystem(sys.id);
-          }),
-        ]
-      : []),
-  ];
-}
-
-// The BlipToaster tracker extras: the settings rows sit at the TOP of the BlipToaster menu, above the asset
-// submenus and fenced off from them (they are what the cart BOOTS with, the asset menus are what it boots
-// FROM). Inline rather than behind a "Settings" submenu of their own: there are only a handful, and one of the
-// two things you come to this menu to do should not cost a level. Empty when the ROM carries no readable
-// settings block.
-function blipToasterExtras(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView): MenuItem[] {
-  const rows = blipToasterSettingsRows(ctx, sys);
-  if (rows.length === 0) return [];
-  return [...rows, separator("bliptoaster-settings-sep")];
-}
-
-// --- LSDj Songs submenu (the SAV's 32 saved-song slots: export / replace / delete / add) ---------------
-// Songs are the battery, NOT a ROM override: edits act directly on the live SRAM (like LSDj's own FILE
-// screen) via mutateLiveSav (src/tracker/liveSav) - read the live sav, apply a BYTE-LEVEL transform (never
-// the lossy Song model - see lsdjSongOps), write the resolved .sav, cold-boot the core from it. Durable on
-// disk and reflected in the running LSDj. A no-op if there's no readable SRAM or the op returns null.
-// Returns whether the edit landed, so a caller that CHAINS edits (save the working song, then load another)
-// can stop when the first one declined rather than discarding work the save didn't actually preserve.
-function mutateSavBytes(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, fn: (sav: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array | null): boolean {
-  return mutateLiveSav(ctx.stores.backend, ctx.stores.project.systems, sys, fn);
-}
-
-// Export the saved song in `slot` to a picked `.lsdsng` file (byte-exact — decompress the slot, re-wrap).
-function exportSong(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, slot: number, name: string): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  browseThen(ctx, { title: `Export song ${slot}`, patterns: ["*.lsdsng"], saving: true, defaultName: `${sanitizeName(name)}.lsdsng` }, (path) => {
-    const bytes = ctx.stores.project.systems.readSram(sys.id);
-    if (!bytes) return;
-    const raw = decompressSlot(bytes, slot);
-    if (!raw) return;
-    be.writeFileAtomic(path, encodeLsdsngRaw(savSongName(bytes, slot) || name, savSongVersion(bytes, slot), raw));
-  });
-}
-
-// Replace the song in `slot` from a picked `.lsdsng` or `.lsdprj` (byte-exact; a bad file leaves the sav
-// alone). A `.lsdprj` also imports its kits (see importLsdprj).
-function replaceSong(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, slot: number): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  browseThen(ctx, { title: `Replace song ${slot}`, patterns: ["*.lsdsng", "*.lsdprj"] }, (path) => {
-    if (path.toLowerCase().endsWith(".lsdprj")) {
-      importLsdprj(ctx, sys, path, slot);
-      return;
-    }
-    const data = be.readFile(path);
-    if (!data) return;
-    mutateSavBytes(ctx, sys, (sav) => replaceSongInSav(sav, slot, data));
-  });
-}
-
-// Import a `.lsdprj` (song + its kit banks). The song goes into a slot (targetSlot for Replace, else the
-// first free slot); its kits are deduped against the effective ROM and the missing ones are recorded as
-// lsdj-assets kit overrides that LINK the `.lsdprj` by path (+ ordinal), with the song's kit references
-// remapped to the assigned slots (all byte-level — the Song model can't hold 6-bit kit indices). One rebuild
-// (loadSram) applies the kit overrides → romBytes and boots the imported song from the .sav.
-function importLsdprj(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView, path: string, targetSlot?: number): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  const systems = ctx.stores.project.systems;

-  const liveSram = systems.readSram(sys.id);

-  const overrides = lsdjOverrides(sys);

-}
-
-// Add a song: a `.lsdsng`/`.lsdprj` into the first free slot (the same importer drag-and-drop uses), or a
-// selection of songs from a `.sav`/`.srm` (the checkbox picker, validated against the cart's console).
-function addSongFromDisk(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView): void {
-  const be = ctx.stores.backend;
-  browseThen(ctx, { title: "Add Song", patterns: ["*.lsdsng", "*.lsdprj", ...SAV_PATTERNS] }, (path) => {

-      const importer = resolveTracker(sys.roles)?.songImport;

-}
````

`test/menu/bliptoaster.test.ts` gains its two cases in this task's commit, and they are the two defects the stage 4
review found in the code this task introduces: a second NES project stages BlipToaster's settings at its OWN system's
cart only, and a step costs no ROM read after the cache is warm. Every other existing test passes unchanged but for
the import paths Task 2 repointed; the asset and song menu tests are untouched.

````diff
diff --git a/packages/retroplug/test/menu/bliptoaster.test.ts b/packages/retroplug/test/menu/bliptoaster.test.ts
index 96952f81e..a1622ac8d 100644
--- a/packages/retroplug/test/menu/bliptoaster.test.ts
+++ b/packages/retroplug/test/menu/bliptoaster.test.ts
@@ -360,3 +360,47 @@ test("Select keeps the menu open, so a run of themes can be auditioned without r
   // Its neighbours do NOT: Export opens a dialog the menu should get out of the way of.
   expect(actionsOf(themes, "bliptoaster-theme-2").find((a) => a.id === "bliptoaster-theme-2-export")!.keepOpen).toBe(undefined);
 });
+
+test("a second NES project stages BlipToaster's settings at its OWN system only, not at the other NES's cart", () => {
+  // The cart node the project places belongs to the first NES in slot order, which is not necessarily this one: every
+  // NES drives a real cart by default. BlipToaster's rig SysEx is for the BlipToaster ROM's node, so a project where
+  // another system drives the N8 must not send it there - the menu's old cartFor() rule, which only staged at the
+  // cart when it WAS this system's.
+  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
+  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
+  be.seed("/roms/other.nes", nesRom());
+  const other = stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/other.nes")!;
+  be.seed("/roms/synth.nes", blipToasterRom());
+  const bt = stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/synth.nes")!;
+  const rows = () =>
+    submenuChildren(
+      buildInstanceMenu({ ...ctxOf(stores), system: stores.project.systems.view().find((s) => s.id === bt)! }).items,
+      "inst-bliptoaster",
+    );
+
+  findItem(rows(), "bliptoaster-set-basech")!.onCycle!(1);
+
+  expect(be.stageNodeMidiCalls.map((c) => c.nodeId)).toEqual([`sys-${bt}`]);
+  expect(be.stageNodeMidiCalls.some((c) => c.nodeId === `cart-${other}`)).toBe(false);
+});
+
+test("the live theme's marker reads the same cached ROM the rows do: a rebuild reads the file no more than once",
+  () => {
+  // The `*` marker is what makes the theme/font lists the picker, so it is read once per ROW. Reading it from disk
+  // there copied the whole image for every one of the sixteen theme rows on every menu build (a synchronous native RPC
+  // in the plugin); it goes through the shell's per-path cache the rows already use, so a warm rebuild reads nothing.
+  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
+  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
+  const items = blipToasterItems(be, stores, "/roms/counted.nes");
+  let romReads = 0;
+  const read = be.readFile.bind(be);
+  be.readFile = (path: string): Uint8Array | null => {
+    if (path === "/roms/counted.nes") romReads++;
+    return read(path);
+  };
+  items(); // the first build seeds the per-path caches
+  romReads = 0;
+  items();
+  items();
+  expect(romReads).toBe(0);
+});
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
/ assetMenu / bake machinery and reads the contributed specs.

project with more than one the placed cart belongs to the first in slot order, and
staging there for another system's cart would send this cart's rig to a console running

file once per row per build, which copied the whole image for every theme row on every

actions read has one typed reader (readRitOverrides, in ritAssets.ts), so the raw cast

group maps that id to today's screen through uiViews, the one interim cart-named id the
shell keeps until F4c. MenuContext carries the host App builds, and a composer that only
has the stores (the menu tests) gets one built from the context's own peers, so every
existing menu test runs unchanged; those two peers are documented as the fallback's
inputs.

New workspace dependencies (@retroplug/ui for risa, smsggdj and bliptoaster) and one new
rule-9 contract entry (@retroplug/core/path). The recorded menu matrix (stage 2's) holds
every tracker submenu, the asset rows' verbs and the node MIDI each settings or Select
step stages, so this stage changes none of them; nothing is re-recorded.
````

### Task 4: the device menus contribute themselves, and their services

Design sections 4.4, 4.5, 6 (E3, E7, E12), 7.3 and 8's fourth stage. `n8` and `launchpad` contribute `ts/ui/` modules
published through one `./ui` export each, they read the shell only through the host (`host.devices.rpc`, `host.config`,
`host.controller`, `host.systems.drivenCart()`), and the three watchers become services: a poll every 6 frames for the
card, a `start`, a `subscribe` and a poll every 3 frames for the scan, with the version-and-edge latches in each
service's closure and reset per mount. The Link Group becomes sameboy's `instance.footer` builder, the instance title
reads `Embed.shortLabel`, and `ui/app/useUiServices.ts` with `ui/app/serviceTicker.ts` is the one generic hook.

The proof written here is the ratchet (`test/boundaries/ui-cart-imports.test.ts` over its own Node runner): until F4c,
five `ui/` files may import a cart, console or device package, the list is derived from the manifests, and a listed file
that stops importing one fails too. The device-pack scan gains the `ui` and `cli` control-plane rule, because the
Launchpad scenario reaches the host through its menu half.

Expected: `d19747e6d18dd6d5def75d4a5839d6fd225398b2`: the blob 8e9c64128 holds for this file, so the applied diff is the prototype's change to it, byte for byte.

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/ui/index.ts`:

````ts
// The Launchpad's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.4 and 4.5): the control surface's
// submenu in the instance menu's device block, the scan rows Settings > MIDI offers (the one place a Launchpad can be
// FOUND), and the service that steps a scan and reclaims the recorded pair at startup.
//
// The submenu appears only when a surface is actually there - over USB by port name, or on a port pair a Settings >
// MIDI scan recorded (launchpadDetected). Detecting one is not a name test, because a Launchpad also speaks TRS/DIN: on
// a machine short of USB ports it arrives through an ordinary MIDI interface, on a port named after the INTERFACE, and
// nothing about that name says "Launchpad". Nor can it be done passively - DIN has no enumeration and no idle
// heartbeat, so the OS sees the interface and nothing else. It takes a Universal Device Inquiry, which is a transmit,
// which is why FINDING one lives in Settings > MIDI as a deliberate user action and this submenu only ever reads the
// answer. The port cyclers still offer every port unfiltered, so a wrong guess is fixable here.
//
// The rows straddle two scopes on purpose, because setting the feature up needs both: the ports + Connect are HOST
// state (persisted in config.json's controlSurface, shared by every project), while the app, its own knobs and Enable
// are PROJECT state (persisted in the .rplg, since which cart a surface drives is a property of the project). The shell
// hands both scopes in as the host's `config` and `controller` groups.
//
// The app's rows are built from the registry: the project's app id picks the contribution, and the knobs are the ones
// ITS module declares (menu), defaulted and bounded by ITS schema. So a second app is a package's change, not a
// shell one.
import { action, cycler, infoRow, separator, submenu, type MenuItem } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import {
  configRowCycler, defineUi, legacyConfigIndex, type MenuBuilder, type UiHost, type UiService,
} from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES, type ControllerTarget } from "../enums";
import type { ControllerApp } from "@retroplug/core/host";
import {
  applyLaunchpadScan, cancelLaunchpadScan, connectLaunchpad, forgetLaunchpad, getLaunchpadConfig,
  getLaunchpadScan, hasLaunchpad, launchpadDetected, launchpadScanBusy, looksLikeLaunchpad, pollControllerRole,
  onResetLaunchpadScanForTest, pollLaunchpadScan, restoreLaunchpad, setLaunchpadPorts, startLaunchpadScan,
  subscribeLaunchpad, type LaunchpadConfig, type LaunchpadScanStatus,
} from "./launchpadDevices";

const CONTROLLER_TARGET_LABELS: Record<ControllerTarget, string> = {
  system: "Emulated Cart",
  midiOut: "MIDI Out (real hardware)",
};

/** The read-only line describing what the controller has done to the cart's sync role. `driving` is the app's own answer
 *  (controllerSyncOverride): the mode its launches need is the one the cart is being put in, which is NOT "the mode is
 *  not the string off" - an app whose off-mode is spelt differently, or that has none, would then read as driving while
 *  nothing was sent. `cartSync` is the cart's OWN SYNC setting as last polled, which is what decided it. The wording
 *  names the APP and no mode, so a second app needs no change here. */
function cartSyncLabel(app: string, driving: boolean, cartSync: string | null): string {
  if (driving) return cartSync ? `Cart: ${app} - driving it` : `Cart: ${app} - driving it (SYNC unread)`;
  return `Cart: ${app} - not driving it: its SYNC is ${cartSync ?? "unread"}`;
}

/** The read-only status line: what the link is doing, in the words a player would use. */
function launchpadStatus(cfg: LaunchpadConfig): string {
  if (cfg.connected) {
    // `dropped` is what the device never got while it WAS attached (a full send ring, an oversized message): frames the
    // surface is missing, which a repaint replaces but the row still reports.
    if (cfg.dropped > 0) return `connected (${cfg.dropped} dropped)`;
    // The name a scan read off the device, when there is one. Worth the room: it is the difference between
    // "the cable reaches a Launchpad" and "the ports opened", which otherwise read identically here.
    return cfg.deviceLabel ? `connected - ${cfg.deviceLabel}` : "connected";
  }
  if (cfg.error) return `Error: ${cfg.error}`;
  if (cfg.enabled) return !cfg.selectedInput || !cfg.selectedOutput ? "pick both ports" : "not connected";
  // Nothing chosen, the feature off, and a device on a port named like its own USB interface: the whole of what an
  // upgrade from the legacy host needs is that there is nothing to migrate and where a device is found (design
  // section 5). The scan lives in Settings > MIDI because this submenu only exists for a device already known.
  if (!cfg.selectedInput && !cfg.selectedOutput && cfg.inputs.some(looksLikeLaunchpad))
    return "a Launchpad is here - Connect, or Settings > MIDI to scan for one";
  return "not connected";
}

/** Cycler names for one direction's ports, hinted ones tagged. Index 0 is "(none)" - a port must be chosen,
 *  since there is no sensible "all devices" for a device we claim exclusively. */
function launchpadPortNames(ports: string[], selected: string): { names: string[]; index: number } {
  const label = (p: string) => (looksLikeLaunchpad(p) ? `${p} (detected)` : p);
  const names = ["(none)", ...ports.map(label)];
  if (selected === "") return { names, index: 0 };
  const i = ports.indexOf(selected);
  if (i >= 0) return { names, index: i + 1 };
  names.push(`${selected} (not connected)`); // a persisted pick whose device is away still shows
  return { names, index: names.length - 1 };
}

/** The app's own rows, built from the registry and the app's schema: one per knob the app declares (`menu`), showing
 *  what the project holds and defaulting to what the schema fills, so the shell names no app, no knob and no value.
 *  A hand-edited value keeps the index these rows have always shown (legacyConfigIndex), so the menu reads as it did
 *  before the rows moved; the app's runtime still falls back to the schema's default (parseAppConfig). */
function controllerAppRows(
  host: UiHost,
  app: ControllerApp | undefined,
  config: Record<string, unknown>,
): MenuItem[] {
  if (!app || !app.menu) return [];
  const defaults = app.config.parse({}); // the schema is the source of a knob's default, as it is of its bounds
  const current = (key: string): unknown => (config[key] !== undefined ? config[key] : defaults[key]);
  const set = (key: string, value: unknown) => host.controller.set({ appConfig: { [key]: value } });
  return app.menu.map((field) =>
    configRowCycler(`lp-app-${field.key}`, field, current(field.key), defaults[field.key], (value) =>
      set(field.key, value), legacyConfigIndex(field, current(field.key))),
  );
}

function launchpadMenuChildren(host: UiHost, cfg: LaunchpadConfig): MenuItem[] {
  const controller = host.controller.settings();
  const store = host.config;
  const inp = launchpadPortNames(cfg.inputs, cfg.selectedInput);
  const out = launchpadPortNames(cfg.outputs, cfg.selectedOutput);
  const portAt = (ports: string[], n: number, current: string) => (n === 0 ? "" : ports[n - 1] ?? current);
  const rpc = host.devices.rpc;

  // Polled on the song-watch timer (refreshControllerSong), so reading it here costs a field access
  // rather than a 128 KB battery copy per menu render.
  const cartSync = controller.enabled ? host.controller.cartSync() : null;
  // What the published document will have the cart's sync node run, computed by the SAME helper buildGraph uses - so
  // the row cannot describe something other than what is happening.
  const syncOverride = controller.enabled ? host.controller.syncOverride() : null;
  const apps = host.controller.apps();
  const appIdx = Math.max(0, apps.findIndex((a) => a.id === controller.app));
  const app = apps.find((a) => a.id === controller.app);

  // Greyed while a scan runs: its answer is about to become the selection (launchpadScanBusy). The port pickers are
  // greyed while connected too: stepping one live would claim every pair it passed - Programmer-mode bytes at whatever
  // device each step landed on. Disconnect, pick, Connect.
  const scanning = launchpadScanBusy();
  const pickable = (item: MenuItem): MenuItem => (scanning || cfg.connected ? { ...item, disabled: true } : item);

  return [
    pickable(cycler("lp-input", "Input Device", inp.names, inp.index, (n) =>
      setLaunchpadPorts(store, portAt(cfg.inputs, n, cfg.selectedInput), cfg.selectedOutput, rpc))),
    pickable(cycler("lp-output", "Output Device", out.names, out.index, (n) =>
      setLaunchpadPorts(store, cfg.selectedInput, portAt(cfg.outputs, n, cfg.selectedOutput), rpc))),
    // Keyed on what the link IS doing, not on the saved intent: a pair saved as connected whose device was away at
    // launch is not connected, and reading "Disconnect" there left no way to retry but pressing twice. So it offers
    // Connect (which retries) beside a way to stop it reconnecting at every launch.
    action("lp-connect", cfg.connected ? "Disconnect" : "Connect",
      () => connectLaunchpad(store, !cfg.connected, cfg, rpc), scanning),
    ...(cfg.enabled && !cfg.connected
      ? [action("lp-stop", "Stop Connecting at Launch", () => connectLaunchpad(store, false, cfg, rpc), scanning)]
      : []),
    infoRow("lp-status", `Status: ${launchpadStatus(cfg)}`), // read-only
    // What the controller is doing to the cart's sync role, and why. Shown rather than applied silently: the override
    // does not touch the saved project (it happens in the published document), so without a row here the LSDj submenu
    // would go on reporting the user's own setting while the cart ran a different one.
    //
    // A cart that is not in the mode the app needs ignores row launches ENTIRELY WITHOUT COMPLAINT - it goes on playing
    // and stepping to the host clock, so the only symptom is that the pads stop doing anything. And the way players land
    // there is nasty: LSDj refuses to change SYNC while the cart is playing, so reaching for the setting mid-session
    // leaves it wherever the first press landed, with no way back until playback stops (measured in
    // test-native/lsdj-sync-toggle).
    ...(syncOverride
      ? [infoRow("lp-cart-sync", cartSyncLabel(app?.label ?? controller.app, syncOverride.driving, cartSync))]
      : []),
    separator("lp-sep-app"),
    // Project scope from here down: these ride the .rplg, and each edit publishes the graph.
    cycler("lp-enabled", "Use in Project", ["Off", "On"], controller.enabled ? 1 : 0, (n) =>
      host.controller.set({ enabled: n === 1 })),
    cycler("lp-app", "App", apps.map((a) => a.label), appIdx, (n) =>
      host.controller.set({ app: apps[n].id, appConfig: {} })),
    ...controllerAppRows(host, app, controller.appConfig),
    // Where launches go. "Emulated Cart" hands them to the tracker's own sync role in the same block; "MIDI Out" sends
    // them out of the host, which is how a real Game Boy behind an Arduinoboy is driven.
    cycler("lp-target", "Launches To", CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES.map((t) => CONTROLLER_TARGET_LABELS[t]),
      Math.max(0, (CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES as readonly string[]).indexOf(controller.target)), (n) =>
        host.controller.set({ target: CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES[n] })),
  ];
}

/** The instance menu's entry: `[]` on a host with no facet, and on one where no surface is here (then Settings > MIDI
 *  is the way in). */
const launchpadInstanceMenu: MenuBuilder = {
  placement: "instance.devices",
  build(host) {
    const cfg = getLaunchpadConfig(host.config, host.devices.rpc);
    if (!cfg || !launchpadDetected(cfg)) return [];
    return [submenu("inst-launchpad", "Launchpad", launchpadMenuChildren(host, cfg))];
  },
};

/** The read-only line under the scan row: what it is doing, or what the last one concluded.
 *
 *  A finished scan outranks the recorded device, and reads its own replies rather than waiting for them to
 *  be applied. Both halves matter: re-scanning after unplugging something has to be able to say "nothing
 *  answered" instead of going on naming what used to be there, and the verdict must not flicker through
 *  "nothing" while the apply edge lands a frame later.
 *
 *  `skipped` is worth showing rather than swallowing. A MIDI input is exclusive on Windows, so a port
 *  another application is holding simply cannot be listened on - and "nothing answered" then means
 *  something quite different from "nothing is there". */
function launchpadScanLabel(scan: LaunchpadScanStatus | null, cfg: LaunchpadConfig | null): string {
  if (scan?.busy) return scan.phase || "Scanning...";
  if (scan?.cancelled) return "Cancelled";
  if (scan?.done) {
    // A confirmed find leads even if something went wrong afterwards (a port that would not close): it was applied, so
    // the row has to say so.
    const hit = scan.found;
    if (hit) return `${hit.name} on ${hit.input}`;
    // "Could not look" stays attached to whatever else is said: on Windows a port another program holds cannot be
    // probed at all, and the device being looked for may be behind exactly that port.
    const inUse = scan.skipped > 0 ? ` (${scan.skipped} port(s) in use elsewhere)` : "";
    if (scan.error) return `Error: ${scan.error}${inUse}`;
    if (scan.unsupported) return `${scan.unsupported} - not supported${inUse}`;
    return `Nothing answered${inUse}`;
  }
  if (cfg?.deviceLabel && cfg.selectedInput) return `${cfg.deviceLabel} on ${cfg.selectedInput}`;
  return "Not scanned";
}

/** Settings > MIDI's control-surface rows: the one place a Launchpad can be FOUND, which is why they live here and not
 *  in the instance menu's submenu (that one only appears once a device is known, so a TRS-attached surface would have
 *  nowhere to be set up from). Settings is where you describe your rig; the instance menu is where you play the
 *  hardware you have. */
const launchpadScanRows: MenuBuilder = {
  placement: "settings.midi",
  build(host) {
    const rpc = host.devices.rpc;
    if (!hasLaunchpad(rpc)) return [];
    const lpcfg = getLaunchpadConfig(host.config, rpc);
    const scan = getLaunchpadScan(rpc);
    return [
      separator("midi-sep-surface"),
      // Cancel stays reachable whatever the link holds: it is the only way to stop a scan, and a pair claimed
      // behind one (a restore landing mid-scan) would otherwise leave it running with nothing to press.
      action("midi-scan", scan?.busy ? "Cancel Control Surface Scan" : "Scan for Control Surface",
        () => void (scan?.busy ? cancelLaunchpadScan() : startLaunchpadScan(rpc)),
        !!lpcfg?.connected && !scan?.busy),
      infoRow("midi-scan-status", `Control Surface: ${launchpadScanLabel(scan, lpcfg)}`),
      // Greyed while a scan runs as well: its answer is about to become the selection, and forgetLaunchpad refuses
      // mid-scan (a Forget that did nothing would read as a broken row).
      action("midi-scan-forget", "Forget Control Surface", () => forgetLaunchpad(host.config, rpc),
        !lpcfg?.selectedInput || !!lpcfg?.connected || !!scan?.busy),
    ];
  },
};

// The service's own latches: the scan version it last painted (a repaint only when it moves) and the finishing EDGE
// it has taken (a finished scan is applied once; `busy` re-arms it). `start` puts them back, so a remount re-takes an
// already finished scan's finishing edge and repaints once, which the applied-scan guard makes a no-op for the config
// it would write.
let seenVersion = -1;
let settled = false;

/** Where a mount starts the latches: no version painted and no finishing edge taken, so the next poll applies a scan
 *  that is already finished; a test that resets the scan state goes through this too. */
function resetServiceLatches(): void {
  seenVersion = -1;
  settled = false;
}

onResetLaunchpadScanForTest(resetServiceLatches);

/** One frame-poll tick: step a running scan, take a finished one's answer once, and let the device go when the open
 *  project stops wanting it. True = repaint (the scan moved). */
function pollLaunchpad(host: UiHost): boolean {
  const rpc = host.devices.rpc;
  const scan = pollLaunchpadScan(rpc);
  let repaint = false;
  if (scan) {
    if (scan.busy) settled = false; // a fresh run: its result has not been taken yet
    if (scan.done && !scan.busy && !settled) {
      settled = true;
      applyLaunchpadScan(host.config, scan, rpc);
    }
    if (scan.version !== seenVersion) {
      seenVersion = scan.version;
      repaint = true;
    }
  }
  // And whether the open project still runs the controller: when it stops, the device is let go (see
  // pollControllerRole) rather than left locked in Programmer mode with nothing driving it.
  pollControllerRole(host.controller.settings().enabled, rpc);
  return repaint;
}

const launchpadService: UiService = {
  id: "launchpad",
  // Reclaim the control surface config.json left enabled, once the UI is up, and tell the host it is done: a standalone
  // holds its MIDI stream and audio back until that word arrives (rp_device_host::restored), so a restored device's
  // pair is reserved before the shared stream ever opens it and costs no audio restart. Inert where no facet is
  // mounted.
  start: (host) => {
    resetServiceLatches();
    restoreLaunchpad(host.config, host.devices.rpc);
  },
  subscribe: subscribeLaunchpad,
  poll: { frames: 3, run: pollLaunchpad },
};

// Everything the module offers the shell and the tests: the port/scan seam (`./launchpadDevices`) is the contract a menu
// row, a service and a test all read, so it stays published from the package's one UI entry.
export * from "./launchpadDevices";

export default defineUi({
  menus: [launchpadInstanceMenu, launchpadScanRows],
  services: [launchpadService],
});
````
