````ts
// The N8 Pro's UI contribution (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.4 and 4.5): the submenu a project
// with a physical Everdrive drives, on the instance menu AND the start menu (the streaming and card ops need no loaded
// system, so a cart is configured before anything is opened), and the service that keeps its card row live.
//
// The submenu shows only when a physical N8 is actually detected (a serial port with the cart's USB VID:PID) - no
// hardware, no menu. Streaming: pick a serial port (auto-detecting the N8), Connect to open the link, tune the
// timed-release lookahead; the native host reconnects + persists (n8.cfg) on the spot. Card ops (Load ROM / back up and
// restore the battery): long capability jobs on the driven cart's rp.n8.nes node, which report progress on the
// read-only card row (the service's poll keeps it live). Those appear only once the link is up (see the gate below).
// One job at a time - every action is disabled while one runs.
import { action, browseThen, cycler, infoRow, separator, submenu, type MenuItem } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import {
  defineUi, type MenuBuildContext, type MenuBuilder, type UiHost, type UiService,
} from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { connectN8, getN8Config, setN8Lookahead, setN8Port, subscribeN8, type N8Config } from "./n8Devices";
import {
  getN8CartJob, n8DumpSram, n8LoadRom, n8RestoreSram, onResetN8CartJobForTest, projectCart, type N8CartJob,
} from "./n8SdOps";

const N8_LOOKAHEADS = [0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50];

/** A physical N8 counts as "here" only when one is actually enumerated (a serial port flagged isN8 by its USB
 *  VID:PID). null cfg = the host lacks the seam (headless harness). Gates whether the whole submenu renders. */
function n8Detected(cfg: N8Config | null): boolean {
  return !!cfg && cfg.ports.some((p) => p.isN8);
}

/** The read-only card-operation row: progress while busy, else the last result / error, else Ready. */
function n8SdLabel(job: N8CartJob): string {
  if (job.busy) {
    const pct = job.bytesTotal > 0 ? ` ${Math.floor((job.bytesDone / job.bytesTotal) * 100)}%` : "";
    return `${job.op === "load" ? "Uploading" : job.op === "dump" ? "Reading" : "Writing"}${pct}`;
  }
  if (job.error) return `Error: ${job.error}`;
  if (job.result) return job.result;
  return "Ready";
}

function n8MenuChildren(host: UiHost, cfg: N8Config, ctx: MenuBuildContext): MenuItem[] {
  // Port cycler: index 0 = "(auto-detect)" (empty selection); the rest are the DETECTED N8 ports only. A plain
  // serial port can't be an Everdrive, so we don't offer it (the cart is identified by its USB VID:PID). A
  // persisted selection that isn't currently enumerated is still shown, tagged "(not detected)", so it never
  // silently vanishes.
  const rpc = host.devices.rpc;
  const n8Ports = cfg.ports.filter((p) => p.isN8);
  const portValues = n8Ports.map((p) => p.port);
  const names = ["(auto-detect)", ...portValues];
  let index = 0;
  if (cfg.selectedPort !== "") {
    const i = portValues.indexOf(cfg.selectedPort);
    if (i >= 0) index = i + 1;
    else { names.push(`${cfg.selectedPort} (not detected)`); index = names.length - 1; }
  }
  const portName = (n: number) => (n === 0 ? "" : portValues[n - 1] ?? cfg.selectedPort);
  const laIdx = Math.max(0, N8_LOOKAHEADS.indexOf(cfg.lookaheadMs));
  const status = cfg.enabled
    ? cfg.connected
      ? `Streaming (${cfg.bytes} bytes)`
      : cfg.error
        ? `Error: ${cfg.error}`
        : "Connecting..."
    : "Off";

  // A card job is one at a time and holds the cart, so every action here (Connect included, which would have to wait
  // for the job's current step) is disabled while one runs, and the status row shows its progress.
  const job = getN8CartJob();
  const busy = job.busy;
  const items: MenuItem[] = [
    // The port, the link and the lookahead are the host's link, which a card job holds while it runs (a disconnect
    // during one waits for its current step), so all three wait too.
    cycler("n8-port", "Port", names, index, (n) => setN8Port(portName(n), rpc), busy),
    action("n8-connect", cfg.enabled ? "Disconnect" : "Connect", () => connectN8(!cfg.enabled, rpc), busy),
    cycler("n8-lookahead", "Lookahead", N8_LOOKAHEADS.map((m) => `${m} ms`), laIdx,
      (n) => setN8Lookahead(N8_LOOKAHEADS[n], rpc), busy),
    separator("n8-sep-status"),
    infoRow("n8-status", `Status: ${status}`),  // read-only streaming status row
  ];

  // The card operations (Load ROM / back up and restore the battery) are the driven cart's node's capability jobs, so
  // they appear while the project drives a cart - or while one runs. They need the link up (a job reaches the cart
  // only through it), and a job reads disconnected while it runs, so `connected` blips false mid-job; `busy` keeps the
  // block put. After a ROM load streaming stays stopped (a new game booted), so the block hides until you reconnect.
  // The project's driven cart, whichever instance's menu is showing: the cart is the PROJECT's (the document places
  // one, for the first system that drives it), so a menu of another system still reaches it, as it always has.
  const cart = projectCart(host);
  if (cart && (cfg.connected || busy)) {
    // Load ROM needs the cart at its menu; the battery rows reach its SD card's save file for the driven ROM (see
    // n8SdOps): back up takes about a minute for 64 KB and shows its progress, and a restore only lands when the
    // game next boots - so restore first, then load.
    items.push(
      separator("n8-sep-sd"),
      // The dialog offers every console's ROM globs, as it always has: the filter is the product's ROM list (what a
      // project can load), which only the shell's console registry can name, and a package may not read it.
      action("n8-load-rom", "Load ROM to N8...", () =>
        browseThen(host, { title: "Load ROM to N8", patterns: [...ctx.romPatterns] },
          (p) => n8LoadRom(host, cart, p)), busy),
      action("n8-dump-sram", "Dump SRAM to file...", () =>
        browseThen(
          host,
          { title: "Dump N8 SRAM", patterns: ["*.srm", "*.sav"], saving: true, defaultName: "n8.srm" },
          (p) => n8DumpSram(host, cart, p)), busy),
      action("n8-restore-sram", "Restore SRAM from file...", () =>
        browseThen(host, { title: "Restore N8 SRAM", patterns: ["*.srm", "*.sav"] },
          (p) => n8RestoreSram(host, cart, p)), busy),
      infoRow("n8-sd-status", `SD: ${n8SdLabel(job)}`),  // read-only card-operation status row
    );
  }
  return items;
}

/** The instance menu's entry, in the tracker block (it drives a real NES). `[]` when no cart is attached, which hides
 *  the entry: the submenu exists only for hardware that is here. */
const n8InstanceMenu: MenuBuilder = {
  placement: "instance.devices",
  build(host, _sys, ctx) {
    const cfg = getN8Config(host.devices.rpc);
    if (!n8Detected(cfg)) return [];
    return [submenu("inst-n8", "N8 Pro", n8MenuChildren(host, cfg!, ctx))];
  },
};

/** The start menu's entry, in its own fenced block: streaming and the card operations need no loaded system, so the
 *  cart can be configured (or a ROM loaded onto it) before a project is opened. */
const n8StartMenu: MenuBuilder = {
  placement: "start",
  build(host, _sys, ctx) {
    const cfg = getN8Config(host.devices.rpc);
    if (!n8Detected(cfg)) return [];
    return [separator("start-sep-n8"), submenu("start-n8", "N8 Pro", n8MenuChildren(host, cfg!, ctx))];
  },
};

// ~10 Hz at 60 fps - smooth enough for the progress bar and to catch "done" promptly, cheap enough to run forever (one
// small read, no repaint unless the version changed).
const POLL_FRAMES = 6;

/** The card row's poll: the snapshot is replaced as a job moves, so the service repaints its host only when the
 *  version it last saw moves (a progress tick, done, or an error). The latch starts where a mount finds it - -1, so the
 *  first poll repaints once, as the old per-mount ref did - and `start` puts it back on every mount. */
let seenVersion = -1;

onResetN8CartJobForTest(() => {
  seenVersion = -1;
});

const n8Service: UiService = {
  id: "n8",
  start: () => {
    seenVersion = -1;
  },
  subscribe: subscribeN8,
  poll: {
    frames: POLL_FRAMES,
    run() {
      const job = getN8CartJob();
      if (job.version === seenVersion) return false;
      seenVersion = job.version;
      return true;
    },
  },
};

// The device module is published through this entry, as the launchpad pack publishes its own, so a pack's contract is
// one module: its contribution plus the seam a test or another surface reaches it by.
export * from "./n8Devices";
export * from "./n8SdOps";

export default defineUi({ menus: [n8InstanceMenu, n8StartMenu], services: [n8Service] });
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The services, and the hooks they replace**

`ui/app/useUiServices.ts` runs each contribution's `start` in an effect, subscribes every `subscribe` through
`useRerenderOn` (the list is a module constant, so the call is stable) and hands the frame counting to
`serviceTicker.ts`'s `tickServices` over one `useNativeEvent("frame")`; `App.tsx` runs it and loses `useN8SdWatch`,
`useLaunchpadScanWatch`, `restoreLaunchpad` and the two `subscribe*` imports. Each `start` puts its latches back where
a mount finds them, so a remount repaints once and takes an already finished scan's finishing edge once more (the
applied-scan guard makes the re-applied edge a no-op for `config.json`). `resetLaunchpadScanForTest` and
`resetN8CartJob` clear them too, and the pack's `resolveClient`/`resolveLink` and the scan clock read the
test-injected globals before their module state.

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/app/useUiServices.ts`:

````ts
// Run the product's UI services (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.5): the device state the menu shows
// that no store can see, kept current without a hook of its own per device.
//
// A service is data a package contributes (`UiService`): `start` runs once when the UI is up (a device reclaimed from
// config.json), `subscribe` asks for a repaint when the native host pushes a change, and `poll` runs every `frames`
// render frames and answers whether what it shows MOVED. So each device's cadence and its version latch live in the
// package, and this hook is the one place a frame becomes a poll and a `true` becomes a repaint.
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";

import type { UiHost } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { uiServices } from "../host/menuContributions";
import { useRerenderOn } from "../hooks/useRerender";
import { useNativeEvent } from "../lvgl/useNativeEvent";
import { tickServices } from "./serviceTicker";

export function useUiServices(host: UiHost): void {
  const services = uiServices(); // a module constant, so the dependencies below are stable
  // Every subscription through the shell's one re-render hook, whose own force-update the polls below share: the list
  // is module data, so the call is stable and this runs once per mount.
  const rerender = useRerenderOn(...services.flatMap((service) => (service.subscribe ? [service.subscribe] : [])));
  // One `start` per mount (the host is the memoised one App built): a device reclaimed from config.json, once.
  useEffect(() => {
    for (const service of services) service.start?.(host);
  }, [services, host]);
  // One frame event, a counter per service, so two devices keep their own cadence rather than the fastest one's.
  const ticks = useRef<number[]>(services.map(() => 0));
  useNativeEvent("frame", () => {
    if (tickServices(services, host, ticks.current)) rerender();
  });
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/app/serviceTicker.ts`:

````ts
// One frame's worth of the contributed UI services' polls (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.5): a
// counter per service, so two devices keep their own cadence rather than the fastest one's, and one answer for whether
// anything moved. Kept out of the hook so the cadence and the repaint answer are testable with no display.
import type { UiHost, UiService } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";

/** Advance the counters one frame: run every service whose counter reaches its own `frames`, and answer whether any of
 *  them reported movement (the caller repaints once for the frame, not once per service). `ticks` is the per-service
 *  counter, which the caller keeps across frames; a list that changed length is re-sized here. */
export function tickServices(services: readonly UiService[], host: UiHost, ticks: number[]): boolean {
  if (ticks.length !== services.length) ticks.splice(0, ticks.length, ...services.map(() => 0));
  let moved = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < services.length; i++) {
    const poll = services[i].poll;
    if (!poll) continue;
    if (++ticks[i] < poll.frames) continue;
    ticks[i] = 0;
    if (poll.run(host)) moved = true;
  }
  return moved;
}
````

````diff
-// actually detected (a serial port with the cart's USB VID:PID, n8Detected below) - no hardware, no menu.
-// Streaming: pick a serial port (auto-detecting the N8), Connect to open the link, tune the timed-release
-// lookahead; the native host reconnects + persists (n8.cfg) on the spot. Card ops (Load ROM / back up and
-// restore the battery): long capability jobs on the driven cart's rp.n8.nes node, which report progress on the
-// read-only card row (useN8SdWatch keeps it live). Those appear only once the link is up (see the gate below).
-// One job at a time - every action is disabled while one runs.
-const N8_LOOKAHEADS = [0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50];
-
-// A physical N8 counts as "here" only when one is actually enumerated (a serial port flagged isN8 by its USB
-// VID:PID). null cfg = the host lacks the seam (headless harness). Gates whether the whole submenu renders.
-function n8Detected(cfg: N8Config | null): boolean {
-  return !!cfg && cfg.ports.some((p) => p.isN8);
-}
-
-// The read-only card-operation row: progress while busy, else the last result / error, else Ready.
-function n8SdLabel(job: N8CartJob): string {
-  if (job.busy) {
-    const pct = job.bytesTotal > 0 ? ` ${Math.floor((job.bytesDone / job.bytesTotal) * 100)}%` : "";
-    return `${job.op === "load" ? "Uploading" : job.op === "dump" ? "Reading" : "Writing"}${pct}`;
-  }
-  if (job.error) return `Error: ${job.error}`;
-  if (job.result) return job.result;
-  return "Ready";
-}
-
-/** The cart node this menu's card rows act on: the project's driven cart when `sys` is that system, or (with no
- *  `sys`) the project's cart alone. Null when the project drives none, and the card block is not built at all. */
-function cartFor(ctx: MenuContext, sys: SystemView | null): { system: SystemView; nodeId: string } | null {
-  const cart = projectCart(ctx.systems);
-  return cart && (sys === null || cart.system.id === sys.id) ? cart : null;
-}

-// "Launchpad" submenu (in the instance menu's tracker block, beside N8 Pro - a control surface plays a
-// tracker, so it belongs with them). Standalone-only, and shown only when a device is actually there
-// (launchpadDetected), the same rule the N8 Pro submenu next door follows.
-//
-// Detecting one is not a name test, because a Launchpad also speaks TRS/DIN: on a machine short of USB ports
-// it arrives through an ordinary MIDI interface, on a port named after the INTERFACE, and nothing about that
-// name says "Launchpad". Nor can it be done passively - DIN has no enumeration and no idle heartbeat, so the
-// OS sees the interface and nothing else. It takes a Universal Device Inquiry, which is a transmit, which is
-// why FINDING one lives in Settings > MIDI as a deliberate user action and this submenu only ever reads the
-// answer. The port cyclers still offer every port unfiltered, so a wrong guess is fixable here.
-//
-// The rows straddle two scopes on purpose, because setting the feature up needs both: the ports + Connect
-// are HOST state (persisted in config.json's controlSurface, shared by every project), while the app, its own knobs and
-// Enable are PROJECT state (persisted in the .rplg, since which cart a surface drives is a property of the project).
-//
-// The app's rows are built from the registry: the project's app id picks the contribution, and the knobs are the ones ITS
-// module declares (menu), defaulted and bounded by ITS schema. So a second app is a package's change, not a shell one.
-const CONTROLLER_TARGET_LABELS: Record<ControllerTarget, string> = {
-  system: "Emulated Cart",
-  midiOut: "MIDI Out (real hardware)",
-};
-
-/** The read-only line describing what the controller has done to the cart's sync role. `driving` is the app's own answer
- *  (controllerSyncOverride): the mode its launches need is the one the cart is being put in, which is NOT "the mode is
- *  not the string off" - an app whose off-mode is spelt differently, or that has none, would then read as driving while
- *  nothing was sent. `cartSync` is the cart's OWN SYNC setting as last polled, which is what decided it. The wording
- *  names the APP and no mode, so a second app needs no change here. */
-function cartSyncLabel(app: string, driving: boolean, cartSync: string | null): string {
-  if (driving) return cartSync ? `Cart: ${app} - driving it` : `Cart: ${app} - driving it (SYNC unread)`;
-  return `Cart: ${app} - not driving it: its SYNC is ${cartSync ?? "unread"}`;
-}
-
-/** The read-only status line: what the link is doing, in the words a player would use. */
-function launchpadStatus(cfg: LaunchpadConfig): string {
-  if (cfg.connected) {
-    // `dropped` is what the device never got while it WAS attached (a full send ring, an oversized message): frames the
-    // surface is missing, which a repaint replaces but the row still reports.
-    if (cfg.dropped > 0) return `connected (${cfg.dropped} dropped)`;
-    // The name a scan read off the device, when there is one. Worth the room: it is the difference between
-    // "the cable reaches a Launchpad" and "the ports opened", which otherwise read identically here.
-    return cfg.deviceLabel ? `connected - ${cfg.deviceLabel}` : "connected";
-  }
-  if (cfg.error) return `Error: ${cfg.error}`;
-  if (cfg.enabled) return !cfg.selectedInput || !cfg.selectedOutput ? "pick both ports" : "not connected";
-  // Nothing chosen, the feature off, and a device on a port named like its own USB interface: the whole of what an upgrade
-  // from the legacy host needs is that there is nothing to migrate and where a device is found (design section 5). The
-  // scan lives in Settings > MIDI because this submenu only exists for a device already known.
-  if (!cfg.selectedInput && !cfg.selectedOutput && cfg.inputs.some(looksLikeLaunchpad))
-    return "a Launchpad is here - Connect, or Settings > MIDI to scan for one";
-  return "not connected";
-}
-
-/** Cycler names for one direction's ports, hinted ones tagged. Index 0 is "(none)" - a port must be chosen,
- *  since there is no sensible "all devices" for a device we claim exclusively. */
-function launchpadPortNames(ports: string[], selected: string): { names: string[]; index: number } {
-  const label = (p: string) => (looksLikeLaunchpad(p) ? `${p} (detected)` : p);
-  const names = ["(none)", ...ports.map(label)];
-  if (selected === "") return { names, index: 0 };
-  const i = ports.indexOf(selected);
-  if (i >= 0) return { names, index: i + 1 };
-  names.push(`${selected} (not connected)`); // a persisted pick whose device is away still shows
-  return { names, index: names.length - 1 };
-}
-
-/** The app's own rows, built from the registry and the app's schema: one per knob the app declares (`menu`), showing
- *  what the project holds and defaulting to what the schema fills, so the shell names no app, no knob and no value. */
-function controllerAppRows(ctx: MenuContext, app: ControllerAppContribution | undefined, config: Record<string, unknown>): MenuItem[] {
-  if (!app || !app.menu) return [];
-  const project = ctx.stores.project;
-  const defaults = app.config.parse({}); // the schema is the source of a knob's default, as it is of its bounds
-  const current = (key: string): unknown => (config[key] !== undefined ? config[key] : defaults[key]);
-  const set = (key: string, value: unknown) => project.setController({ appConfig: { [key]: value } });
-  return app.menu.map((field) =>
-    configRowCycler(`lp-app-${field.key}`, field, current(field.key), defaults[field.key], (value) =>
-      set(field.key, value),
-    legacyConfigIndex(field, current(field.key))),
-  );
-}

-function launchpadMenuChildren(ctx: MenuContext, cfg: LaunchpadConfig): MenuItem[] {
-  const project = ctx.stores.project;
-  const controller = ctx.settings.controller;
-  const store = ctx.stores.userConfig;
-  const inp = launchpadPortNames(cfg.inputs, cfg.selectedInput);
-  const out = launchpadPortNames(cfg.outputs, cfg.selectedOutput);

-  // Polled on the song-watch timer (refreshControllerSong), so reading it here costs a field access
-  // rather than a 128 KB battery copy per menu render.
-  const cartSync = controller.enabled ? project.controllerCartSync() : null;
-  // What the published document will have the cart's sync node run, computed by the SAME helper buildGraph uses - so
-  // the row cannot describe something other than what is happening.
-  const syncOverride = controllerSyncOverride(ctx.systems, controller.enabled ? { ...controller, cartSync } : null);
-  const apps = controllerApps.list();
-  const appIdx = Math.max(0, apps.findIndex((a) => a.id === controller.app));
-  const app = controllerApp(controller.app);
-
-  // Greyed while a scan runs: its answer is about to become the selection (launchpadScanBusy). The port pickers are
-  // greyed while connected too: stepping one live would claim every pair it passed - Programmer-mode bytes at whatever
-  // device each step landed on. Disconnect, pick, Connect.
-  const scanning = launchpadScanBusy();
-  const pickable = (item: MenuItem): MenuItem => (scanning || cfg.connected ? { ...item, disabled: true } : item);
-
-  return [
-    pickable(cycler("lp-input", "Input Device", inp.names, inp.index, (n) =>
-      setLaunchpadPorts(store, portAt(cfg.inputs, n, cfg.selectedInput), cfg.selectedOutput))),
-    pickable(cycler("lp-output", "Output Device", out.names, out.index, (n) =>
-      setLaunchpadPorts(store, cfg.selectedInput, portAt(cfg.outputs, n, cfg.selectedOutput)))),
-    // Keyed on what the link IS doing, not on the saved intent: a pair saved as connected whose device was away at
-    // launch is not connected, and reading "Disconnect" there left no way to retry but pressing twice. So it offers
-    // Connect (which retries) beside a way to stop it reconnecting at every launch.
-    action("lp-connect", cfg.connected ? "Disconnect" : "Connect", () => connectLaunchpad(store, !cfg.connected, cfg), scanning),
-    ...(cfg.enabled && !cfg.connected
-      ? [action("lp-stop", "Stop Connecting at Launch", () => connectLaunchpad(store, false, cfg), scanning)]
-      : []),
-    infoRow("lp-status", `Status: ${launchpadStatus(cfg)}`), // read-only
-    // What the controller is doing to the cart's sync role, and why. Shown rather than applied silently: the override
-    // does not touch the saved project (it happens in the published document), so without a row here the LSDj submenu
-    // would go on reporting the user's own setting while the cart ran a different one.
-    //
-    // A cart that is not in the mode the app needs ignores row launches ENTIRELY WITHOUT COMPLAINT - it goes on playing
-    // and stepping to the host clock, so the only symptom is that the pads stop doing anything. And the way players land
-    // there is nasty: LSDj refuses to change SYNC while the cart is playing, so reaching for the setting mid-session
-    // leaves it wherever the first press landed, with no way back until playback stops (measured in
-    // test-native/lsdj-sync-toggle).
-    ...(syncOverride
-      ? [infoRow("lp-cart-sync", cartSyncLabel(app?.label ?? controller.app, syncOverride.driving, cartSync))]
-      : []),
-    separator("lp-sep-app"),
-    // Project scope from here down: these ride the .rplg, and each edit publishes the graph.
-    cycler("lp-enabled", "Use in Project", OFF_ON, controller.enabled ? 1 : 0, (n) =>
-      project.setController({ enabled: n === 1 })),
-    cycler("lp-app", "App", apps.map((a) => a.label), appIdx, (n) =>
-      project.setController({ app: apps[n].id, appConfig: {} })),
-    ...controllerAppRows(ctx, app, controller.appConfig),
-    // Where launches go. "Emulated Cart" hands them to the tracker's own sync role in the same block; "MIDI Out" sends
-    // them out of the host, which is how a real Game Boy behind an Arduinoboy is driven.

-      Math.max(0, CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES.indexOf(controller.target)), (n) =>
-        project.setController({ target: CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES[n] })),
+    ...menuPlacement("settings.midi", hostOf(ctx), ctx.system ?? null, buildContext(ctx)),
   ];
 }
 
-function n8MenuChildren(ctx: MenuContext, cfg: N8Config): MenuItem[] {

-  // serial port can't be an Everdrive, so we don't offer it (the cart is identified by its USB VID:PID). A

-    : "Off";

-  // for the job's current step) is disabled while one runs, and the status row shows its progress.
-  const job = getN8CartJob();

-    // during one waits for its current step), so all three wait too.
-    cycler("n8-port", "Port", names, index, (n) => setN8Port(portName(n)), busy),
-    action("n8-connect", cfg.enabled ? "Disconnect" : "Connect", () => connectN8(!cfg.enabled), busy),
-    cycler("n8-lookahead", "Lookahead", N8_LOOKAHEADS.map((m) => `${m} ms`), laIdx,
-      (n) => setN8Lookahead(N8_LOOKAHEADS[n]), busy),
-    separator("n8-sep-status"),
-    infoRow("n8-status", `Status: ${status}`),  // read-only streaming status row
-  ];
-
-  // The card operations (Load ROM / back up and restore the battery) are the driven cart's node's capability jobs, so
-  // they appear while the project drives a cart - or while one runs. They need the link up (a job reaches the cart
-  // only through it), and a job reads disconnected while it runs, so `connected` blips false mid-job; `busy` keeps the

-    // game next boots - so restore first, then load.
-    items.push(
-      separator("n8-sep-sd"),
-      action("n8-load-rom", "Load ROM to N8...", () =>
-        browseThen(hostOf(ctx), { title: "Load ROM to N8", patterns: ROM_PATTERNS },
-          (p) => n8LoadRom(ctx.stores.backend, cart, p)), busy),
-      action("n8-dump-sram", "Dump SRAM to file...", () =>

-          hostOf(ctx),
-          { title: "Dump N8 SRAM", patterns: ["*.srm", "*.sav"], saving: true, defaultName: "n8.srm" },
-          (p) => n8DumpSram(ctx.stores.backend, cart, p)), busy),
-      action("n8-restore-sram", "Restore SRAM from file...", () =>
-        browseThen(hostOf(ctx), { title: "Restore N8 SRAM", patterns: ["*.srm", "*.sav"] },
-          (p) => n8RestoreSram(ctx.stores.backend, cart, p)), busy),
-      infoRow("n8-sd-status", `SD: ${n8SdLabel(job)}`),  // read-only card-operation status row
-    );
-  }
-  return items;
-}
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The ratchet, and its fixture**

The runner walks `ui/` and fails for any file not on its five-file list that imports a cart, console or device package
(by specifier or by a relative path that lands in such a package's tree), and fails for a listed file that stops
importing one. The package list is derived from the workspace manifests, so a package added to the product cannot be
left off a hand-kept list; `@retroplug/launchpad/enums` and `/registry` are the two contract specifiers the shell
itself reaches, and `ui/generated/` is not judged.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/run-ui-cart-imports.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Walks the app's ui/ tree for an import of a cart, console or device package, for
// test/boundaries/ui-cart-imports.test.ts (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.3).
//
//   node test/boundaries/run-ui-cart-imports.mjs [--packages <name,...>] [--contracts <specifier,...>] [--root <dir>]
//
// The imports come from the boundary check's own scanner (TypeScript's preProcessFile), so a type-only import, an
// `export ... from` and a `require` all count: ui/ may carry a cart's code only through ui/generated/menus.ts, which is
// not judged (it is the one place that names every package), and a device pack's UI module MAY be reached through the
// generated list, never by a view directly. A RELATIVE import that lands in such a package's tree counts too, so
// reaching one by a path rather than a specifier is the same reach. Prints one JSON line:
// { hits: [{ file specifier }] }, file relative to the repository root.
//
// The package list is DERIVED from the workspace manifests unless --packages names one (a fixture): a cart, a console
// and a device pack each has a control-plane app module (`retroplug.app`), which is the code a view may not name, so a
// package added to the product cannot be left off a hand-kept list. The shell is the one exclusion: its own app module
// is what composes the UI, not a cart's.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const ts = createRequire(import.meta.url)("typescript-5");
const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../../..");

function option(name) {
  const at = process.argv.indexOf(name);
  return at === -1 ? undefined : process.argv[at + 1];
}

const packages = option("--packages");
const contracts = option("--contracts");
const root = resolve(option("--root") ?? REPO);

/** Every workspace package with a control-plane app module but the shell: a cart's, a console's or a device pack's
 *  code, which is what a view may not name. */
function derivedPackages() {
  const names = [];
  for (const entry of readdirSync(join(root, "packages"), { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (!entry.isDirectory() || entry.name === "retroplug") continue;
    try {
      const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, "packages", entry.name, "package.json"), "utf8"));
      if (manifest.retroplug?.app) names.push(manifest.name);
    } catch {
      // A directory with no manifest of its own is not a package.
    }
  }
  return names;
}

const PACKAGES = new Set(packages ? packages.split(",").filter((entry) => entry !== "") : derivedPackages());
const CONTRACTS = new Set((contracts ?? "").split(",").filter((entry) => entry !== ""));
/** The directory under packages/ each of those names: a relative import is resolved to a path and matched by it. */
const PACKAGE_DIRS = new Set([...PACKAGES].map((name) => name.split("/").pop()));
const uiRoot = join(root, "packages/retroplug/ui");

function walk(dir, out = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : 1))) {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      if (path === join(uiRoot, "generated")) continue; // the one place that names every package
      walk(path, out);
    } else if (/\.(ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/.test(entry.name)) out.push(path);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The package name a bare specifier names: the scoped pair ("@retroplug/lsdj/runtime" -> "@retroplug/lsdj"). */
function nameOf(specifier) {
  const parts = specifier.split("/");
  return specifier.startsWith("@") && parts.length > 1 ? `${parts[0]}/${parts[1]}` : specifier;
}

const hits = [];
for (const file of walk(uiRoot)) {
  const scanned = ts.preProcessFile(readFileSync(file, "utf8"), true, true);
  for (const { fileName } of scanned.importedFiles) {
    if (CONTRACTS.has(fileName)) continue; // a package's contract module the shell reaches through its own list
    const reach = fileName.startsWith(".")
      // A relative import counts by where it LANDS: reaching a cart's tree by a path is the same reach as its specifier.
      ? relative(join(root, "packages"), resolve(dirname(file), fileName)).replaceAll("\\", "/").split("/")[0]
      : null;
    if (reach !== null ? !PACKAGE_DIRS.has(reach) : !PACKAGES.has(nameOf(fileName)) && !PACKAGES.has(fileName)) continue;
    hits.push({ file: relative(root, file).replaceAll("\\", "/"), specifier: fileName });
  }
}
console.log(JSON.stringify({ hits }));
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/ui-cart-imports.test.ts`:

````ts
// The ui/ ratchet (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.3): until F4c moves the remaining React views into
// their packages, ONLY the five view files below may import a cart's code, and each must still import one (so F4c
// deletes this list by emptying it, rather than leaving a rule that has quietly stopped applying to anything). The two
// overlays are React and the three hooks/data modules are not; all five are F4c's views.
//
// Everything else under ui/ reaches a cart, a console or a device through the generated registries: ui/generated/menus.ts
// (not judged: it is the one place that names every package), src/generated/* through a store, or - for a menu entry -
// the package's own `ui` module, which this stage moved the device menus into. A view importing a cart's runtime is the
// last of F4c's work, which is why the list exists rather than a broad permission.
//
// The scanner is Node's (the boundary check's), so the test spawns test/boundaries/run-ui-cart-imports.mjs.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";

/** F4b's five remaining cart imports under ui/: the two overlays, the two runtime hooks and the HD session, which F4c
 *  moves into their packages. */
const ALLOWED = [
  "packages/retroplug/ui/screens/grid/LsdjOverlay.tsx",
  "packages/retroplug/ui/screens/grid/RisaOverlay.tsx",
  "packages/retroplug/ui/screens/grid/useLsdjRuntime.ts",
  "packages/retroplug/ui/screens/grid/useRisaRuntime.ts",
  "packages/retroplug/ui/screens/hd/useLsdjHdSession.ts",
];

// The packages whose code a view may not name are DERIVED by the runner from the workspace manifests (a console, an
// embedded ROM, a protocol or a device script), so a package added to the product cannot be left off a hand-kept list.

/** The two contract modules of such a package the SHELL itself reaches (rule 9's own entries: the controller target enum
 *  the project config persists, and the app registry it fills), which a UI host may therefore name directly. */
const CONTRACTS = ["@retroplug/launchpad/enums", "@retroplug/launchpad/registry"];

interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number }>;
  };
};

async function read(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  let bytes = new Uint8Array(0);
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (!value) continue;
    const next = new Uint8Array(bytes.length + value.length);
    next.set(bytes);
    next.set(value, bytes.length);
    bytes = next;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(bytes);
}

async function scan(root?: string): Promise<{ hits: { file: string; specifier: string }[] }> {
  // The runner resolves the repository from its own path, as the literal scan does; the test's working directory is the
  // shell package, so the script is named relative to it.
  const child = tjs.spawn(
    [tjs.env.RP_NODE ?? "node", "test/boundaries/run-ui-cart-imports.mjs",
      "--contracts", CONTRACTS.join(","), ...(root ? ["--root", root] : [])],
    { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" },
  );
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([read(child.stdout), read(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`run-ui-cart-imports failed (${status.exit_status}): ${err || out}`);
  return JSON.parse(out.trim().split("\n").at(-1)!) as { hits: { file: string; specifier: string }[] };
}

test("only the five remaining view files import a cart, a console or a device package", async () => {
  const { hits } = await scan();
  const files = [...new Set(hits.map((hit) => hit.file))].sort();
  // A file NOT on the list importing one is the ratchet biting: it would reach a cart's code directly.
  expect(files.filter((file) => !ALLOWED.includes(file))).toEqual([]);
  // And a listed file that stopped importing one shrinks the list with it.
  expect(files).toEqual([...ALLOWED].sort());
});

test("a relative reach from ui/ into a cart's tree is the same reach, and is counted", async () => {
  // A view may reach a console's code by a path as well as by a specifier; the ratchet resolves a relative import to
  // where it lands, so a run around the rule by `../..` fails here.
  const { hits } = await scan("test/boundaries/fixtures/ui-relative");
  expect(hits.map((hit) => hit.file)).toEqual(["packages/retroplug/ui/evil.ts"]);
});
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The device-pack scan's `ui` and `cli` rule**

`build-device-pack.mjs`'s whole-core scan skips the modules a manifest names as `app`, `ui` and `cli` (and the
directory of one that is its directory's index), and refuses a core module that imports one of them or a module under
such a directory, naming the importing file and the member. The fixture scenarios are three: a core importing its
`ts/ui` module, a core importing a helper beside `ts/ui/index.ts`, and a core importing the package's `cli` module;
the fourth (`ui-module-skip`) is the case the scan must let through.

````ts
// A package's UI half: the manifest's `ui` module, which the toolchain's whole-core scan skips, because a menu's code is
// the DESKTOP's (it reaches @retroplug/ui and the host, which the engine has none of). A call the engine lacks is fine
// HERE and in the rest of ts/ui, so this module calls one.
export function shown(row: number): boolean {
  return Number.isInteger(row);
}
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The tests: services, ids, the matrix's extension and the repointed imports**

`test/services.test.ts` is the mock tier's (a service is plain data: divisors through `tickServices`, one repaint
answer per frame, the startup call, the remount's re-taken edge, a list whose length changed re-sizing its counters);
`test-ui/ui-services.test.ts` drives the same through frames (the scan advances and repaints at its own cadence, the
restore runs once per mount and again after a remount, an N8 push repaints without a frame);
`test/menu/menu-ids.test.ts` refuses a builder that emits an id its tree already has. The matrix gains the
`launchpad-cart-sync` case and the card rows' dialog options, re-recorded from the design commit's code, and the menu
tests repoint their imports at the two packs' `./ui` entries. `test-native/launchpad-devices.test.ts` passes
`makeCall()` once, which is the one host-less caller's change.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/services.test.ts`:

````ts
// The device services (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.5 and 7.5 item 7): the N8 Pro's card row, the
// Launchpad's scan and its startup restore, driven the way the UI drives them but with no display and no hardware - the
// menu tests' own seam (a MockBackend store graph and the packs' fake clients).
//
// What is pinned is what a service IS, because that is all `useUiServices` reads: the frame cadence, whether a poll
// answers "repaint" (a version it last saw moving, never a steady state), and the startup call a restore makes once.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MockBackend } from "../testing/mockBackend";
import { composeAppStores, type AppStores } from "../src/appStores";
import { createUiHost, type UiHost } from "../ui/host/uiHost";
import { uiServices } from "../ui/host/menuContributions";
import type { UiHost as AnyUiHost, UiService } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { tickServices } from "../ui/app/serviceTicker";
import { getN8CartJob, n8RestoreSram, projectCart, resetN8CartJob, setN8LinkClient } from "@retroplug/n8/ui";
import {
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest, setLaunchpadClient, setLaunchpadScanClock, startLaunchpadScan,
} from "@retroplug/launchpad/ui";
import type { LaunchpadClient } from "@retroplug/launchpad/client";
import { nesRom } from "./systems/fixtures";

/** A full UI host over a mock store graph, with a system that drives a cart. */
function rig(): { stores: AppStores; host: UiHost } {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
  be.seed("/roms/a.nes", nesRom());
  stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/a.nes");
  const host = createUiHost(stores, { views: { open: () => {} }, beginImport: () => {} });
  return { stores, host };
}

function service(id: string): UiService {
  const found = uiServices().find((each) => each.id === id);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${id} service is contributed`);
  return found;
}

/** A fake Launchpad facet, the client's own interface, with the write counts a startup restore leaves. */
function fakeLaunchpad(connected: boolean) {
  const status = {
    connected, generation: connected ? 1 : 0, sent: 0, dropped: 0,
    input: connected ? "LPProMK3 MIDI" : "", output: connected ? "LPProMK3 MIDI" : "", error: "",
  };
  const counts = { claims: 0, releases: 0, restored: 0 };
  const open = new Map<number, { input: boolean; name: string }>();
  let next = 1;
  const client = {
    ports: () => ({ inputs: ["LPProMK3 MIDI"], outputs: ["LPProMK3 MIDI"] }),
    status: () => ({ ...status, connected: counts.claims > 0 || connected }),
    claim: () => {
      counts.claims++;
      return { ...status, connected: true, generation: 1 };
    },
    release: () => {
      counts.releases++;
      return { ...status, connected: false, generation: 0 };
    },
    send: () => true,
    restored: () => {
      counts.restored++;
      return true;
    },
    openInputs: (names: string[]) => names.map((name) => (open.set(next, { input: true, name }), next++)),
    openOutput: (name: string) => (open.set(next, { input: false, name }), next++),
    sendOn: () => true,
    read: () => ({ messages: [], dropped: 0 }),
    close: (handle: number) => open.delete(handle),
    portError: () => "",
  };
  return { client: client as unknown as LaunchpadClient, counts };
}

test("the product contributes a card-row service and a control-surface service at their own cadences", () => {
  // The two watchers this stage replaced ran at ~10 Hz and ~20 Hz; a service keeps its own frame divisor, so one
  // device's cadence cannot drift with the other's.
  expect(service("n8").poll!.frames).toBe(6);
  expect(service("launchpad").poll!.frames).toBe(3);
  expect(typeof service("launchpad").start).toBe("function");
});

test("the N8 card poll repaints only when the job's snapshot moves, and a job does move it", () => {
  const { host } = rig();
  setN8LinkClient({
    linkConfig: () => ({ ports: [], selectedPort: "", connected: false, enabled: false, lookaheadMs: 10, bytes: 0, error: "" }),
    setPort: () => {},
    connect: () => {},
    setLookahead: () => {},
  });
  try {
    const n8 = service("n8");
    resetN8CartJob(); // a fresh snapshot, whose version bump is the first thing a poll sees
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
    // The steady state is a read and no repaint: the snapshot the row shows has not moved.
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
    // A card operation that cannot read its file still ends, and the row must repaint to show its error.
    n8RestoreSram(host, projectCart(host)!, "/saves/missing.srm");
    expect(getN8CartJob().error).toBe("cannot read /saves/missing.srm");
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
    // A remount starts from the latch's initial state (the service's start puts it back, as the old per-mount ref
    // began), so the first poll after one repaints once even though the snapshot has not moved.
    n8.start!(host);
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
    expect(n8.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
  } finally {
    setN8LinkClient(undefined);
    resetN8CartJob();
  }
});

test("the control-surface service claims the recorded pair at startup and says the word once", () => {
  const { stores, host } = rig();
  const facet = fakeLaunchpad(false);
  setLaunchpadClient(facet.client);
  stores.userConfig.setControlSurface({
    enabled: true, input: "LPProMK3 MIDI", output: "LPProMK3 MIDI", device: "Launchpad Pro [MK3]",
  });
  try {
    const launchpad = service("launchpad");
    launchpad.start!(host);
    expect(facet.counts.claims).toBe(1); // the saved pair, taken
    // The host holds its own MIDI stream and audio back until it hears this, so the restore sends it whatever happened.
    expect(facet.counts.restored).toBe(1);
  } finally {
    setLaunchpadClient(undefined);
    resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  }
});

test("the control-surface poll steps a scan and repaints on its news, then settles to no repaint", () => {
  const { host } = rig();
  const facet = fakeLaunchpad(false);
  setLaunchpadClient(facet.client);
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  setLaunchpadScanClock(() => 0); // a frozen clock: a probe's answer window never closes, so the scan stays in flight
  try {
    const launchpad = service("launchpad");
    expect(startLaunchpadScan()).toBe(true);
    // The first poll sees the version the scan published when it started (the service's latch starts empty), and every
    // tick that changes nothing answers "no repaint" - which is what keeps the menu off the render path while a scan
    // waits out a window.
    expect(launchpad.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
    expect(launchpad.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
    expect(launchpad.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
    // A remount puts the latches back where a mount finds them, so its first poll repaints once more (the old hooks'
    // refs did the same) and takes the finishing edge again, which the applied-scan guard makes a no-op.
    launchpad.start!(host);
    expect(launchpad.poll!.run(host)).toBe(true);
    expect(launchpad.poll!.run(host)).toBe(false);
  } finally {
    setLaunchpadClient(undefined);
    resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  }
});

test("the frame ticker gives each service its own cadence and answers one repaint per frame", () => {
  // What `useUiServices` does with a frame, without a display: a counter per service, so a 3-frame device and a
  // 6-frame one keep their own cadences, and one answer for the frame (the hook repaints once, not once per service).
  const runs: string[] = [];
  const poll = (id: string, frames: number, moved: boolean): UiService => ({
    id,
    poll: { frames, run: () => (runs.push(id), moved) },
  });
  const services = [poll("three", 3, true), poll("six", 6, false), { id: "none" } as UiService];
  const ticks = services.map(() => 0);
  const host = {} as AnyUiHost;
  for (let frame = 1; frame <= 12; frame++) {
    const moved = tickServices(services, host, ticks);
    if (frame === 3 || frame === 6 || frame === 9 || frame === 12) expect(moved, `frame ${frame}`).toBe(true);
    else expect(moved, `frame ${frame}`).toBe(false);
  }
  // The three-frame service runs at 3, 6, 9 and 12; the six-frame one at 6 and 12 only.
  const counts = runs.reduce<Record<string, number>>((all, id) => ((all[id] = (all[id] ?? 0) + 1), all), {});
  expect(counts).toEqual({ three: 4, six: 2 });
  // A list that changed length re-sizes its counters rather than reusing another service's.
  const one = [poll("late", 2, false)];
  expect(tickServices(one, host, ticks)).toBe(false);
  expect(ticks.length).toBe(1);
  expect(ticks[0]).toBe(1);
  expect(tickServices(one, host, ticks)).toBe(false);
  expect(ticks[0]).toBe(0);
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-ui/ui-services.test.ts`:

````ts
// The contributed UI services through the real app (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md sections 4.5 and 7.5 item
// 7): what only a display can show is that a frame becomes a poll and a poll's "moved" becomes a repaint, and that a
// mount runs the startup work once. The services' own model is pinned in test/services.test.ts; here the App runs them.
//
// The devices are faked at the packs' own clients, as the menu tests fake them: a Launchpad that answers a scan and
// counts its restores, and an N8 link whose status the test moves. No hardware is touched.
import { test, expect, ui, navTo, Key } from "ui-harness";
import type { LaunchpadClient } from "@retroplug/launchpad/client";
import type { N8LinkClient } from "@retroplug/n8";

// Settings > MIDI (where a control surface is found) and Settings > Audio are standalone-only, so the host says it is
// one; the MIDI lists are fixed so both submenus render with no device.
const g = globalThis as Record<string, unknown>;
g.__rp_isStandalone = true;
g.__rp_getMidiConfig = () => ({ inputs: [], outputs: [], selectedInput: "", selectedOutput: "" });

const labelOf = (prefix: string) => ui.findByTextContaining(prefix)?.text ?? "(missing)";

// The Launchpad's scan state machine is driven by the wall clock, so the test owns it: nothing finishes until the test
// says the window has passed.
const clock = { ms: 0 };

/** A Launchpad that answers nothing and counts what a mount does to it. */
function fakeLaunchpad() {
  const counts = { claims: 0, restored: 0, opens: 0 };
  const open = new Map<number, { input: boolean; name: string }>();
  let next = 1;
  const client = {
    ports: () => ({ inputs: ["LPProMK3 MIDI"], outputs: ["LPProMK3 MIDI"] }),
    status: () => ({
      connected: counts.claims > 0, generation: counts.claims > 0 ? 1 : 0, sent: 0, dropped: 0,
      input: counts.claims > 0 ? "LPProMK3 MIDI" : "", output: counts.claims > 0 ? "LPProMK3 MIDI" : "", error: "",
    }),
    claim: () => {
      counts.claims++;
      return { connected: true, generation: 1, sent: 0, dropped: 0, input: "LPProMK3 MIDI",
        output: "LPProMK3 MIDI", error: "" };
    },
    release: () => ({ connected: false, generation: 0, sent: 0, dropped: 0, input: "", output: "", error: "" }),
    send: () => true,
    restored: () => {
      counts.restored++;
      return true;
    },
    openInputs: (names: string[]) => {
      counts.opens++;
      return names.map((name) => (open.set(next, { input: true, name }), next++));
    },
    openOutput: (name: string) => {
      counts.opens++;
      return (open.set(next, { input: false, name }), next++);
    },
    sendOn: () => true,
    read: () => ({ messages: [], dropped: 0 }),
    close: (handle: number) => open.delete(handle),
    portError: () => "",
  };
  return { client: client as unknown as LaunchpadClient, counts };
}
const launchpad = fakeLaunchpad();

/** The N8's link, faked: one attached port, off until the menu's Connect row turns it on. */
const n8State = { enabled: false, connected: false, selectedPort: "" };
const n8Link: N8LinkClient = {
  linkConfig: () => ({
    ports: [{ port: "/dev/ttyACM0", isN8: true }],
    selectedPort: n8State.selectedPort,
    connected: n8State.connected,
    enabled: n8State.enabled,
    lookaheadMs: 10,
    bytes: 0,
    error: "",
  }),
  setPort: (port: string) => {
    n8State.selectedPort = port;
  },
  connect: (enabled: boolean) => {
    n8State.enabled = enabled;
  },
  setLookahead: () => {},
};

// The App is a prebuilt bundle with its own copies of the packs' modules, so the only thing it shares with this test is
// globalThis: the packs' test seams read these, and nothing in production sets them.
Object.assign(g, {
  __rp_launchpadClient: launchpad.client,
  __rp_launchpadClock: () => clock.ms,
  __rp_n8LinkClient: n8Link,
});

test("a control-surface scan advances and repaints through frames once its window passes", () => {
  expect(ui.boot()).toBeTruthy();
  ui.pump(30); // settle the mount and run the startup restore
  expect(navTo("Settings")).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Enter);
  ui.pump(8);
  expect(navTo("MIDI")).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Enter);
  ui.pump(8);

  clock.ms = 0;
  expect(navTo("Scan for Control Surface")).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Enter);
  ui.pump(1);
  // The scan's poll runs every 3 frames; one frame in, the row still reads what starting published.
  expect(labelOf("Control Surface:").includes("Nothing answered")).toBe(false);
  // The scan's own window: each step is one poll period's worth of frames, with the clock moved on so the window can
  // close. THE CADENCES are pinned by services.test.ts's divisors; this case holds that through frames a poll advances
  // the scan and its finishing edge repaints the row.
  for (let i = 0; i < 4 && !labelOf("Control Surface:").includes("Nothing answered"); i++) {
    clock.ms += 1000;
    ui.pump(3);
  }
  expect(labelOf("Control Surface:")).toBe("Control Surface: Nothing answered");
});

test("the startup restore runs once per mount, and a remount runs it again", () => {
  expect(ui.boot()).toBeTruthy();
  // A mount whose start sees the fake, counted from zero whatever the App's own first mount did.
  launchpad.counts.restored = 0;
  ui.reopen();
  ui.pump(10);
  const afterMount = launchpad.counts.restored;
  expect(afterMount).toBe(1); // the mount's start, and nothing else
  ui.pump(20); // frames pass: the effect must not run again
  expect(launchpad.counts.restored).toBe(afterMount);
  ui.reopen(); // unmount + remount
  ui.pump(10);
  expect(launchpad.counts.restored).toBe(afterMount + 1);
  ui.pump(10);
  expect(launchpad.counts.restored).toBe(afterMount + 1);
});

test("a native N8 change repaints the menu through the service's subscription", () => {
  expect(ui.boot()).toBeTruthy();
  ui.pump(30);
  ui.fileDrop(ui.romDir() + "/bliptoaster.nes", 0, 0);
  ui.pump(30);
  expect(ui.findByTestId("tile-0") != null).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Esc); // the instance menu
  ui.pump(10);
  expect(navTo("N8 Pro")).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Enter);
  ui.pump(10);
  expect(labelOf("Status:")).toBe("Status: Off");
  // The Port cycler: stepping it applies through the link and emits, and the menu repaints off the subscription without
  // a frame (a poll would not have run in two pumps; the label is read off the new config).
  expect(navTo("Port")).toBeTruthy();
  ui.tapKey(Key.Enter);
  ui.pump(2);
  expect(labelOf("Port:")).toBe("Port: /dev/ttyACM0");
});
````

````ts
// The menu's one-id rule (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 4.4): the menu is keyed by id, so a
// contributed builder that emits one of the shell's own ids (a footer builder emitting `inst-exit`) would silently take
// that row's place. The composers assert it over the tree they built, which is the only place both halves are known.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { action, submenu } from "@retroplug/ui/menu";
import { assertUniqueMenuIds } from "../../ui/host/menuContributions";

test("two rows of one id in one menu are refused, naming the id and the menu", () => {
  expect(() => assertUniqueMenuIds([action("a", "A", () => {}), action("a", "B", () => {})], "a menu"))
    .toThrow("two menu rows share the id a in a menu");
});

test("a nested row of an id its menu already has is refused too", () => {
  const tree = [submenu("outer", "Outer", [action("inst-exit", "Exit", () => {})]), action("inst-exit", "Exit", () => {})];
  expect(() => assertUniqueMenuIds(tree, "the instance menu"))
    .toThrow("two menu rows share the id inst-exit in the instance menu");
});
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````ts
// The CLI tool contract (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 5.1): a package's subcommand is data it
// contributes, run against the groups of the CLI host, so the shell's dispatcher carries no cart's or device's code.
import type { Host } from "./host";

/** What a CLI tool may reach: the file and image helpers, the kit compiler, the native facets' devices and the
 *  process a session runs in. No dialogs (a tool takes paths), no live systems and no views; this is the one name for
 *  it, which the shell's host builder returns and a package's `run` receives. */
export type CliHost = Host<"files" | "png" | "kits" | "devices" | "process" | "songs">;

export interface CliTool<H = CliHost> {
  /** The subcommand, what the user types after `retroplug-cli`. */
  readonly name: string;
  /** One line for the top-level command index. */
  readonly summary: string;
  /** The full `retroplug-cli <name> --help` text: flags, defaults, examples. */
  readonly help: string;
  /** A live tool (a MIDI bridge): it calls `host.process.keepAlive()` and returns, and the dispatcher leaves it running
   *  until the process ends. Omit for a batch command. */
  readonly longRunning?: boolean;
  /** Run against the tool's host, given its own argument vector (everything after the command name). A promise is
   *  waited for before the process exits, so a rejection is still reported as a failed command. */
  run(host: H, args: string[]): void | Promise<void>;
}

/** The identity a package's tools module default-exports; it exists so the contribution is checked where it is
 *  written. */
export function defineCliTools(tools: readonly CliTool[]): readonly CliTool[] {
  return tools;
}
````

````ts
// A tiny RIFF/PCM16 WAV codec's pure half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 5.2): the header, the
// int16 body, the whole-buffer encoder, the two stereo helpers and the decoder. A package's CLI tool imports these
// from here; the backend-bound streaming writer (`createWavWriter`) stays in the shell's src/render/wav.ts, which
// imports what it needs from this module.
function writeAscii(view: DataView, offset: number, s: string): void {
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) view.setUint8(offset + i, s.charCodeAt(i));
}

/** The fixed 44-byte canonical RIFF/PCM16 header. Only two fields depend on length: offset 4 (RIFF
 *  chunk size = 36 + dataSize) and offset 40 (dataSize), so a streaming writer emits this with
 *  dataSize=0, appends the PCM, then re-emits it at offset 0 with the final dataSize (createWavWriter). */
export function wavHeader(sampleRate: number, channels: number, dataSize: number): Uint8Array {
  const buf = new ArrayBuffer(44);
  const view = new DataView(buf);
  writeAscii(view, 0, "RIFF");
  view.setUint32(4, 36 + dataSize, true);
  writeAscii(view, 8, "WAVE");
  writeAscii(view, 12, "fmt ");
  view.setUint32(16, 16, true); // fmt chunk size
  view.setUint16(20, 1, true); // PCM
  view.setUint16(22, channels, true);
  view.setUint32(24, sampleRate, true);
  view.setUint32(28, sampleRate * channels * 2, true); // byte rate
  view.setUint16(32, channels * 2, true); // block align
  view.setUint16(34, 16, true); // bits per sample
  writeAscii(view, 36, "data");
  view.setUint32(40, dataSize, true);
  return new Uint8Array(buf);
}

/** Convert interleaved float PCM in [-1,1] (clamped: the render pipeline isn't hard-clamped) to the
 *  little-endian int16 body a WAV carries. Iterates 0..length, so it honors a `subarray` view (non-zero
 *  byteOffset), which the streaming writer feeds per-chunk sub-slices with. */
export function pcm16(pcm: Float32Array): Uint8Array {
  const out = new Uint8Array(pcm.length * 2);
  const view = new DataView(out.buffer);
  for (let i = 0; i < pcm.length; i++) {
    const v = pcm[i] > 1 ? 1 : pcm[i] < -1 ? -1 : pcm[i];
    view.setInt16(i * 2, (v * 32767) | 0, true);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Encode interleaved PCM (as renderAudio returns it) to a 16-bit WAV, whole-buffer. `pcm` is L,R,L,R…
 *  in [-1,1]; `channels` is how those samples interleave. (Streaming callers use createWavWriter.) */
export function encodeWav(pcm: Float32Array, sampleRate = 44100, channels = 2): Uint8Array {
  const header = wavHeader(sampleRate, channels, pcm.length * 2);
  const body = pcm16(pcm);
  const out = new Uint8Array(header.length + body.length);
  out.set(header);
  out.set(body, header.length);
  return out;
}

/** Interleave K equal-length stereo streams (each L,R,L,R…) into one 2K-channel interleaved buffer,
 *  channel order [s0.L, s0.R, s1.L, s1.R, …]. Feeds encodeWav(_, sr, 2*K) for a single multichannel WAV
 *  (Game Boy: 4 stereo channel-streams → 8 channels). Streams must share a frame count. */
export function interleaveStereoStreams(streams: Float32Array[]): Float32Array {
  const k = streams.length;
  if (k === 0) return new Float32Array(0);
  const frames = streams[0].length / 2;
  for (const s of streams)
    if (s.length !== streams[0].length) throw new Error("interleaveStereoStreams: streams differ in length");
  const out = new Float32Array(frames * 2 * k);
  for (let f = 0; f < frames; f++)
    for (let s = 0; s < k; s++) {
      out[f * 2 * k + s * 2 + 0] = streams[s][f * 2 + 0];
      out[f * 2 * k + s * 2 + 1] = streams[s][f * 2 + 1];
    }
  return out;
}

/** Split one interleaved-stereo buffer (L,R,L,R…) into its two mono channels [L…], [R…]. Feeds
 *  encodeWav(_, sr, 1) for individual-mono export (Game Boy: 4 stereo streams → 8 mono files). */
export function deinterleaveStereo(pcm: Float32Array): [Float32Array, Float32Array] {
  const frames = pcm.length / 2;
  const l = new Float32Array(frames);
  const r = new Float32Array(frames);
  for (let f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
    l[f] = pcm[f * 2 + 0];
    r[f] = pcm[f * 2 + 1];
  }
  return [l, r];
}

/** Decode a PCM WAV to { sampleRate, channels, interleaved pcm } in [-1,1]. Handles what encodeWav writes
 *  (16-bit, canonical 44-byte header) plus what an external recorder hands back from real hardware: 24/32-bit
 *  int and 32-bit float, WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, and extra chunks before `data` (so it walks chunks rather
 *  than assuming fixed offsets). */
export function decodeWav(bytes: Uint8Array): { sampleRate: number; channels: number; pcm: Float32Array } {
  const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
  const tag = (o: number) => String.fromCharCode(view.getUint8(o), view.getUint8(o + 1), view.getUint8(o + 2), view.getUint8(o + 3));
  if (tag(0) !== "RIFF" || tag(8) !== "WAVE") throw new Error("decodeWav: not a RIFF/WAVE file");

  let format = 0, channels = 0, sampleRate = 0, bits = 0;
  let dataAt = -1, dataSize = 0;
  for (let o = 12; o + 8 <= bytes.byteLength; ) {
    const id = tag(o);
    const size = view.getUint32(o + 4, true);
    const body = o + 8;
    if (id === "fmt ") {
      format = view.getUint16(body, true);
      channels = view.getUint16(body + 2, true);
      sampleRate = view.getUint32(body + 4, true);
      bits = view.getUint16(body + 14, true);
      // WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE: the real format is the first 2 bytes of the SubFormat GUID.
      if (format === 0xfffe && size >= 40) format = view.getUint16(body + 24, true);
    } else if (id === "data") {
      dataAt = body;
      dataSize = Math.min(size, bytes.byteLength - body);
    }
    o = body + size + (size & 1); // chunks are word-aligned
  }
  if (dataAt < 0 || !channels || !sampleRate) throw new Error("decodeWav: missing fmt/data chunk");

  const bytesPer = bits >> 3;
  if (!bytesPer) throw new Error("decodeWav: bad bits-per-sample");
  const count = Math.floor(dataSize / bytesPer);
  const pcm = new Float32Array(count);
  if (format === 3 && bits === 32) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) pcm[i] = view.getFloat32(dataAt + i * 4, true);
  } else if (format === 1 && bits === 16) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) pcm[i] = view.getInt16(dataAt + i * 2, true) / 32768;
  } else if (format === 1 && bits === 32) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) pcm[i] = view.getInt32(dataAt + i * 4, true) / 2147483648;
  } else if (format === 1 && bits === 24) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const p = dataAt + i * 3;
      const v = (view.getUint8(p) | (view.getUint8(p + 1) << 8) | (view.getInt8(p + 2) << 16));
      pcm[i] = v / 8388608;
    }
  } else if (format === 1 && bits === 8) {
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) pcm[i] = (view.getUint8(dataAt + i) - 128) / 128;
  } else {
    throw new Error(`decodeWav: unsupported format ${format} @ ${bits}-bit`);
  }
  return { sampleRate, channels, pcm };
}
````

Create `packages/tracker/ts/nes/kitSpec.ts`:

````ts
// The NES DMC kit-compile spec (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 5.2): one source sample per slot, and a
// whole bank. It lives in tracker because the format is SHARED - risa's kit format compiles it, and BlipToaster's CLI
// tool compiles the same 8 KB bank through that format by its id - so a package that is not risa can name it without
// depending on risa. The types are dsp's KitSampleSpec plus the DMC slot's own knobs.
import type { KitSampleSpec } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";

/** One source sample for the DMC compiler: a kit sample plus the PAL DPCM playback-rate index (0..15, default 12), a
 *  loop flag, and whether to peak-normalize into the 7-bit domain (default true). */
export interface NesDmcSampleSpec extends KitSampleSpec {
  rate?: number;
  loop?: boolean;
  normalize?: boolean;
}

/** A whole DMC kit compile: a 6-char kit name and up to 16 samples. */
export interface NesDmcKitSpec {
  name: string;
  samples: NesDmcSampleSpec[];
}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The tools, moved into their packages**

Each is a `git mv` with its own package's relative imports, behind a `ts/cli/index.ts` that default-exports
`defineCliTools([...])` and is the manifest's `cli` member. `n8` exports `./cli`, `./bridge` and `./ui`; `runBridge`
is the loop `n8-bridge` and risa's `n8-sync` share, so `n8` stays free of every cart. `bliptoaster-rom` compiles
through `host.kits.compile<NesDmcKitSpec>("risa", spec)` with the NES codecs from `@retroplug/tracker/nes/*`, so
BlipToaster imports no risa; `n8-load` prints its battery listing through `host.songs.list`; and no tool imports
`Session`, `makeCall`, `createMidiClient` or `keepAlive`.

Create `packages/risa/ts/cli/n8Sync.ts`:

````ts
// `retroplug-cli n8-sync` - translate a MIDI clock/transport into risa's host-sync bytes on a physical Everdrive N8
// Pro. It lives in risa, which depends on n8 and drives that pack's shared bridge loop; n8 itself names no cart.
import type { CliHost, CliTool } from "@retroplug/core/cliTool";
import { COMMON_FLAGS, printInputs, runBridge } from "@retroplug/n8/bridge";
import { RisaSyncTranslator } from "../risaSyncTranslator";

const SYNC_HELP = [
  "usage: retroplug-cli n8-sync [--list] [--midi-in <name>] [--serial <port>] [--lookahead-ms <N>]",
  "",
  "  Turn an incoming MIDI clock/transport (Start/Continue/Stop + 24-PPQN clock, optional Song Position)",
  "  into risa's host-sync protocol on a physical N8, so a risa cart plays locked to the DAW. Runs until",
  "  Ctrl-C. Load a risa ROM first (retroplug-cli n8-load).",
  "",
  ...COMMON_FLAGS,
].join("\n");

export const n8SyncTool: CliTool = {
  name: "n8-sync",
  summary: "drive risa host-sync on a physical Everdrive N8 Pro from a MIDI clock",
  help: SYNC_HELP,
  longRunning: true,
  run(host: CliHost, args: string[]): void {
    if (args.includes("--list")) {
      printInputs(host);
      host.process.exit(0);
      return;
    }
    const translator = new RisaSyncTranslator();
    runBridge(host, args, "RetroPlug N8 Sync", (bytes, out) => translator.onMessage(bytes, out));
  },
};
````

Create `packages/n8/ts/cli/n8Bridge.ts`:

````ts
// `retroplug-cli n8-bridge` - stream live MIDI to a physical Everdrive N8 Pro over USB, entirely in TS (it replaced the
// native subcommand). The bridge loop itself is the pack's `/bridge` entry, which risa's n8-sync drives too.
import type { CliHost, CliTool } from "@retroplug/core/cliTool";
import { COMMON_FLAGS, printInputs, runBridge } from "../bridge";

const BRIDGE_HELP = [
  "usage: retroplug-cli n8-bridge [--list] [--midi-in <name>] [--serial <port>] [--lookahead-ms <N>]",
  "",
  "  Stream live MIDI straight to a physical Everdrive N8 Pro's cart FIFO over USB, so a controller / DAW",
  "  plays the real NES (for the BlipToaster ROM). Runs until Ctrl-C.",
  "",
  ...COMMON_FLAGS,
].join("\n");

export const n8BridgeTool: CliTool = {
  name: "n8-bridge",
  summary: "stream live MIDI to a physical Everdrive N8 Pro over USB",
  help: BRIDGE_HELP,
  longRunning: true,
  run(host: CliHost, args: string[]): void {
    if (args.includes("--list")) {
      printInputs(host);
      host.process.exit(0);
      return;
    }
    runBridge(host, args, "RetroPlug N8", (bytes, out) => {
      for (const b of bytes) out.push(b); // raw forward
    });
  },
};
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The six example sessions, and the SDK they import**

`mgb-smoke`, `analyze-mgb` and `export-mgb-channels` are mgb's, `export-nes-channels` and `export-nes-mono` are
mesen's, and `analyze-lsdj-sync` is lsdj's; `render-rom`, `render-song` and `rom-test` stay in `cli/sessions`. Each
package lists its sessions in `retroplug.examples` and declares `retroplug.host: ["retroplug-cli"]`, each example
imports `retroplug-cli` by the bare specifier, and `tools/build-session.js` marks it external (the binary serves it
from its loaded-module table, as it does for a test). `retroplug_examples()` in `cmake/packages.cmake` reads the
manifests and builds each to the same `build/cli/<name>.js`, skipping an empty list and refusing a duplicate name once
the shell's three are appended; the shell's own `tsconfig.json` includes `../*/examples` and extends the generated
paths.

````diff
diff --git a/cmake/packages.cmake b/cmake/packages.cmake
index 422dd2a5d..df136fb5f 100644
--- a/cmake/packages.cmake
+++ b/cmake/packages.cmake
@@ -2234,3 +2234,34 @@ function(_retroplug_entry_declarations out)
     endforeach()
     set(${out} "${_decls}" PARENT_SCOPE)
 endfunction()
+
+# retroplug_examples(<names-out> <entries-out>): every package's example sessions, in product order, from the manifests'
+# `retroplug.examples` lists (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 5.3). The first output holds the names the
+# sessions run as (the .js file's stem), the second their TypeScript entries, so a caller zips the two lists. A package
+# in the product list with no examples member contributes nothing; the shell's own sessions are not a package's and are
+# named by the target itself.
+function(retroplug_examples names_out entries_out)
+    set(_names "")
+    set(_entries "")
+    foreach(_package IN LISTS RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES)
+        set(_manifest "${RP_PACKAGES_DIR}/${_package}/package.json")
+        file(READ "${_manifest}" _json)
+        string(JSON _type ERROR_VARIABLE _err TYPE "${_json}" retroplug examples)
+        if(NOT _err STREQUAL "NOTFOUND")
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        string(JSON _count LENGTH "${_json}" retroplug examples)
+        if(_count EQUAL 0)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        math(EXPR _last "${_count} - 1")
+        foreach(_i RANGE ${_last})
+            string(JSON _name GET "${_json}" retroplug examples ${_i} name)
+            string(JSON _entry GET "${_json}" retroplug examples ${_i} entry)
+            list(APPEND _names "${_name}")
+            list(APPEND _entries "${RP_PACKAGES_DIR}/${_package}/${_entry}")
+        endforeach()
+    endforeach()
+    set(${names_out} "${_names}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+    set(${entries_out} "${_entries}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+endfunction()
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The host-module list, rule 3, and the generator's two paths files**

`host-modules.json` (module, surface, provider, declaration file) is the one list; rule 3 accepts a bare specifier on
it when the importing package's manifest declares it in `retroplug.host`, refuses one it does not declare, refuses a
declared name the list lacks, warns about a declaration nothing imports, walks `ts/` plus `examples/`, and - the last
pass's controller decision - refuses a host module imported from a file its surface does not own (`surfaceOf` reads
the file's own directory: `examples/**` and `ts/cli/**` are `cli`, `ts/ui/**` is `ui`). The generator writes
`tsconfig.host-modules.json` and `tsconfig.paths.json` (the same entries plus `tsconfig.aliases.json`'s `ui-harness`),
refuses an examples package whose parsed `extends` does not name the first, refuses an example outside `examples/` and
a name two packages share, and the root `typecheck` script runs the generator first so a fresh checkout typechecks.

Create `packages/retroplug/host-modules.json`:

````json
[
  {
    "module": "retroplug-cli",
    "surface": "cli",
    "provider": "the retroplug-cli binary's loaded-module table",
    "types": "cli/sdk-types.d.ts"
  }
]
````

````diff
-  "compilerOptions": {

-    // tsconfig does. Nothing in the app imports it; it exists so cli/sdkSurfaceCheck.ts can be
-    // type-checked against the .d.ts, which is hand-maintained and has twice shipped out of step
-    // with the implementation it describes.
-    "paths": {
-      "retroplug-cli": ["./cli/sdk-types.d.ts"],
-      // The alias scripts/run-ui-tests.mjs gives esbuild. Without it the 37 test-ui files cannot be
-      // type-checked at all, which is why they were excluded - and therefore never checked.
-      "ui-harness": ["./test-ui/uiHarness.ts"]
-    }
-  },
+  // options are tsconfig.base.json's (the same ones each package's tsconfig extends); the paths are the generated
+  // file's, which carries both the host modules a package imports through its surface's host (`retroplug-cli` today,
+  // from host-modules.json) and the one alias the UI tests use (from tsconfig.aliases.json). The runtime's ambient
+  // globals come from the base's `files`.
+  "extends": ["../../tsconfig.base.json", "./tsconfig.paths.json"],
   // The shell's own trees, and every workspace package's TS half by one glob, so a package added to the workspace is
   // type-checked without an entry here: its own ts/ tree, sources and ts/test alike. packages/native's device-mode
   // fixture packs stay listed (they are fixtures of a native test, not a package).
-  "include": ["src", "testing", "test", "test-native", "test-ui", "cli", "tools-src", "../*/ts",
+  "include": ["src", "testing", "test", "test-native", "test-ui", "cli", "tools-src", "../*/ts", "../*/examples",
               "../native/test/device-mode/script-packs"],
   // The package generator's and the boundary check's fixture trees: data they read (and the generator writes), laid out
   // as a workspace root and its packages are, not modules of this program (their imports name a fixture tree's files,
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The recorded help and index, and the tests that follow**

`recorded-help.json` is 13 tools' name, summary and whole `--help` text, captured from the OLD binary before anything
moved, and `recorded-index.json` is the old index verbatim. `test/cli/cli.test.ts` gains three cases: every tool's
summary and help equal the record, `topLevelHelp` equals the index rebuilt from those rows in the registry's order
(failing for a row the record lacks or a tool no row answers to), and `composeTools`' clash refusal. The four native
tool tests pass `cliHost(session)` to `run` - the signature moved, so the call site did, and no assertion changed.
`test/cli/n8Play.test.ts` is a `git mv` into `n8/ts/test`. `test/hosts/host-groups.test.ts` gains the CLI host's
argument vector cases.
