````json
    "summary": "Strip and run a directory of TypeScript test files",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli test <dir> [name-filter] [options] [-- session-args...]\n\nStrip and run every *.test.ts in <dir>. Each file runs in its own process (a fresh Engine and a fresh\nconfig dir), and the exit code is nonzero if any file fails, so this is a real pass/fail gate.\n\n  <dir>             directory of *.test.ts / *.test.js files\n  [name-filter]     only run files whose name contains this substring\n\noptions:\n  --rom <path>      passed to every test file as its first argument\n  --out <dir>       where to write stripped output (default: <dir>'s sibling .rp-test-build, or a\n                    directory under the temp dir when that sibling is not writable)\n  --jobs N, -j N    run N files at once (default: half the logical cores; also RP_TEST_JOBS).\n                    -j1 runs them one at a time and streams each child's output live.\n  -- <args...>      extra arguments appended to every test file's argv\n\nTypeScript is stripped, not compiled: only erasable syntax is supported. enum, namespace and\nconstructor parameter properties emit runtime code and are rejected with a file:line:col error.\n\nexample:\n  retroplug-cli test tests --rom rom/build/bliptoaster.nes\n  retroplug-cli test tests pulse --rom rom/build/bliptoaster.nes"
  },
  {
    "name": "run",
    "summary": "Strip and run a single TypeScript session file",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli run <session.ts> [args...]\n\nStrip and run a single TypeScript session file. Everything after the path is passed to the session as\nits arguments (read with hostArgs()).\n\n  --out <dir>   where to write stripped output (default: the session dir's sibling .rp-test-build; when\n                that is not writable - a file straight under /tmp has \"/\" for a sibling - a directory\n                under the temp dir is used instead, and the run says so)\n\nTypeScript is stripped, not compiled: only erasable syntax is supported. enum, namespace and\nconstructor parameter properties are rejected with a file:line:col error.\n\nexample:\n  retroplug-cli run repro/verify-pitch.ts rom/build/bliptoaster.nes"
  },
  {
    "name": "render",
    "summary": "Render a ROM/SAV to a WAV file (full mix or per-channel stems)",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli render <rom> [options]\n\nRender a Game Boy (.gb/.gbc), GBA (.gba), NES (.nes), Master System (.sms) or Game Gear (.gg) ROM to a WAV file. The ROM is booted and its audio\nis written to disk. Play is pressed so a song begins (use --no-start to capture raw boot audio): a cart's\nown gesture where it has one (risa's SELECT+START, smsggdj's Pause), else its console's default (a Game\nBoy's Start, which starts LSDj and leaves mGB alone - it plays from incoming MIDI). The song length is\nauto-detected (rendered up to the cart's end of song) for a ROM whose cart has a probe (LSDj on a Game\nBoy, risa on a NES) - its battery need not be beside it - unless you pin a fixed length with --duration.\n\nsmsggdj (.sms/.gg) differs twice. It boots to a BLANK song by design - it keeps no working song in its\nbattery - so --song/--song-index is REQUIRED or the render is silence. And its songs loop forever: H is\na phrase hop, nothing in its command set stops the transport, and a track that reaches the end of its\ncolumn loops back to the top of its block. There is no HFF-style stop to detect, so --duration is\nrequired too, or you get the full --max-duration cap.\n\nDurations accept a unit: 500ms, 3s, 2m (decimals ok, e.g. 1.5s); a bare number is milliseconds.\n\nArguments:\n  <rom>                  Path to the ROM. A sibling <rom>.sav is loaded automatically if present.\n\nOptions:\n  --sav <file>           Battery save (.sav) to load. Default: <rom>.sav next to the ROM, if it exists.\n  --state <file>         Savestate to restore after boot (instead of a fresh boot).\n  --out <file>           Output path. Default: the working/selected song's name for a tracker cart, else\n                         the ROM name; <name>.wav for a mix, <name>_<channel>.wav for --split.\n  --duration <time>      Fixed render length (e.g. 3s, 500ms, 2m). Turns OFF song-length auto-detection.\n                         Default: auto for an LSDj / risa ROM, otherwise the --max-duration cap (10m).\n                         smsggdj songs have no end, so pin this for any .sms/.gg render.\n  --max-duration <time>  Safety cap for song-length auto-detect when no HFF stop is found. Default: 10m.\n  --sample-rate <hz>     Output sample rate. Default: 44100. Higher rates resample the console's audio up\n                         (larger WAV, same song); must be set before the ROM boots (it always is here).\n  --split <mode>         What to write (default: mix):\n                           mix       one WAV of the final mix (Game Boy: stereo; NES: mono)\n                           channels  one WAV per sound channel (Game Boy: 4 stereo stems;\n                                     NES: 5 mono core channels: square1/2, triangle, noise, dmc)\n                           pins      NES analog output pins: pulse, tnd, expansion (3 mono WAVs)\n  --bpm <n>              Host tempo (BPM) for tempo-synced playback. Use with --transport.\n  --transport            Run the host transport (play), so tempo-synced ROMs advance. Default: off.\n  --no-start             Do NOT press Start on boot; render the raw boot/menu audio.\n  --song <name>          LSDj / risa / smsggdj: play a saved song, by name (case-insensitive). LSDj and\n                         risa promote it to the working song in the battery before boot; smsggdj has no\n                         working song in its battery, so it is written into the booted cart's work RAM.\n  --song-index <0-31>    The same, by slot number instead of by name.\n  --list-songs           LSDj / risa / smsggdj: print the sav's saved song names and exit (renders nothing).\n  -h, --help             Show this help and exit.\n\nExamples:\n  retroplug-cli render song.gbc                          # LSDj: auto-length stereo mix -> song.wav\n  retroplug-cli render song.gbc --split channels         # 4 per-channel stereo stems\n  retroplug-cli render song.gbc --song INTRO --out intro.wav\n  retroplug-cli render game.nes --split channels --duration 5s   # NES core channels, fixed 5s\n  retroplug-cli render song.gbc --sample-rate 96000      # render at 96 kHz\n  retroplug-cli render smsggdj.sms --sav set.sav --song DEMO --duration 30s   # smsggdj: both flags needed"
  },
  {
    "name": "lsdj-rom",
    "summary": "inspect / extract / metadata-patch LSDj ROM kits, palettes and fonts",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli lsdj-rom <subcommand> ...\n\n  info           <rom> [--json]                     version + kit/palette/font inventory\n  extract        <rom> <outDir> [--rate N]          dump each kit sample to a mono WAV + rom.json\n  patch          <rom> <manifest.json> <out>        realize a manifest (builds/imports/metadata)\n  build-kit      <kit.json> <out.kit> [--no-rotate] compile a .kit from a (slotless) kit entry\n  import-sample  <rom> <kit> <audio> [flags]        compile one sample + splice into a kit\n  remove-sample  <rom> <kit> <slot> [--out]         drop a sample from a kit\n  export-palette <rom> <index> <out.lsdpal>         write palette <index> to a .lsdpal\n  import-palette <rom> <in.lsdpal> <index> [--out]  import a .lsdpal into palette <index>\n  export-font    <rom> <index> <out.png> [--gfx]    write font <index> to a .png (--gfx = extended)\n  import-font    <rom> <in.png> <index> [--out]     import a .png into font <index>\n  export-kit     <rom> <index> <out.kit>            write kit <index>'s 16 KB bank to a .kit\n  import-kit     <rom> <in.kit> <index> [--out]     import a .kit bank into kit <index>\n  (asset files are the community lsdpatch formats; font --gfx = the 46 shared extended tiles, 64x120)\n\nimport-sample / build-kit effect flags: --gain X  --no-normalize\n                     --dither HighPassTPDF|ShapedTPDF|ErrorDiffusion|JJN|SierraLite  --no-dither\n                     --filter LowPass|HighPass|\u2026  --cutoff HZ  --q Q\n                     (--cutoff defaults to 5734 Hz; a source at or below 11468 Hz is refused without a lower --cutoff)\n\nONE schema for patch (whole ROM) and build-kit (a single, slotless kit entry). Every entry\neither BUILDS/IMPORTS from a file or TWEAKS metadata; `slot` = the asset index.\n  { \"kits\":     [{ \"slot\": 20, \"name\": \"DRUMS\", \"build\": [\"kick.wav\", {\"file\":\"sn.wav\",\"name\":\"SN\"}] },\n                 { \"slot\": 30, \"file\": \"DONK.kit\" },\n                 { \"slot\": 5,  \"name\": \"RENAMED\", \"samples\": [{ \"index\": 0, \"name\": \"BD\" }] }],\n    \"palettes\": [{ \"slot\": 1, \"file\": \"x.lsdpal\" }, { \"slot\": 0, \"set\": 0, \"color\": 0, \"rgb\": [255,0,0] }],\n    \"fonts\":    [{ \"slot\": 0, \"file\": \"x.png\" }, { \"slot\": 1, \"tile\": 3, \"pixels\": [ /* 64 */ ] }] }\nbuild-kit takes ONE kit entry without a slot, e.g.\n  { \"name\": \"MYKIT\", \"build\": [{ \"file\": \"kick.wav\", \"name\": \"BD\" }, \"snare.wav\"] }   \u2192 then import-kit\n  (build source: a path string, or { file, name?, offset?, length?, effects? })"
  },
  {
    "name": "risa-rom",
    "summary": "inspect / extract / metadata-patch risa ROM kits, themes and fonts",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli risa-rom <subcommand> ...\n\n  info          <rom> [--json]                     theme / font / kit inventory\n  extract       <rom> <outDir> [--rate N]          dump each kit sample to a mono WAV + themes/fonts + rom.json\n  patch         <rom> <manifest.json> <out>        realize a manifest (builds/imports/metadata)\n  build-kit     <kit.json> <out.rkit> [flags]      compile a .rkit from a (slotless) kit entry\n  import-sample <rom> <kit> <audio> [flags]        compile one sample + splice into a kit\n  remove-sample <rom> <kit> <slot> [--out]         empty a kit slot (index preserved)\n  export-theme  <rom> <index> <out.rit>            write theme <index> to a .rit (palette-role JSON)\n  import-theme  <rom> <in.rit> <index> [--out]     import a .rit into theme <index>\n  export-font   <rom> <index> <out.chr>            write font <index>'s 8 KB CHR bank to a .chr\n  import-font   <rom> <in.chr> <index> [--out]     import a .chr bank into font <index>\n  export-kit    <rom> <index> <out.rkit>           write kit <index>'s 8 KB DPCM bank to a .rkit\n  import-kit    <rom> <in.rkit> <index> [--out]    import a .rkit bank into kit <index>\n  (themes are risa's .rit palette-role JSON; fonts are raw 8 KB NES CHR banks; kits are 8 KB DPCM banks)\n\nbuild-kit / import-sample flags:  --rate N (PAL DPCM index 0-15, default 12)  --loop  --no-normalize\n                     --gain X  --filter LowPass|HighPass|...  --cutoff HZ  --q Q   (no dither; DMC is 1-bit)\n\nONE schema for patch (whole ROM) and build-kit (a single, slotless kit entry). Every entry either\nBUILDS/IMPORTS from a file or TWEAKS metadata; `slot` = the asset index.\n  { \"kits\":   [{ \"slot\": 0, \"name\": \"DRUMS\", \"build\": [\"kick.wav\", {\"file\":\"sn.wav\",\"name\":\"SN\",\"rate\":12}] },\n               { \"slot\": 1, \"file\": \"HAT.rkit\" },\n               { \"slot\": 2, \"name\": \"RENAMED\", \"samples\": [{ \"index\": 0, \"name\": \"BD\" }] }],\n    \"themes\": [{ \"slot\": 0, \"file\": \"dark.rit\" }],\n    \"fonts\":  [{ \"slot\": 0, \"file\": \"big.chr\" }] }\nbuild-kit takes ONE kit entry without a slot, e.g.\n  { \"name\": \"MYKIT\", \"build\": [{ \"file\": \"kick.wav\", \"name\": \"BD\", \"rate\": 12 }, \"snare.wav\"] }   \u2192 then import-kit\n  (build source: a path string, or { file, name?, rate?, loop?, normalize?, offset?, length?, effects? })"
  },
  {
    "name": "bliptoaster-rom",
    "summary": "inspect / extract / edit BlipToaster ROM kits, theme and font (+ compile WAV \u2192 .rkit)",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli bliptoaster-rom <subcommand> ...\n\n  info          <rom> [--json]                     theme / font / kit inventory + baked settings\n  settings      <rom> [field flags] [--out <nes>]  print or patch the baked rig settings (no flags = print)\n  extract       <rom> <outDir> [--rate N]          dump each kit sample to a mono WAV + theme/font + rom.json\n  patch         <rom> <manifest.json> <out>        realize a manifest (builds/imports/metadata)\n  build-kit     <kit.json> <out.rkit> [flags]      compile a .rkit from a (slotless) kit entry\n  import-sample <rom> <kit> <audio> [flags]        compile one sample + splice into a kit\n  remove-sample <rom> <kit> <slot> [--out]         empty a kit slot (index preserved)\n  export-theme  <rom> <index> <out.rit>            write theme <index> to a .rit (palette-role JSON)\n  import-theme  <rom> <in.rit> <index> [--out]     import a .rit into theme <index>\n  export-font   <rom> <index> <out.chr>            write font <index>'s 8 KB CHR bank to a .chr\n  import-font   <rom> <in.chr> <index> [--out]     import a .chr bank into font <index>\n  export-kit    <rom> <index> <out.rkit>           write kit <index>'s 8 KB DPCM bank to a .rkit\n  import-kit    <rom> <in.rkit> <index> [--out]    import a .rkit bank into kit <index>\n  (themes are risa's .rit palette-role JSON; fonts are raw 8 KB NES CHR banks; kits are 8 KB DPCM banks)\n  (kit <index> is a switchable ROM bank: 0 on NROM, 0..15 on a banking build \u2014 see `info`)\n\nsettings flags (each optional; only the ones given are written):\n  --base-channel 1-16   the cart's base MIDI channel (BASE01..BASE16)\n  --kit 0-15            the DMC kit bank ch5 plays out of at boot\n  --ppu on|off          draw the screen at boot (off = dark until START, the old Mode 1)\n  --mode1 on|off        DEPRECATED alias for the INVERSE of --ppu (the byte's meaning flipped)\n  --curve linear|log    the velocity curve on every channel (the VRC7 build has none)\n  --theme 0-15          the colour theme the screen comes up in\n  --font 0-3            the CHR font the screen comes up in\n  Each is a BOOT default, not a lock: the cart's own CCs (14/15/16/17) still move it live, and the next\n  cold boot returns to the baked value. RetroPlug's BlipToaster > Settings submenu edits the same block\n  non-destructively (pinned in the project, folded into the ROM in memory) instead of writing the file.\n\nbuild-kit / import-sample flags:  --rate N (PAL DPCM index 0-15, default 12)  --loop  --no-normalize\n                     --gain X  --filter LowPass|HighPass|\u2026  --cutoff HZ  --q Q   (no dither \u2014 DMC is 1-bit)\n\nONE schema for patch (whole ROM) and build-kit (a single, slotless kit entry). Every entry either\nBUILDS/IMPORTS from a file or TWEAKS metadata; `slot` = the asset index.\n  { \"kits\":   [{ \"slot\": 0, \"name\": \"DRUMS\", \"build\": [\"kick.wav\", {\"file\":\"sn.wav\",\"name\":\"SN\",\"rate\":12}] },\n               { \"slot\": 1, \"file\": \"HAT.rkit\" },\n               { \"slot\": 2, \"name\": \"RENAMED\", \"samples\": [{ \"index\": 0, \"name\": \"BD\" }] }],\n    \"themes\": [{ \"slot\": 0, \"file\": \"dark.rit\" }],\n    \"fonts\":  [{ \"slot\": 0, \"file\": \"big.chr\" }],\n    \"settings\": { \"theme\": 11, \"font\": 2, \"kit\": 3, \"baseChannel\": 3, \"ppu\": true, \"velCurve\": false } }\n  (\"settings\" is not per-slot - it is the one baked block, and only the fields named are written)\nbuild-kit takes ONE kit entry without a slot, e.g.\n  { \"name\": \"MYKIT\", \"build\": [{ \"file\": \"kick.wav\", \"name\": \"BD\", \"rate\": 12 }, \"snare.wav\"] }   \u2192 then import-kit\n  (build source: a path string, or { file, name?, rate?, loop?, normalize?, offset?, length?, effects? })"
  },
  {
    "name": "n8-load",
    "summary": "load + boot a ROM on a physical Everdrive N8 Pro over USB (menu-driven)",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli n8-load [options] [<rom.nes>]\n\n  Load + boot a ROM on a physical Everdrive N8 Pro over USB by driving its on-device menu. The N8\n  firmware parses the ROM and sources the mapper core from its own SD, so no low-level FPGA/mapper\n  work happens here. Auto-detects the N8 (VID:PID 38df:0017).\n\n  <rom.nes>          upload this local ROM to usb-games/ and boot it (default: resources/roms/bliptoaster.nes)\n  --sd-path <path>   instead, boot a ROM already on the N8 SD card by its SD path\n  --srm <save.srm>   restore this battery save on boot (written to EDN8/gamedata/<rom>/bram.srm)\n  --sram-only        with --srm: write the save STRAIGHT to cart SRAM (a running game; no reboot).\n                     WARNING: corrupts the menu if run on the file browser\n  --dump-sram <file> read the cart SRAM (64 KB game region) out to <file> (no ROM, no reboot)\n  --ls <path>        list an SD-card directory (use \"/\" for root) and exit\n  --get-file <sd-path> <local-dest>  read an SD-card file over USB to a local file (no reboot)\n  --put-file <local-src> <sd-path>   write a local file to the SD card over USB (no reboot). Creates\n                     missing parent directories. The way to put a DATA file on the card - unlike --srm,\n                     which lands in the fixed 64 KB per-game save slot\n  --screenshot <out.png>  capture the N8 MENU screen over USB to a PNG (the menu must be showing)\n  --sniff            read a RUNNING game's live APU/PPU/OAM state over USB and print it (a game must\n                     be running - the sniffer is off at the menu)\n  --pal              with --sniff: decode the APU timers at the PAL CPU clock (1.6626 MHz) instead of\n                     NTSC. The sniffer cannot tell the region; on a PAL console the NTSC decode reads\n                     7.6% high (440 Hz shows as 474)\n  --sniff-raw <file> dump the raw 512-byte sniffer region to a file (no decode)\n  --dump-chr <file>  read the running game's 8 KB visible CHR bank over USB. A .png dest renders an\n                     editable grayscale tile grid; else a raw 8 KB .chr. Needs a RUNNING game - at the\n                     menu the CHR chip holds the N8 OS font, so this errors instead of returning it\n  --chr-bank <n>     with --dump-chr / --patch-chr: pick the 8 KB CHR bank by number instead of the one\n                     the live mapper registers say is on screen. Required on a multi-bank cart whose\n                     mapper isn't decoded here (the error lists the range)\n  --color [--palette N]  with --dump-chr <.png>: render the game's REAL colours via the live sniffer\n                     palette (BG palette group N, 0-3). A viewing aid\n  --patch-chr <hex-offset> <file>  live-patch the running game's CHR (graphics) from <file>, at an offset\n                     into the SAME visible 8 KB bank --dump-chr returns (verified; shows on-screen next\n                     frame). <file> = a .png tile grid or raw .chr bytes. Works on CHR-ROM and CHR-RAM,\n                     though a CHR-RAM game may overwrite the patch itself on its next redraw\n  --patch-prg <hex-offset> <file>  live-patch the running game's PRG (code) from raw <file> at PRG+offset.\n                     WARNING: a bad code patch can crash the game (power-cycle to recover)\n  --info             print the N8's device info (serial, firmware/bootloader versions, NES/Famicom form\n                     factor, flash size, voltages) over USB\n  --df               print the SD card's free space\n  --mkdir <path>     create a directory on the SD card\n  --rm <path>        delete a file or empty directory on the SD card (PERMANENT)\n  --savestate <sd-path>  read + decode an N8 save-state (EDN8/gamedata/<rom>/NN.SAV): the full captured\n                     state - CPU regs, WRAM, APU/PPU, CHR - that the live --sniff can't reach\n  --show-song        decode the live cart battery (risa/LSDj) and print its songs\n  --serial <port>    use this serial port (default: auto-detect the N8)\n\n  Run load from the N8 file-browser menu. If a load fails with 'out of memory' (a dirty menu heap\n  after a prior failed load), power-cycle the console to a fresh menu and retry.\n\n  HAZARD - reading CART memory takes the bus off the console. Every option that touches PRG / CHR /\n  SRM (--dump-chr, --patch-chr, --patch-prg, --dump-sram, --show-song) is a USB DMA, and the FPGA\n  hands that memory controller to the DMA for the WHOLE command (edn8-pro-pub everdrive.sv:\n  `chr = dma.req_chr ? dma.mem : mao.chr`, and the PPU reads 0x00 meanwhile). A timing-sensitive\n  game can fail to survive that - measured on a mapper-30 CHR-RAM ROM, where a single 16-byte read\n  is enough to wedge it until a power-cycle, while an NROM CHR-ROM game is unaffected. Reads of the\n  SYSTEM region are NOT a DMA and never touch the cart bus, so --sniff / --info are always safe;\n  prefer them for polling a running game.\n\n  There is no --to-menu: a RUNNING game cannot be returned to the menu over USB. The N8's menu\n  commands ('t'/'n'/'s'/'r') are answered by the N8 OS, which is not running while a game is, and\n  the cartridge has no way to reset the console - the FPGA only DETECTS a reset (the CPU clock\n  stopping) and switches to the OS mapper on it. So loading a second ROM takes the console's reset\n  button or a power-cycle (/workspaces/.nes-power.sh reset, then ~35 s for the menu)."
  },
  {
    "name": "n8-bridge",
    "summary": "stream live MIDI to a physical Everdrive N8 Pro over USB",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli n8-bridge [--list] [--midi-in <name>] [--serial <port>] [--lookahead-ms <N>]\n\n  Stream live MIDI straight to a physical Everdrive N8 Pro's cart FIFO over USB, so a controller / DAW\n  plays the real NES (for the BlipToaster ROM). Runs until Ctrl-C.\n\n  --list             list the available MIDI input ports and exit\n  --midi-in <name>   forward from this MIDI input (default: all hardware inputs)\n  --serial <port>    use this serial port (default: auto-detect the N8, VID:PID 38df:0017)\n  --lookahead-ms <N> delay every message by N ms (constant-delay smoothing; default 0 = immediate)"
  },
  {
    "name": "n8-sync",
    "summary": "drive risa host-sync on a physical Everdrive N8 Pro from a MIDI clock",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli n8-sync [--list] [--midi-in <name>] [--serial <port>] [--lookahead-ms <N>]\n\n  Turn an incoming MIDI clock/transport (Start/Continue/Stop + 24-PPQN clock, optional Song Position)\n  into risa's host-sync protocol on a physical N8, so a risa cart plays locked to the DAW. Runs until\n  Ctrl-C. Load a risa ROM first (retroplug-cli n8-load).\n\n  --list             list the available MIDI input ports and exit\n  --midi-in <name>   forward from this MIDI input (default: all hardware inputs)\n  --serial <port>    use this serial port (default: auto-detect the N8, VID:PID 38df:0017)\n  --lookahead-ms <N> delay every message by N ms (constant-delay smoothing; default 0 = immediate)"
  },
  {
    "name": "n8-play",
    "summary": "play a scripted MIDI sequence on a physical Everdrive N8 Pro (no MIDI hardware needed)",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli n8-play [--serial <port>] [--exp-vol <0-255> | --rom <rom.nes>] [--prime off] <step>...\n\n  Sends a fixed MIDI sequence to the N8's cart FIFO, which the BlipToaster ROM reads at $40F0/$40F1.\n  The scripted twin of n8-bridge: reproducible hardware checks with no controller attached.\n\nsteps (MIDI channels are 1-based, matching the BlipToaster monitor's CH column):\n  on:<ch>:<note>[:<vel>]   note on  (velocity defaults to 100)\n  off:<ch>:<note>          note off\n  cc:<ch>:<num>:<val>      control change\n  wait:<ms>                hold for <ms> before the next step\n  raw:<hex,hex,...>        these bytes, verbatim (raw:ff is the panic byte; raw:f0,7d,42,02,f7 a SysEx)\n  sysex:<hex,hex,...>      a SysEx payload (7-bit, manufacturer id first) wrapped in F0..F7\n  file:<path>              the bytes of a file, verbatim (what retroplug-n8-hwtest fifowr sends)\n\noptions:\n  --serial <port>    use this serial port (default: auto-detect the N8, VID:PID 38df:0017)\n  --exp-vol <0-255>  set the FPGA expansion-audio master volume first (0 mute, 128 unity, 255 2x).\n                     REQUIRED for expansion chips (VRC6/VRC7/N163/S5B/MMC5) - at 0 they are silent\n                     however correct the ROM is. Live-only: it applies to the running cart.\n  --rom <rom.nes>    the ROM that is running: defaults --exp-vol to 128 when its mapper carries\n                     expansion audio (5, 19, 24, 26, 69, 85) and leaves it alone otherwise. With\n                     neither flag the register is left as it was, and the run warns about it.\n  --prime off        skip the priming CC (BlipToaster drops its first message after boot)\n\n  Nothing is reset between invocations: a note held by one call keeps sounding through the next,\n  so a check can hold a note with one command and push a SysEx (or a capture) with another.\n\nexample - hold a 2 s A4 on the S5B's Square A with the hardware envelope on:\n  retroplug-cli n8-play --exp-vol 128 \\\n      cc:6:29:80 cc:6:28:64 cc:6:20:127 on:6:69 wait:2000 off:6:69\nexample - upload a flat wave to the N163 build while a note is held from an earlier call:\n  retroplug-cli n8-play --rom build/bliptoaster-n163.nes --prime off \\\n      sysex:7d,42,01,00,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08,08"
  },
  {
    "name": "analyze-capture",
    "summary": "measure a hardware audio capture: level, pitch, envelope swing, band energy",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli analyze-capture <capture.wav> [--channel N] [--expect-hz F] [--band lo:hi] [--floor dB]\n\n  Reports what a real console actually produced, from a WAV captured off its analog output.\n  With no --channel it surveys every channel's level (find which input the console is on);\n  with --channel it reports that channel in full.\n\noptions:\n  --channel N     analyse this 1-based channel (else: level survey of all channels)\n  --expect-hz F   also report the error in cents vs this frequency\n  --band lo:hi    report the energy in a band, e.g. --band 4000:12000 for noise/hiss content\n  --shape         report duty (fraction above zero) + crest (peak/rms): tells a clean square at a\n                  new pitch apart from a duty-skewed / truncated one, which rms alone cannot\n  --env-rate      also report how FAST the amplitude repeats (Hz) - swing shows an envelope is\n                  running, this shows a speed control changing it (rate moves, swing does not)\n  --trim a:b      analyse only seconds a..b (measure the SUSTAIN, not the attack/release)\n  --floor dB      the silence floor for the envelope stats AND the pitch (default -70; a quiet NES\n                  capture idles near -76 dBFS, so anything above -70 is really sounding). A window\n                  under the floor reports 'pitch: silent' - the detector would otherwise read the\n                  noise floor itself as a confident tone (750 Hz at confidence 1.00 on an idle input)\n\n  The envelope swing is what distinguishes a HARDWARE volume envelope (Sunsoft 5B CC20/28/29)\n  from a flat tone - both have the same average level, so RMS alone cannot tell them apart.\n\nexample - was the S5B note pulsing, and in tune?\n  retroplug-cli analyze-capture /tmp/s5b.wav --channel 3 --expect-hz 440"
  },
  {
    "name": "grab-frame",
    "summary": "grab one NES video frame off the USB capture card as a PNG (warm-up frames discarded)",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli grab-frame <out.png> [--device /dev/video0] [--size 720x576] [--standard PAL]\n                                [--frames 30] [--retries 2] [--fail-on-black]\n\n  Runs ffmpeg for a run of frames, keeps the LAST one, decodes it and measures it. The capture\n  card's first frames after it is opened (and for a while after a power-cycle) are flat black with\n  no error - indistinguishable from a console showing nothing - so a black result is retried with\n  a longer run and, if it stays black, reported as such instead of handed back as the screen.\n\noptions:\n  --device <node>    the V4L2 capture node (default /dev/video0)\n  --size WxH         the capture size (default 720x576, the card's PAL mode; NTSC is 720x480)\n  --standard STD     the video standard to request (default PAL)\n  --frames N         frames to grab before keeping one (default 30 - ~1.2 s, past the warm-up)\n  --retries N        how many times to double N on a black frame (default 2)\n  --fail-on-black    exit 1 when the frame is still black after the retries (default: exit 0 + warn)\n\nexample:\n  retroplug-cli grab-frame /tmp/nes.png && <read /tmp/nes.png>"
  },
  {
    "name": "launchpad-probe",
    "summary": "drive a real Novation Launchpad and report what it sends back",
    "help": "usage: retroplug-cli launchpad-probe [--list] [--loopback] [--in <name>] [--out <name>] [--seconds N]\n\n  Drive a real Novation Launchpad with RetroPlug's own protocol layer: enter Programmer mode, paint a\n  test pattern, and report every press decoded through the device profile. Use it to confirm the grid\n  mapping and the edge-button CC numbers against hardware. Returns the device to Live mode on exit.\n\n  --list          list the MIDI input + output ports (marking any that match the Pro MK3) and exit\n  --loopback      self-test with NO device: send a whole-surface bulk-LED sysex out of our own virtual\n                  port and check it arrives intact (the caller wires output->input; see\n                  tools/run-launchpad-loopback.sh)\n  --in <name>     read from this MIDI input   (default: the port matching \"LPProMK3 MIDI\")\n  --out <name>    light this MIDI output      (default: the same)\n  --sweep         light each named edge button in turn (one per second) so you can read off which\n                  physical button each name actually addresses - the map check without pressing anything\n  --verbose       also print MIDI clock and other realtime bytes (the device free-runs a clock, so this\n                  is hundreds of lines a second - off by default)\n  --seconds <N>   how long to listen before restoring Live mode (default 60)"
  }
]
````

````diff
@@ -33,3 +46,45 @@ test("cli: the real registry exposes risa-rom with build-kit / theme / kit subco
   expect(risa!.help.includes("import-kit")).toBeTruthy();
   expect(topLevelHelp(tools, "RetroPlug v0.0.0").includes("risa-rom")).toBeTruthy(); // auto-appears in the index
 });
+
+test("cli: every tool's summary and help are the recorded ones", () => {
+  // Recorded from the pre-F4b binary (`recorded-help.json`), which printed each tool's own help text, so a move either
+  // changed a byte a user reads or did not. The index's order is E1's one change; the lines themselves are not.
+  const recorded = recordedHelp as { name: string; summary: string; help: string }[];
+  expect(tools.length).toBe(recorded.length);
+  for (const want of recorded) {
+    const tool = tools.find((t) => t.name === want.name);
+    expect(tool !== undefined, want.name).toBe(true);
+    expect(tool!.summary, want.name).toEqual(want.summary);
+    expect(tool!.help, want.name).toEqual(want.help);
+  }
+});
+
+test("cli: the whole command index is the recorded rows, in the registry's order", () => {
+  // `recorded-index.json` is the pre-F4b binary's index exactly as it printed it, kept verbatim so the record stays a
+  // recording. E1's one change is the order, which the names test above pins; rebuilding the index from the record in
+  // the registry's order holds every row's own text (the columns included) to what the old binary printed, and fails
+  // for a row the record lacks or one no tool answers to. Taken at v0.8.0, the version the recording was made at.
+  const lines = recordedIndex.split("\n");
+  const isRow = (line: string): boolean => /^ {2}\S/.test(line);
+  const first = lines.findIndex(isRow);
+  const last = lines.length - 1 - [...lines].reverse().findIndex(isRow);
+  const rowOf = new Map(lines.filter(isRow).map((line) => [line.trim().split(/\s+/)[0], line]));
+  const rows = tools.map((tool) => {
+    const row = rowOf.get(tool.name);
+    expect(row !== undefined, tool.name).toBe(true);
+    return row!;
+  });
+  // Every recorded row is one a tool answers to, so no row can sit unused in the record.
+  expect(rowOf.size).toBe(tools.length);
+  expect([...lines.slice(0, first), ...rows, ...lines.slice(last + 1)].join("\n")).toEqual(
+    topLevelHelp(tools, "RetroPlug v0.8.0"),
+  );
+});
+
+test("cli: a contributed tool whose name a shell tool has is refused", () => {
+  // The dispatcher finds the first tool by name, so a package's `render` would be shadowed silently.
+  expect(() => composeTools([fakeTool("render", "shell")], [fakeTool("render", "package")])).toThrow(
+    "a package declares the CLI tool render, which the shell already has",
+  );
+});
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf build-box/pio/n8_host.elf build-box/native/n8_host.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f4b-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f4b-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f4b-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f4b-img.bin'`

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(f4b): the CLI tools and the example sessions, and the host modules

The last surface the shell still hard-coded: seven cart and device subcommands in `cli/sessions`
and six example sessions that named a cart, beside the shell's own five tools.

The tool contract. `core/ts/cliTool.ts` defines `CliTool` (name, summary, help, longRunning,
`run(host, args)`), `defineCliTools` and the CLI host's groups; a package names a module in its
manifest's new `retroplug.cli`, and the generator writes `packages/retroplug/cli/generated/
tools.ts` from them in product order, refusing a tool name two packages declare at load. The
shell's `cli/tools.ts` keeps its five (they drive the whole booted session and keep their
`Session` signature as `CliTool<Session>`) and appends the contributed ones through one adapter
that binds each to `cliHost(session)`; a contributed name the shell already has is refused
there. That is E1, the one user-visible change: the command index is now the shell's five then
the packages' in product order (`launchpad-probe, lsdj-rom, n8-load, n8-bridge, n8-play,
risa-rom, n8-sync, bliptoaster-rom`). Every tool's `--help` and summary is byte-identical to the
old binary's: `test/cli/cli.test.ts` pins the whole index, and the recorded anchor was compared
tool by tool.

The seven tools moved with history: `lsdj-rom` to lsdj, `risa-rom` to risa, `bliptoaster-rom`
to bliptoaster, `n8-load` / `n8-play` / `n8-bridge` to n8, `n8-sync` to risa (n8 exports the
shared `runBridge` loop as `@retroplug/n8/bridge`, and n8 stays cart-free), and
`launchpad-probe` to launchpad. Each reaches the shell only through the CLI host -
`host.files`, `host.png`, `host.kits.compile`, `host.devices.rpc` / `.midi()`,
`host.process` and `host.songs.list` - so no tool imports `Session`, `makeCall`,
`createMidiClient` or `keepAlive` any more. `n8-load`'s battery listing prints
`host.songs.list`, byte-identical to the recorded oracle. `encodeWav` and the rest of the pure
WAV codec moved to `@retroplug/dsp/wav` (the streaming writer stays in the shell's render
library, and `cli/wav.ts` re-exports both), and the NES DMC kit-spec types moved to
`@retroplug/tracker/nes/kitSpec` as `NesDmcSampleSpec` / `NesDmcKitSpec` (risa keeps its old
names as aliases), so `bliptoaster-rom` compiles through `host.kits.compile("risa", spec)` with
no dependency on risa.

The example sessions moved to `examples/` in the package they are about (mgb: mgb-smoke,
analyze-mgb, export-mgb-channels; mesen: export-nes-channels, export-nes-mono; lsdj:
analyze-lsdj-sync) and import the SDK by the bare `retroplug-cli` specifier, which the binary
serves from its loaded-module table - confirmed first, as E4 asked: `retroplug-cli
build/cli/mgb-smoke.js` builds a screenshot. Each manifest lists them in `retroplug.examples`
and declares `retroplug.host: ["retroplug-cli"]`; `cmake/packages.cmake`'s `retroplug_examples()`
reads the manifests, the `retroplug-example-session` target builds each to the same
build/cli/<name>.js (the shell's render-rom/render-song/rom-test stay), and `tools/build-session.js`
marks `retroplug-cli` external. The SDK gained the four exports the sessions need: `runSession`
(documenting that it is for a session by path, never a test), `DirectGraph`,
`interleaveStereoStreams` and `deinterleaveStereo`, in `cli/sdk.ts`, `cli/sdk-types.d.ts` and the
drift check. The four native tool tests stay in test-native with their imports repointed and
`cliHost(session)` passed to `run`; `n8Play`'s pure cases moved to `n8/ts/test`.

The host-module list. `packages/retroplug/host-modules.json` names every host module (its
surface, provider and declaration file) and the generator writes the typecheck `paths` into
`tsconfig.host-modules.json`, which the shell's and every examples package's tsconfig extend; the
shell restates its own host path because a tsconfig's `paths` replaces rather than merges (the UI
alias rides with it). Rule 3 grows to `ts/` plus `examples/`, and its `surface` is ENFORCED: a bare
specifier on the list is admitted when the importing package declares it in `retroplug.host` AND the
file is one that surface owns (a package's `examples/` or `ts/cli/` for the CLI's, `ts/ui/` for the
UI's), one it does not declare is refused, one imported from an app, protocol, console or test file
is refused naming the surface the module belongs to, a declaration the list lacks is refused, and an
unused declaration warns. Each case has a fixture, and the rule is RED against them before it
passes. `@retroplug/dsp/wav` joins the shell's rule-9 contract list for the render library's
import.

Proof. `pnpm test`, `test:native` (the four tool suites and `launchpad-devices`),
`test:cli-ts`, `test:ui`, `typecheck`, `check:boundaries` and `check:docs` pass; each example
builds and runs (the two Reaper analyzes' example-session halves run here, their Reaper staging
halves do not); the old binary's help anchor matches. No golden, parity, kit, render, image or
pack-byte moved.
EOF
````

### Task 6: rule 9 and the scanner over `cli/`, the bundle split, and the docs

Design sections 7.1 to 7.5, 8's sixth stage and 10. The two checks grow their second root: rule 9 walks `src` and
`cli` with per-root semantics (a `src` file reaches only `src`, a `cli` file reaches `cli/` or `src/`, never `ui/` or
another package relatively; each root's `generated/` is unjudged), and the literal scanner takes `--dirs src,cli` plus
`--carts`, so a cart id or a ROM extension a tool's help text spells is refused. The bundle check lands with both sides:
the six non-UI bundles (the control plane, the render worker, the SDK, the CLI dispatcher, the planner and the script
nodes) carry no `@retroplug/ui`, no package's own `ts/ui/` and no `ui/generated/`, and the UI bundle carries no
package's `ts/cli/`, no `cli/generated/` and no `core/ts/cliTool.ts`.

The docs pass is this task's too, `spec/07-remaining-work.md` records what F4b leaves for F4c, and the design lands
here: section 11 records the prototype and sections 1 to 10 are corrected in place to what the build found (they are
the header's departure list, and this task's last diff). Each check is shown
RED first on the tree that precedes the change that satisfies it, and the last pass's two widenings (the script-node
bundle and the `ts/ui/` and `ts/cli/` sides) carry their own REDs.

- [ ] **Step 3: The bundle check, both sides, and the script nodes**

`tools/build-ui.js` exports `uiBuildOptions` and an in-memory `bundleInputs(entry, outfile?)` (`write: false`, the
metafile in hand), with the script body behind `require.main === module` so the CMake call is unchanged.
`test/script/bundle-split.mjs` bundles the control plane, the render worker, the SDK, the dispatcher, the planner and
the script nodes through `build-session.js` and the UI through `build-ui.js`; `bundle-ui-split.test.ts` holds both
sides, and the dispatcher's case proves it still carries its own generated table while the planner carries its
protocol data.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-split.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The driver behind test/script/bundle-ui-split.test.ts: bundles each surface's entry the way the build does (through
// tools/build-session.js and tools/build-ui.js, in memory) and prints one JSON line - per bundle, the absolute paths of
// the modules that went in. The split is then a fact about the metafile rather than a claim about the imports: the
// control plane, the render worker, the script nodes, the SDK, the CLI dispatcher and the planner carry no UI code, and
// the UI bundle carries no CLI one.
//
// The build is Node's (esbuild is not a txiki module), so the test runs this in a node child, as
// bundle-protocol.test.ts does with its own driver.
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { resolve } from "node:path";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const { bundleInputs } = require("../../../../tools/build-session.js");
const { bundleInputs: uiBundleInputs } = require("../../../../tools/build-ui.js");

// The entries, and the format the build gives each: the render worker and the script nodes are iifes (a bare QuickJS
// runtime evals them). The script-node bundle is every Engine's, so it is a non-UI surface like the rest.
const BUNDLES = [
    ["control-plane", "src/pluginControlPlane.ts", "esm"],
    ["render-worker", "src/render/worker.ts", "iife"],
    ["script-nodes", "src/generated/scriptNodes.ts", "iife"],
    ["cli-sdk", "cli/sdk.ts", "esm"],
    ["cli-dispatcher", "cli/cli.ts", "esm"],
    ["planner", "src/graph/protocolNodes.ts", "esm"],
];

const out = {};
for (const [name, entry, format] of BUNDLES) {
    const built = bundleInputs(entry, format);
    out[name] = built.inputs.map((input) => resolve(process.cwd(), input));
}
// The UI bundle's own inputs are relative to the repository root (its absWorkingDir).
out.ui = uiBundleInputs(resolve(process.cwd(), "ui/main.tsx")).inputs;
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(out));
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-ui-split.test.ts`:

````ts
// The UI/non-UI bundle split (docs/modular-graph-phase-f4b-design.md section 7.4): until per-product bundles land,
// every product loads every package's registries, so this is the precondition that a non-UI surface carries no UI code
// and the UI carries no CLI code. Two generated modules make the split possible and would undo it silently:
// ui/generated/menus.ts (the packages' menu contributions) and cli/generated/tools.ts (their CLI tools), and beside
// them the packages' own `ts/ui/` and `ts/cli/` trees, reached through their `./ui` and `./cli` entries. The control
// plane, the render worker, the script nodes, the SDK, the CLI dispatcher and the planner must carry no `ui` module
// (the package, any package's `ts/ui/`, the menus); the UI must carry no CLI one (any package's `ts/cli/`, the tool
// contract, the tools). The dispatcher is the bundle that carries the tools, which is why it is named here.
//
// The bundles are built as the build builds them, in memory: tools/build-session.js's bundleInputs (esm/iife) and
// tools/build-ui.js's, and esbuild's metafile says which modules went in. The build is Node's, so test/script/
// bundle-split.mjs runs it in a child, as bundle-protocol.test.ts does.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn and a child's pipe, declared locally as bundle-protocol.test.ts declares them.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** Every bundle's input modules, as absolute paths. */
async function bundles(): Promise<Record<string, string[]>> {
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "test/script/bundle-split.mjs"], {
    stdout: "pipe",
    stderr: "pipe",
  });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`the bundle split could not be built: ${err || out}`);
  }
  return JSON.parse(out) as Record<string, string[]>;
}

/** The UI's own modules: the `ui` package, any package's UI module tree, and the shell's generated menu table. No
 *  non-UI surface may load one. */
const isUi = (path: string): boolean =>
  /\/packages\/ui\//.test(path) ||
  /\/packages\/[^/]+\/ts\/ui\//.test(path) ||
  /\/packages\/retroplug\/ui\/generated\//.test(path);
/** The CLI's own modules: the shell's generated tool table, any package's CLI module tree, and the tool contract every
 *  one of them implements. The UI may load none of them. */
const isCli = (path: string): boolean =>
  /\/packages\/retroplug\/cli\/generated\//.test(path) ||
  /\/packages\/[^/]+\/ts\/cli\//.test(path) ||
  /\/packages\/core\/ts\/cliTool\.ts$/.test(path);

const NON_UI = ["control-plane", "render-worker", "script-nodes", "cli-sdk", "cli-dispatcher", "planner"];

test("no non-UI bundle carries any package's UI module or the generated menu table", async () => {
  const built = await bundles();
  for (const name of NON_UI) {
    const ui = built[name]!.filter(isUi);
    console.log(`# ${name}: ${built[name]!.length} modules, ${ui.length} UI: ${ui.join(", ")}`);
    expect(ui, `${name} carries UI code`).toEqual([]);
  }
});

test("the UI bundle carries no package's CLI module, no tool contract and no tool table", async () => {
  // A package's own `./cli` entry is the sharp case: it carries the tool AND `@retroplug/core/cliTool`, and neither is
  // the generated table, so the table alone would not see it.
  const built = await bundles();
  const cli = built.ui!.filter(isCli);
  console.log(`# ui: ${built.ui!.length} modules, ${cli.length} CLI: ${cli.join(", ")}`);
  expect(cli).toEqual([]);
});

test("the CLI dispatcher carries the generated tool table, and the planner the generated protocol data", async () => {
  // The split is not "carry no generated module": each surface carries its own. A dispatcher that lost the tool table
  // would list no package command, and a planner without the protocol data would place none.
  const built = await bundles();
  expect(built["cli-dispatcher"]!.some(isCli)).toBe(true);
  expect(built.planner!.some((path) => /\/src\/generated\/protocol\.ts$/.test(path))).toBe(true);
});
````

````diff
+**The generated module's refusals** (`ui/generated/menus.ts`, at load, so a bad contribution fails the product's start
+and not a menu click): a row id used twice in a placement (a tracker's extras count as `instance.tracker:<id>`), a
+builder at a placement `PLACEMENTS` does not list, a row over a role kind no registered role type declares, a row whose
+`key` (or a `when.key`) its role's schema does not declare, a `TrackerUi.id` no registered tracker integration has or two
+packages both contribute, and a `UiService.id` declared twice; the shell's menu composers add `assertUniqueMenuIds` over
+every tree they build (a builder that emitted `inst-exit` is refused).

+`n8` and `launchpad` contribute `ts/ui/` modules, each published through one `./ui` export (a pack's UI contract is one
+module: the contribution plus the seam a test or another surface reaches it by; n8 dropped the two subpath exports it
+first had). `packages/n8/ts/ui/` holds `n8Devices.ts` and `n8SdOps.ts` (both git renames) and an `index.ts` with
+`n8MenuChildren`, `n8Detected`, the card-row label and the two builders; `packages/launchpad/ts/ui/` holds
+`launchpadDevices.ts` (a rename) and an `index.ts` with `launchpadMenuChildren`, `controllerAppRows`, the status, sync
+and scan labels, the port-name helpers, the two builders and the service. They read the shell through the host
+(`makeCall` became `host.devices.rpc`, `UserConfigStore` became `host.config`, `drivenCartSystem` became
+`host.systems.drivenCart()` through `projectCart(host)`, so the `"mesen"` literal is gone from the pack, `SystemView`
+became `SystemInfo`). `launchpadDevices.ts`'s `resolveClient` takes the caller's channel and has no global fallback
+(`test-native/launchpad-devices`, the one host-less caller, passes `makeCall()` once). The module-global state they keep
+(the card job, the probed link, the scan) is per bundle, as today. A menu's card rows act on the PROJECT's cart whichever
+instance's menu is showing, as `cartFor(ctx, null)` did, and the Load ROM dialog offers the shell's `ROM_PATTERNS`
+through `MenuBuildContext.romPatterns` (the pack names no list of its own; a test pins the dialog to it).
+
+The three watchers became `services`: the N8 card's versioned poll every 6 frames, the Launchpad scan's versioned poll
+with its finishing-edge apply and `pollControllerRole` every 3 frames, and `restoreLaunchpad` (the launchpad service's
+`start`), plus a `subscribe` for each native-host push. The version-and-edge latches move into each service's own
+closure and `poll.run` returns whether the version moved; **each `start` puts the latches back where a mount finds them**,
+because the refs they replaced were per mount, so a remount repaints once and takes an already finished scan's finishing
+edge once more (the applied-scan guard makes the re-applied edge a no-op for `config.json`). `ui/app/useUiServices.ts`
+is the one generic hook: it runs `start` in an effect, subscribes every `subscribe` through `useRerenderOn` (the list is
+a module constant, so the call is stable) and hands the frame counting to `ui/app/serviceTicker.ts`'s `tickServices`
+over one `useNativeEvent("frame")`, which `test/services.test.ts` pins with fake services (per-service divisors, one
+repaint answer per frame, a list whose length changed re-sizing its counters). `App.tsx` lost `useN8SdWatch`,
+`useLaunchpadScanWatch`, `restoreLaunchpad` and the two `subscribe*` imports. The packs' `resolveClient`, `resolveLink`
+and the scan clock read a test-injected global (`__rp_launchpadClient`, `__rp_launchpadClock`, `__rp_n8LinkClient`)
+before their module state, because the UI bundle holds its own copies of the modules a test could set; nothing in
+production sets one.
+
+The device-pack scan (`build-device-pack.mjs`'s whole-core scan) skips the modules a manifest names as `app`, `ui` and
+`cli`, plus the directory of one that is its directory's index, and refuses a core module that imports one of them or a
+module under such a directory, naming the importing file and the member.

 ### 5.4 The host-module list
 
 One shell-owned file, `packages/retroplug/host-modules.json`, lists each host module with the surface that provides it
 and why: `[{ "module": "retroplug-cli", "surface": "cli", "provider": "the retroplug-cli binary's loaded-module table",
 "types": "cli/sdk-types.d.ts" }]`; F4c adds `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `lvgljs-ui`, `lvgljs` with surface `ui`. Rule
-3 (`check-boundaries.mjs:596`, the third-party branch) accepts a bare specifier on the list when the importing package's
+3 (`check-boundaries.mjs`, the third-party branch) accepts a bare specifier on the list when the importing package's
 manifest declares it in `retroplug.host`, refuses one it does not declare, and refuses a declared name the list does not
-have; a declaration nothing imports warns, as an unused dependency does. The rule's import walk grows from `ts/` to
-`ts/` plus `examples/` (today it reads `pkg.ts` only). The generator writes
-`packages/retroplug/tsconfig.host-modules.json` (the `paths` entries; gitignored with the generated modules) and the
-shell's `tsconfig.json` and every package with `examples/` extend it, replacing the hand-written `"retroplug-cli"` entry
-(`tsconfig.json:12`) and adding `../*/examples` to the shell's `include`. `bundles.cmake` gains `ui/generated/menus.ts`
-and `cli/generated/tools.ts` in `retroplug-ts-packages`'s byproducts; `retroplug-cli-bundle`,
+have; a declaration nothing imports warns, as an unused dependency does. The rule's import walk grew from `ts/` to
+`ts/` plus `examples/`. **The `surface` field is enforced, not documentation**: `surfaceOf(pkg, file)` decides a file's
+surface from its own directory (`examples/**` and `ts/cli/**` are `cli`, `ts/ui/**` is `ui`, any other file belongs to
+no surface), `surfacesOf(entry)` reads the entry's `surface` as one name or a list, and a host module imported from a
+file that surface does not own is refused, naming the surface and its trees (a manifest member cannot decide it, since
+the app and protocol paths would have to be trusted, and a filename convention would let a rename open the hole), so
+`retroplug-cli` is reachable only from a package's `examples/` and `ts/cli/`, and F4c's four React modules from
+`ts/ui/` alone.
+
+**The typecheck `paths` come from the generator, in two files.** The generator writes `tsconfig.host-modules.json` (each
+module's `types`, relative to the shell) which every package with `examples/` extends, and `tsconfig.paths.json` (the
+same entries plus the shell's own aliases from the shell-owned `tsconfig.aliases.json`, now `{ "ui-harness": [...] }`)
+which the shell's `tsconfig.json` extends; both are gitignored with the generated modules. Two files because TypeScript
+REPLACES a child's `paths` with the extending config's rather than merging them, so the shell cannot extend the
+package-facing file and add its alias beside it (the design's single file with the shell's hand-written entry removed
+did not survive that). A package with `retroplug.examples` must have a `tsconfig.json` whose parsed `extends` (one or a
+list, resolved against the package) names the generated host-modules file; a missing or unextended one is refused by
+the generator. The root `typecheck` script is `node packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs && pnpm -r typecheck`,
+so the generator has written every generated file before any package's `tsc` runs: a fresh checkout, which has none of
+them, typechecks in CI's order (install, typecheck, build). `bundles.cmake` lists `ui/generated/menus.ts`,
+`cli/generated/tools.ts`, `tsconfig.host-modules.json` and `tsconfig.paths.json` in `retroplug-ts-packages`'s
+byproducts (and `host-modules.json` and `tsconfig.aliases.json` among its sources); `retroplug-cli-bundle`,
 `retroplug-example-session` and the UI bundle already depend on that target.

 ### 7.1 Rule 9 over `cli/`

-`SHELL_IMPORTS`, a relative import must stay in the file's own root or reach `src` from `cli` (a file in `src` reaches
-only `src`, a file in `cli` reaches `cli` or `src`; today's rule is "outside `src`", and a plain union would let `src`
-import `cli`), `cli/generated/` is unjudged (like `src/generated/`), and a stale entry still fails. The list gains
-`@retroplug/core/host`, `@retroplug/core/cliTool`, `@retroplug/core/capability`, `@retroplug/dsp/wav` and
-**`@retroplug/testing`** (the SDK re-exports `test`, `expect`, `skip` and `rom-test.ts` imports them; the brief's list
-omits it), derived from the tree at stage 6 (about 29 entries). **RED first, on `b96fb1bb9`'s `cli/`:** 25 refusals in
-10 files against today's 24-entry list (23 in 8 once `@retroplug/testing` is added); the rule is committed before any
-tool moves, and the fixtures in `test/boundaries` get a `shell-cli-forbidden`, `shell-cli-allowed` and
-`shell-cli-relative` case (a `src` file reaching `cli/` is refused).

+`packages/retroplug/src` reaches only `src/`, a file in `packages/retroplug/cli` reaches `cli/` or `src/` (never `ui/`,
+`test/`, `test-native/`, `tools-src/` or another package relatively; a plain union would let `src` import `cli`), each
+root's `generated/` is unjudged, every `@retroplug/*` specifier in either must be on `SHELL_IMPORTS`, and a stale entry
+fails (the message names both roots). The list is **one list on purpose** (the two roots are one program's halves; the
+comment says so and why no `roots` field), 29 entries, gaining `@retroplug/core/host` and `@retroplug/core/capability`
+(stage 1: every `src` file that names the contract needed them), `@retroplug/core/path` (stage 3), `@retroplug/dsp/wav`
+(stage 5), and `@retroplug/core/cliTool` and **`@retroplug/testing`** (stage 6: the SDK serves the harness and

+7. **Services**: `test/services.test.ts` (mock tier; a service is plain data: divisors through `tickServices`, the

+8. **Battery listing** (`test/hosts/battery-listing.test.ts`): the three strings recorded by running `8a74339b9`'s

+9. **The device-pack scan** (`graph/device-pack`): the `ui` and `cli` control-plane rule, the directory rule and a core
+   importing a package's `cli` module, each refused.
+10. **The oracles that caught defects**: BlipToaster's staged SysEx in a two-NES project, the per-row ROM read count (a
+    counting reader), `inst-link`'s typeof read (`hand-link`), menu id uniqueness.

+## 11. As built (the prototype)
+
+The prototype is six commits on the design commit `8a74339b9`, one per stage, each built by DeepSeek Flash and reviewed
+by Opus, with each review's fix pass folded into the commit it belongs to by fixup and autosquash (the last pass into
+stages 1 to 6 at once, and one pass rebuilt the history of stages 2 to 4: below), so the six trees stand as final and a
+stage report's sha is older than the branch's. **The shas in this section are the branch's now** (`feature/modularize` at
+`4350d9148`; they will be on `proto/f4b-surfaces` once the controller branches it). The whole prototype is 302 files,
++63,151 -3,060 over the design commit, 54,613 lines of it the menu matrix's recorded JSON. Sections 1 to 10 above were
+corrected in place to what the build found; this section is the record of how, and the plan is written against it. Nothing
+was pushed.
+
+**The stages**, by commit subject and current sha (files changed, lines added and removed):
+
+1. `bce662f7e feat(f4b): the host contract, and the three surfaces' hosts` (52, +1188 -443): `core/ts/host.ts` and
+   `capability.ts`, the three builders over `src/hostGroups.ts`, the three slices and `songImportHost.ts` deleted, every
+   hook retyped, `TrackerIntegration.batteryListing` and `src/batteryListing.ts`, the host typing tests.
+2. `9539d0fe2 feat(f4b): the ui package and the declarative menu rows` (67, +56781 -291): `packages/ui`, the menu model
+   moved, the contribution types, `retroplug.ui` and `ui/generated/menus.ts`, the role-row renderer, the SameBoy, Mesen

+4. `8e9c64128 feat(f4b): the device menus contribute themselves, and their services` (62, +1612 -625): the N8 and

+
+**What each review found, and what the fix pass changed.**
+
+1. *Stage 1 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: `ProcessHost.args` was documented as the vector after the tool's name
+   and built as `hostArgs()`, which includes it; `controller.set` laundered an open string into the shell's closed enum
+   with a cast; and `songs.list` was a stopgap in `cli/batteryListing.ts` that made `ui/` import `cli/` (and the carts)
+   and reached `n8-load` with no recorded test. Ten minors. Fix pass: `cliHost(session, args)` returns the tool's own
+   vector (pinned), `controller.set` checks `CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES` and throws, and design 5.2 came forward: the
+   `batteryListing` hook on risa and LSDj, one composer in `src/`, the three strings recorded from `8a74339b9` first
+   (the controller's decision); the shell typing test was shown RED by moving the builders aside.
+2. *Stage 2 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: the recorded rows pinned labels, not values or fallbacks; the matrix
+   missed `inst-link`, the `lp-app-*` rows and the `disabled` flags; the Link Group reader had been rewritten (`Number()`
+   for the old `typeof` rule); `UiHost` was defined twice; and the generated module's checks missed a mistyped key, an
+   unknown tracker id and placement drift. Eight minors. Fix pass: the whole matrix re-recorded from a scratch tree of
+   `8a74339b9` (23 cases, with stored values and hand-edited configs; the Link Group RED shown with a `hand-link` case),
+   one `UiHost`, the generator's added refusals (RED first), `PLACEMENTS` as data.
+3. *Stage 3 (with fixes).* Critical: BlipToaster's settings SysEx was staged at `drivenCart()` without the old
+   `cart.system.id === sys.id` check, so in a two-NES project it reached the other NES's console (RED shown, fixed).
+   Important: the selectable slot read the ROM from disk per row (RED with a counting reader: 34 reads for 17 rows x 2
+   builds); the matrix missed `settings.midi`, Audio and Exit (the mock was not standalone), a scan in flight, an
+   unreadable ROM, the actionCycler verbs, the staged MIDI and the trackers' states; and the stage 2 and 3 commit messages
+   misdescribed their trees. Controller decision: the controller-app rows keep the old display byte for byte and the
+   latent bug is owed (the first fix attempt had presented the changed reading as a named edge). Fix pass: the matrix
+   extended (33 cases and 66 equality cases then; 34 and 102 at the end), `AssetMenuSpec.selectedSlot` taking the build
+   context, `legacyConfigIndex`, the two messages reworded.
+4. *Stage 4 (with fixes).* **Critical: the fix-pass rebase put stage 3's `menuDefs.ts` changes into stage 2** (a
+   conflict at the replay was resolved by taking the post-stage-3 file), so the stage 2 commit did not build, which no
+   review had run a per-commit tree to find. Important: the N8 Load ROM dialog had been narrowed to `*.nes` without a
+   record; `launchpadDevices` kept a `hostCall()` global fallback; the service tests never ran against the old hooks and
+   `useUiServices` had none; the device-pack scan refused only `app` imports; and the service latches survived a remount
+   where the refs they replaced did not. Controller decisions: keep the dialog and the remount behaviour identical,
+   delete the fallback, test `useUiServices` green on the old hooks first, revert a docs edit that was not path-only.
+   Fix pass: **the history rebuilt** (stage 2's `menuDefs.ts` change is 46+/204-, stage 3's 143+/726-, each from the
+   pre-rebase refs by plumbing and verified file by file), **and the per-stage tree rule it led to: every stage's tree is
+   built and tested alone**, not only the tip's; `MenuBuildContext.romPatterns` with a dialog record in the matrix,
+   `hostCall()` deleted, `test-ui/ui-services.test.ts` (3 of 3 green against the old hooks restored in `App.tsx`, then
+   against the new tree) and `serviceTicker.ts`, per-mount latch resets, the scan's `ui` / `cli` import refusal.
+5. *Stage 5 (with fixes).* Critical: the stage 3 tree did not typecheck (a stage 4 test hunk had landed in stage 3, and
+   the tree had been extracted before the commits were sealed), and a fresh checkout's `pnpm typecheck` failed because
+   packages extended the gitignored `tsconfig.host-modules.json` before the generator wrote it (CI's order). Important: no
+   committed help-text oracle; the tool-name clash refusal untested; the SDK drift check not extended; the shell's
+   tsconfig restating the `retroplug-cli` path; manifests reformatted by a serializer (ten, not the eight first counted);
+   the `examples/` walk untested, with one RED claim in the report that was wrong. Seventeen minors. **The rule was
+   tightened: each tested tree must equal its sealed commit** (extract after the last rewrite, compare every file's
+   `git hash-object` with `git ls-tree`). Fix pass: the hunk moved to stage 4, the root `typecheck` script runs the
+   generator first (proved on a fresh `git archive`), `recorded-help.json` and `recorded-index.json`, `composeTools`, the
+   drift check's new shapes (which found real `ConstructSpec` drift), the two generated `paths` files, the manifests
+   hand-formatted again, an `examples/` fixture.
+6. *Stage 6 and the whole prototype (with fixes, no Critical).* All six stage trees typecheck from fresh archives (12
+   runs), the REDs reproduce, and the help texts match the old binary byte for byte. Important: n8's manifest was still
+   machine-formatted (restoring it also found a stale `cli` member in stage 4 that left a duplicate JSON key at stages 5
+   and 6, which last-wins had hidden from every test);
+   the bundle check's UI side let a package's own CLI module through and omitted the script-node bundle;
+   `sdkSurfaceCheck.ts` read `CONSOLES[0]` (sameboy) and spelled a Mesen knob on the Game Boy; the docs pass left
+   `spec/04`, a `spec/06` path and stale comments; and `host-modules.json`'s `surface` was unenforced (controller
+   decision: enforce it now in rule 3). Fifteen minors. Fix pass (into all six commits): n8's manifest, both bundle-check
+   sides with their REDs, `REAL_CARTS`, the docs sweep, `surfaceOf` in rule 3 (RED first), the ratchet's documentation,
+   `composeTools`' message, the examples-`extends` check parsed rather than searched, and the six trees re-extracted and
+   proven equal to their commits (the first run of the proof script was invalid, hashing through the worktree and
+   leaving `deps/dpf.js` empty, and is reported rather than hidden).
+
+**Departures from the design as committed (`8a74339b9`), and why.**
+
+- **`png` joins the song import hook** (`Host<"files" | "png" | "systems">`): `lsdjSongImport` reaches
+  `applyOverridesToRom`, whose font branch decodes a PNG.
+- **`createUiHost(stores, peers)`**, not `(stores, views)`: `beginImport` is App's React state. `devices.rpc` is a plain
+  function resolving on first use in both hosts (`makeCall` throws with no native channel). `ProcessHost.args()` is the
+  tool's own vector. `controller.set` throws on an unknown target. `SystemInfo.roles` is `readonly`.
+- **Core holds a narrow structural `ControllerSettings`** (`target: string`), and `ControllerAppField` is a union held
+  equal to `ConfigRow` by a two-way assignability case: core cannot import launchpad or `ui`.
+- **The capability types are `@retroplug/core/capability`**, their own module (the design said `src/capability.ts`
+  re-exports them from core and named `@retroplug/core/capability` only in rule 9's allowlist).
+- **`batteryListing` came forward into stage 1**, with its recorded oracle, so `ui/` never imported `cli/`; the design
+  had it in stage 5.
+- **`TrackerUi.asset` is optional**; `MenuBuildContext` gained `romPatterns` (the N8 Load ROM dialog, identical to
+  the old one); `AssetMenuSpec.selectedSlot` and `selectSlot` take the build context; `MenuContext.host` is optional with
+  a `hostOf(ctx)` fallback for the menu tests; the generated module's refusals are broader (7.5 item 4); `PLACEMENTS` is
+  data; `UiHost` is declared in the package.
+- **The controller-app rows keep their old display** (`legacyConfigIndex`), not the typed reading the design gave all
+  rows; the display bug is owed (section 10). A controller decision.
+- **Services**: `start` runs once per mount and each `start` resets the latches (the old refs were per mount); the
+  service test is `test/services.test.ts` (mock tier) plus `test-ui/ui-services.test.ts`, with test-injected globals
+  (`__rp_launchpadClient`, `__rp_launchpadClock`, `__rp_n8LinkClient`) because the UI bundle holds its own module
+  copies; frame counting is `serviceTicker.ts`'s `tickServices`. `createSubscribable` moved to `@retroplug/ui/menu` in
+  stage 4 (the design had it in F4c's kit).
+- **The device packs publish one `./ui` export** (n8 dropped two subpath exports); `launchpadDevices.ts`'s `hostCall()`
+  global fallback was deleted; the shell's `SystemView` gained `embeddedRom` for the title's short label.
+- **The device-pack scan skips `ui` and `cli` modules** and refuses a core module that imports one, or a module under
+  such a directory: the design did not foresee the Launchpad scenario reaching the host through its menu half.
+- **The Link Group builder reads a number or Off** (`typeof`), the old rule, not `Number()`; **BlipToaster pins at its own
+  system's cart only**, the old `cartFor` rule.
+- **`src/pathUtil.ts` and `src/savPaths.ts` stay as re-export shims** over `@retroplug/core/path` (so no rename), and
+  tracker keeps its own three-line `pick()`: `ui` depends on `tracker`.
+- **Tools are `ts/cli/` modules** behind a `ts/cli/index.ts`; `n8` exports `./cli`, `./bridge` and `./ui`; `CliHost` is
+  the one host name; `composeTools` is an exported function so the clash refusal is tested; the shell's three example
+  names are known to CMake and refused there if reused.
+- **The SDK drift check was extended** (the four additions' shapes) and found real drift in `sdk-types.d.ts`'s
+  `ConstructSpec`; `sdkSurfaceCheck.ts` reads the console a REAL cart drives, not `CONSOLES[0]`.
+- **Help and summaries are recorded from the old binary** before stage 5 (13 tools), not from `b96fb1bb9`'s source;
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

### Task 7: the acceptance run, and what is owed

This task commits nothing (unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit of its own, named for what it fixes). It is the
phase's acceptance: the tree and a full build, the SERIAL kit's 43 legs, the three oracle families under their require
flags, both device images and the pack's bytes, the SDL legs, the Reaper parameter runs and the whole Reaper suite, a
fresh clone that typechecks before it builds, the boundary and docs checks, both consumer suites, the example sessions,
`test:cli-ts`, `graph/device-pack` at two of the tasks' commits in real worktrees, and the bundle module diff base
against tip. Its figures are compared with the baseline recorded at `8a74339b9` (`/tmp/f4bpro/base-summary.txt` and
`base-*.log`) and with the final verification at the prototype's tip (`/tmp/f4bpro/s6fv-summary.txt` and `s6fv-*.log`).
**There is no hardware leg: no step may touch the NES, the N8, the Pico box, the probe, the Zoom L6 or any MIDI
interface, and the hardware safety rules in this plan's header govern every step here too.**

The baseline and the final run were both the parallel kit's, 47 summary lines each, every leg exit 0, with `pnpm
sdl:controller` run alone:
